foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.31. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ETH/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 60.14% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.87 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.87-0.88). Mid 1 - 0.601/0.87 = 0.31. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.87 = 0.17. High: s 0.88 = 0.32. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 87% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large subsistence agriculture, recurring food aid needs; small marketable surplus. Not from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 67,876,104 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 11.059% / 5 = 1,501,322. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

artillery.note: Educated guess. Gafat Armament Engineering Complex and Bishoftu Automotive overhaul and assemble guns, MRLs and armoured vehicles. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Ethiopian_Army)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Bishoftu Automotive licence assembly. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Ethiopian_Army)

roadKm.note: World Bank IS.ROD.TOTL.KM 44,359 km (2007; federal/regional engineered roads) as mid. High is the road list total 120,171 km (2018, incl. rural roads; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_road_network_size). Low allows for unusable sections; paved length unknown (~16,000 km asphalt).

railKm.note: asOf 2018: 754 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 659 km (2017) spans the range. Addis Ababa-Djibouti standard-gauge electric line is the only railway.

majorPorts.note: Landlocked; trade goes through Djibouti (about 90%), Berbera and Lamu.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 12 ships (10 general cargo, 2 tankers) under Ethiopian Shipping and Logistics Services, 2023; tonnage not in the merchant list. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/et.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck sustainment over long mountain roads; demonstrated deep advances in 2021-22.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Ethiopia has Africa's largest equine herd (donkeys, mules, horses); pack animals used in highland operations. Not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: mountainous highland plateau, harsh terrain and climate for invaders, strategic depth and strong national defence tradition (Adwa 1896).

ethiopia-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Thin and contradictory data: IISS 2026 (as quoted) puts active strength at 503,000 versus 150-300,000 (CIA) and 138,000 (World Bank 2020); equipment lists on Wikipedia mix cumulative deliveries with holdings and are grade C. Internal conflicts ongoing (Fano in Amhara, OLA in Oromia; Pretoria agreement with TPLF 2022 fragile) and tension with Eritrea over sea access. Population convention: everything inside ne:ETH. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-15%). No sea-going navy. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Regional police special forces excluded.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1.4 million km2 for 1000 (low) and 0.63 million for 1100. The world_1000 polygon measures 1.82 million km2 (mid). Taagepera (1997) and Turchin et al. (2006) give 4.1 million km2 for 969, counting Saharan and Hejaz claims (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires, high).

population.note: Seshat codes 13-14 million for 1000 (high) and 3.5-4.5 million for the reduced realm of 1100. HYDE via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population) for 1000: Egypt 5.0M, Syria 1.07M, Lebanon 0.44M, Israel 0.33M, Tunisia 1.0M, Libya 0.5M, about 8.3M before parts of Algeria (2.0M for the whole country), Jordan and the Hejaz; low 9M follows HYDE, mid 11M lies between the two.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Cairo-Fustat, the largest settlement, 120,000 (Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/221), with Alexandria, Damascus, Tinnis and Kairouan.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Battle accounts of the period usually give figures "around the 10,000 mark" for field armies; the Qaysariyya cavalry numbered about 1,000 in 996 (Lev 1987 p. 344); al-Aziz kept 12,000 horses and 36,000 camels (Lev 1987 p. 354), all via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army. Chronicle figures of 100,000-200,000 for Jawhar's 969 army and 300,000 men in Egypt in 993 (Beshir 1978) are called dubious there, and Nasir Khusraw's 215,000 dates from 1047. Total = the Egyptian regiments plus Syrian and Palestinian garrisons, guessed from these anchors.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Bedouin auxiliaries, Zirid Berber forces in Ifriqiya and Syrian town militias.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Fleet crews (~20 galleys at ~150 each), arsenal workers at al-Maqs, engineers and naphtha troops.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. A salaried army of ethnic regiments and slave soldiers, as in the Abbasid snapshot; the general population was not a military reservoir.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Linen and tiraz textiles of Tinnis and Damietta, glass, sugar, paper.

Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Old Roman roads in Syria-Palestine, the Sinai coast road, Nile towpaths and caravan routes in the Maghreb.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Alexandria, Damietta, Tinnis, Ascalon, Acre, Tyre, Tripoli, Mahdia.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Mediterranean and Red Sea trade; Amalfitan traders kept a colony in Cairo (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_navy).

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Sinai desert before the Delta, walled cities and local supply; Syria was contested ground with little population support.

fatimid-caliphate-996.notes: Snapshot = 996, the death of al-Aziz and the accession of al-Hakim; Seshat names 996 as a peak year. Army size is the weakest number: no muster survives, battle accounts give ~10,000 per field army and the chronicle totals (100,000-300,000) are rejected by the modern literature summarised on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_army. The fleet figure is unusually well documented for the year because of the 996 arsenal fire. Population convention: everything inside the world_1000 polygon (Egypt, southern Syria and Palestine, Libya, Zirid-governed Ifriqiya and the Hejaz); Kalbid Sicily, a vassal, is not counted.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.96. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/FIN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 3.49% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.84 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.74-0.93). Mid 1 - 0.035/0.84 = 0.96. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.74 = 0.93. High: s 0.93 = 0.96. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 84% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Roughly self-sufficient in cereals and dairy; mandatory strategic stockpiles.

france-1415.notes: Snapshot = October 1415, the Agincourt campaign. Agincourt numbers are disputed: Curry's record-based 12,000 French vs 9,000 English, against Rogers, Mortimer and Sumption's ~14,000-15,000 French (plus up to 10,000 valets) vs ~6,000 English (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt). The 1415 royal army was largely paid men-at-arms in companies and counts as activePersonnel at the date; the unsummoned arriere-ban is trainedReserves. Population convention: the kingdom per Seshat, including Burgundian and Breton fiefs held under the crown; English Gascony and Calais excluded. Same nationId as later france snapshots.

population.note: HYDE via OWID: France (modern borders) 21,992,348 (1700). Lynn (Giant of the Grand Siecle ch. 1) works with ~20-21.5M for the kingdom c. 1700 after the famine of 1693-94 (1.3M deaths, Nine Years War article). Mid 21.5M.

france-1870.notes: Snapshot = French Empire at the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War (declared 19 July 1870), forces as mobilisation was under way. Population and territory = metropolitan France incl. Savoy and Nice; Algeria and colonies excluded; includes is empty. Personnel: regular army with reservists who had joined and the navy = active; Garde Mobile and reservists not yet joined = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Franco-Prussian War page (Howard 1991 p. 39; Clodfelter 2017 p. 184; Wawro). Branch split is a reconstruction (grade C).

areaKm2.note: world_1914 France polygon = ~530,000 km2 computed on the sphere; published metropolitan area 536,464 km2 (B&H Table 1: 0.5M km2).

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 1: France 1913 = 39.8M (League of Nations 1927); B&H Table 9 (Urlanis) 39.6M; OWID/HYDE 1914 = 39.58M (low). COW tpop 1914 = 33.2M reflects the occupied departments and is not used. Metropolitan France only; colonies (48.3M) excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share France 1910 = 47.5%. 1911 census: 44% urban (communes of 2,000+ agglomerated). Low ~38% in towns of 5,000+.

activePersonnel.note: Cited page: mobilisation ordered 1 Aug 1914 called the classes of 1896-1910, almost three million reservists, on top of the ~0.8M serving conscripts (three-year law); Mid = ~0.8M + ~3M from the cited page, rounded down for exemptions; bounds are a judgement band. Field armies of the north-east ~1.65M in 62 infantry divisions (British Army page). Navy ~60,000 included. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 789k, 1915 = 4,997k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Older territorial reserve classes (ages 42-48, Reserve of the Territorial Army) not yet called in August, plus colonial reservists. France trained ~85% of each class, so almost every adult man had service. Reconstruction, grade C.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. Artillery (87 regiments, 40% of the army by 1918), engineers, trains, depots of 201 reserve and 145 territorial regiments in training, staffs, navy.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total mobilised: 7,935,000 (French reply to the ILO, 1924) or 8,410,000 (US War Dept) on the cited page, incl. ~0.5-0.9M colonial troops; metropolitan ~7.9M / 39.7M = 0.20.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. ~850,000 births per year in the 1890s, half male, ~75% survival to 20 gives ~320,000; the stagnant population was the motive for the 1913 three-year law.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. French aircraft output recalled as ~4,500 (1915), ~7,500 (1916), ~14,900 (1917), ~24,600 (1918) from Morrow, The Great War in the Air (not fetched); fighter share (Nieuport, SPAD) a split by judgement.

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1918; 75 mm output reached several hundred per month by 1916.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Bretagne class completed 1915-16; capital-ship building stopped in 1914.

Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Low = 1938 peacetime share: COW milex 1938 = 919,284 (thousand current US$, https://correlatesofwar.org/wp-content/uploads/NMCv7.zip) against national income of roughly US$10-12bn = ~8%. High: COW milex 1940 = 5,707,762 against the same income = ~50% (first half of 1940 at full mobilisation). Mid ~30% for September 1939 to May 1940 with 4.3M mobilised, between the UK shares of 15% (1939) and 44% (1940) in Harrison 1998 Table 1-8 (https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf). audit 2026-10-30: was 0.06/0.08/0.12 (1938 peacetime share as mid); war-date snapshot takes a wartime estimate as mid, grade D until a source is fetched.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, France agriculture share of employment 1931 = 35.6%, 1936 = 35.6%, 1946 = 36.0%. Mid 1 - 0.356 = 0.64; range a 0.33-0.38. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.15/0.25/0.35 (educated guess about self-sufficiency); recomputed with the formula.

france-1989.notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-1990, data as at 1 June 1989), the last pre-1990 year of the Cold War force. France was a NATO member outside the integrated military command (since 1966); its 1st Army (3 corps) and Rapid Action Force (FAR, 47,000) were national, with agreed contingency plans for engagement alongside CENTAG. Population convention: metropolitan France (OWID 56.7M); overseas departments and territories (DOM-TOM, ~1.3M) excluded and their garrisons listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = armed forces 466,300 excl. Gendarmerie 87,200 (paramilitary); earmarked reserves 353,000 = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles are a reconstruction from regiment counts (French regiments are battalion size); everything else supportPersonnel. Abroad (MB 1989-90): FRG 52,700 (3 armd div with 570 MBT), Berlin 2,700, Djibouti 3,650, Antilles-Guyana 8,200, Indian Ocean 3,300, New Caledonia 9,500, Polynesia 5,400, Chad 1,700, Senegal 1,150, CAR 1,200, Cote d'Ivoire 920, Gabon 550, UNIFIL 530. The MB edition was read from a full-text transcription at samlib.ru (cited URL). Weakest values: merchant tonnage, wartime production and the infantry split (reconstructions/educated guesses).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.35 -> 0.98. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/FRA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 2.33% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.31 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.30-1.33). Mid 1 - 0.023/1.31 = 0.98. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.30 = 0.97. High: s 1.33 = 0.98. Net exporter: production is about 131% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large net exporter of cereals, dairy and wine; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

france-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with the Ministry of the Armed Forces Key Figures 2026 (equipment at end 2025) as the primary order-of-battle source (grade A). foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.26. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/GEO/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 33.95% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.46 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.43-0.50). Mid 1 - 0.340/0.46 = 0.26. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.43 = 0.06. High: s 0.50 = 0.32. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 46% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports most wheat; exports wine, hazelnuts. Not from FAO balance sheets.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Herwig 1997 ch. 2: after mobilisation (2-18 Aug 1914) the army stood at ~3.82M (peace strength ~761,000 plus reservists), the Feldheer in 7 western and 1 eastern army; plus the navy (~80,000 peace, mobilised higher). The British Army page cites 1.85M and 87 infantry divisions for the field armies alone (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army_during_World_War_I), the low bound of the deployable force. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 862k, 1915 = 3,823k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Trained men not called up in August: older Landwehr II and Landsturm I classes and partly trained Ersatz reservists. Prewar Germany trained only ~half of each class (Strachan, To Arms ch. 3), so the residual trained pool was smaller than the 5M+ of France proportionally.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance (1914). Evidence: Feldflieger-Abteilungen and Zeppelins; aerial reports decisive at Tannenberg

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914 aircraft. Evidence: Taube, Albatros B.I, Aviatik; ~230 aircraft

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Germany 1913 = 5,815, 1914 = 4,876 (2011 int$). The August snapshot sits between the prewar level and the wartime 1914 average; mid 5,600. B&H Table 2 gives 3,648 in 1990 int$ for the 1913 Reich.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Mid read from Broadberry and Harrison Table 5; low recalled from Ferguson, not read from a fetched source. Low: peacetime defence spending ~3.5% of NNP in 1913 (Ferguson, Pity of War table 6, isbn 0-7139-9246-8). Mid: B&H Table 5 government spending 23.9% of GDP in 1914 (9.8% in 1913) less civil spending, so ~20% military. High: 43.8% government share in 1915.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Industry, mining and crafts ~40-45% of NNP in 1913 (Hoffmann series as summarised by Ritschl in Broadberry and Harrison 2005, ch. 2).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: cited page, table "Erwerbstaetige und Angehoerige in % der Gesamtbevoelkerung" (Hohorst, Kocka and Ritter 1978 p. 66): agriculture 28.4% in 1907, falling ~0.5 points a year since 1882, so ~0.26 in 1913. s: "by 1914 19 per cent of its total calories were imported" (https://www.habselstree.org.uk/boys/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/06/OP65StJohnFoodSupplyandWorldWarOne.pdf, after Offer), s = 0.81. Mid 1 - 0.26/0.81 = 0.68. Low a 0.284, s 0.80 = 0.645; high a 0.24, s 0.82 = 0.71. Grade C: two sources combined. Import dependence: 19% of calories, 27% of protein, 42% of fats. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.6/0.65/0.68 with an assumed a = 0.35 and s = 1; fetched a and s applied.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Men reaching 20 per year: ~1.9M births per year in the 1890s, half male, ~65% survival to 20 gives ~0.6M; only ~half were trained before 1913 (Strachan ch. 3).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Single-seat fighters per year 1915-1917, a share of total German aircraft output recalled as ~4,500 (1915), ~8,200 (1916), ~19,700 (1917) from Morrow, The Great War in the Air (not fetched); fighter share is a split by judgement.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Two-seat reconnaissance, ground-attack and bomber aircraft per year 1915-1917, the remainder of the totals recalled from Morrow (see fighters).

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1918; the 1916 Hindenburg Programme aimed at ~3,000 guns per month.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Capital ships, cruisers and destroyers completed per year. Capital ships and cruisers 1914-1916 = 3/5/8: 3 Koenig class and Derfflinger in late 1914, 2 Bayern and Luetzow 1916, ~6 light cruisers per year; torpedo boats (destroyers) 1915-1918 = 30/45/60 (Conway's 1906-1921). Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. U-boats commissioned per year: ~52 (1915), 108 (1916), ~87 (1917) (Conway's 1906-1921; Halpern).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Chausseen (metalled highways) and lesser engineered roads of the Reich.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Germany: 1913 = 63,537 km, 1914 = 64,077 km.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Hamburg, Bremen/Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven, Kiel, Danzig, Stettin, Koenigsberg, Luebeck, Emden.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914 (steam and sail vessels of 100 tons gross and over owned, Register Book 1913-14): Germany 5,082,061 GRT, of which steam 4,743,046. High = published 1914 total of ~5.46M GRT. Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Recalled from van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-21730-X), not read from a fetched source. van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 4: the right wing outran its railheads by ~150-300 km by the Marne; horse transport sustained ~25 km/day for a few weeks.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Reich horse census ~4.5M in 1913; ~715,000 horses requisitioned on mobilisation (Strachan ch. 3).

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before July 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities (Metz, Strasbourg, Koenigsberg), population support; no climate depth.

germany-1914.notes: Snapshot date August 1914 after mobilisation (order of 1 Aug; Feldheer concentrated by 17-18 Aug). Territory and population = the German Empire in Europe incl. Alsace-Lorraine; colonies (10.7M people, B&H Table 2) excluded and not listed in includes. Forces are the whole army; the western deployment was ~1.6M men in 7 armies and the eastern 8th Army ~150,000-200,000. Aircraft are all counted as aircraft_strike because no fighters existed in 1914. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, cruisers and destroyers (incl. high-seas torpedo boats) = ships_major, coastal torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Herwig, Strachan, Conway's) are from standard works not fetched online, graded at most B.

areaKm2.note: world_1938 Germany polygon (already includes Austria and the Sudetenland) = ~560,000 km2 computed on the sphere; plus the Protectorate ~48,900 km2. Published Greater Germany + Protectorate 1939 is ~633,000-635,000 km2, used as mid; the polygon is low.

activePersonnel.note: Wehrmacht after mobilisation (26 Aug 1939): Feldheer ~2.75M, Ersatzheer ~1.0M, Luftwaffe ~0.4M, Kriegsmarine 78,000 on 1 Sep 1939 (Kriegsmarine article), SS-Verfuegungstruppe small. trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: conscription only from 1935, so trained reserve classes were thin; Frieser p. 29 notes half of all soldiers in 1939-40 had only weeks of training. Army grew from ~3.7M to 4.2M by May 1940.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: Luftwaffe incl. flak (~0.4M), navy (78,000), artillery, panzer, engineer, signals and supply troops, staffs and the Ersatzheer. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

mobilizationRatio.note: 17.3M served in Heer, Luftwaffe and navy, 18.2M with the Waffen-SS, over the whole war (Overmans 1999, via https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wehrmacht); ~13M at peak strength. Divided by ~87-90M gives ~0.15-0.21.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8 (Germany, % of GNP at current and 1939 prices): 23% in 1939 (mid), 40% in 1940 (high, the war footing reached within a year). Low ~17% = 1938: COW milex 1938 = 7,415,163 (thousand current US$, https://correlatesofwar.org/wp-content/uploads/NMCv7.zip) against German GNP of ~RM 100-130bn (~US$40-52bn) = ~15-19%. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.12/0.17/0.23 (peacetime mid); war-date snapshot (September 1939 mobilisation) takes the 1939 wartime share as mid.

industrialShare.note: Industry and crafts roughly 45% of output in the late-1930s Reich (Tooze, Wages of Destruction ch. 4, economy overview). Grade C. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). Cited page: "Noch 1937 waren 29 Prozent der Beschaeftigten in Deutschland, 9.388.000 Menschen, in der Landwirtschaft taetig" (a = 0.29); "Deutschland konnte wenige Wochen vor dem Krieg eine Selbstversorgungsrate von 83 Prozent aufweisen" (s = 0.83; 84% per NS figures, 65-68% in 1927-28). Mid 1 - 0.29/0.83 = 0.65. Low a 0.32 (Austria, Sudetenland and the Protectorate more agrarian), s 0.80 = 0.60; high a 0.27, s 0.84 = 0.68. Grade C: two figures combined. Import dependence: ~17% of food imported (fats and feed). audit 2026-10-30: was 0.05/0.15/0.25 (read as self-sufficiency); recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: Males reaching 19-20 in 1939: the 1919-20 birth cohorts (~1.26M and ~1.6M births in the Reich, WWI dip) halved for males, minus mortality, plus Austria and the Czech lands. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

germany-1939.notes: Snapshot date 1 September 1939 (invasion of Poland). Territory and population = Greater Germany (Altreich incl. Saar, Austria annexed March 1938, Sudetenland Oct 1938, Memel March 1939) plus the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia (March 1939). The hb:1938:Germany polygon contains Austria and the Sudetenland but not the Protectorate. includes is empty: Austria and the Czech lands are not separate nations in 1939, so they are folded in rather than listed. Annexed Polish lands (Oct 1939) and Slovakia (client state) excluded. May 1940 reference figures for the battle agent (Frieser, Blitzkrieg Legend p. 35-37 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France): Heer 4.2M, Luftwaffe 1.0M, navy 180,000, Waffen-SS 100,000; 3.0M men in 135 divisions for the offensive; 2,439 tanks and 7,378 guns in the west; Murray Table XII: 4,782 aircraft on 11 May 1940 (1,356 single-engine fighters, 354 twin-engine, 1,711 bombers, 414 dive bombers). COW NMC v6 was not downloadable from correlatesofwar.org; v7 (2025 release) was used. Not sourced line by line: Wehrmacht total on 1 Sep 1939 (no fetched page; cited to Dear & Foot and widely reported ~4.5M). audit 2026-10-30: no basemap between 1938 and 1945 draws the Protectorate with Germany (world_1938 has only a rump Czechoslovakia, 90,899 km2, incl. Slovakia), so the hb:1938:Germany polygon (~560,000 km2) stays; it omits the Protectorate (~48,900 km2) that population and area include.

germany-1944.notes: Snapshot date June 1944 (Normandy landings 6 June; Operation Bagration 22 June). Territory = the Greater German Reich (Germany, Austria, Sudetenland, annexed Polish and western territories); occupied Europe (France, the Low Countries, Norway, the General Government, the occupied USSR, Italy, Hungary from March 1944) not counted as territory; basesAbroad lists key positions. The border uses world_1938 (nearest at or before 1944). Forces are the whole Wehrmacht incl. Waffen-SS. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). audit 2026-10-30: no basemap draws the 1944 Reich (world_1945 shows occupation zones); the hb:1938:Germany polygon (~560,000 km2) omits the annexed Polish and western lands that population and area include.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.99. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/DEU/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.07% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.88 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.87-0.89). Mid 1 - 0.011/0.88 = 0.99. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.87 = 0.98. High: s 0.89 = 0.99. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 88% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Germany is a net food importer but a large producer of cereals, dairy and pork.

Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. areaKm2.note: world_1715 United Kingdom (Great Britain) 205,174 km2 + Kingdom of Ireland 82,955 km2 on the sphere = 288,129 km2; Great Britain is ~229,000 km2 in reality, so high allows for the coarse coastline.

population.note: HYDE via OWID: United Kingdom (modern borders, incl. Northern Ireland) 9,288,177 (1750) and 9,823,145 (1760); plus the rest of Ireland. Wrigley-Schofield England 1756 ~6.1M, Webster's Scotland 1755 1.27M, Ireland ~2.4M -> ~10M for the British crowns incl. Ireland. Colonies excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: United Kingdom 23.2% (1750); de Vries gives England 16.7% (towns 10,000+, 1750); Ireland and Scotland lower. Mid 20%.

activePersonnel.note: Brewer, The Sinews of Power (1989) table 2.1: Seven Years War annual average ~93,000 army (British and Irish establishments incl. colonies, excluding Hanoverian and Hessian troops in British pay) and ~74,000-82,000 navy; the Dutch States Navy table gives British naval personnel 85,000 in 1760 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_States_Navy). 1759 near the peak.

trainedReserves.note: Embodied county militia under the Militia Act 1757: ~17,000 in 1759 rising to ~30,000 (Brewer ch. 2); counted as trainedReserves per convention. German auxiliaries in British pay (~50,000) excluded. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

supportPersonnel.note: Navy and marines ~80,000-85,000 (85,000 personnel in 1760, Dutch States Navy table after Rodger and Glete), Royal Artillery (~2,500, 30+ companies), engineers and the Board of Ordnance staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak forces ~200,000 incl. militia (Brewer table 2.1) on ~10M = 2%; ceiling 4-5% (reached in the Napoleonic Wars with volunteers). audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: the earliest fetched figure is OWID/Herrendorf United Kingdom 1801 = 30.8% (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/employment-by-economic-sector.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); Britain c. 1760 was more agrarian (~0.42 assumed) and Ireland (~2.4M of ~10M) ~0.7 (assumed), giving a ~0.49. s = 1 assumed: England was a grain exporter until the 1760s. Mid 1 - 0.49 = 0.51; low a 0.55; high a 0.40. Grade D. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.2/0.3/0.4, inconsistent with the formula; recomputed.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Overseas, sea transport supplied expeditions across the Atlantic and to India. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

great-britain-1759.notes: Snapshot = 1759, the Annus Mirabilis of the Seven Years War. Population: Great Britain and Ireland (the Irish establishment of the army is counted); American colonies, India presidencies and West Indies are bases only, and colonial provincial troops and East India Company sepoys are excluded. Personnel convention: regular army and navy are active; embodied militia is trainedReserves; Hanoverian, Hessian and Brunswick troops in British pay are excluded. Ship-of-the-line count depends on whether ships in ordinary are included (the mid counts ships in sea pay).

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland" = 288,100 km2 on the sphere; Great Britain ~229,000 + Ireland ~84,000 = ~314,000 km2. The 1815 file also has a "United Kingdom" feature that is only the Caribbean colonies.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1816 = 19,520k (UK of Great Britain and Ireland). 1815 taken slightly lower. GB 1811 census ~12.6M civilians plus Ireland ~6M.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share, United Kingdom (modern borders, mostly GB): 32.1% (1810), 35.4% (1820) = high end. Ireland ~7-8% urban pulls the UK-with-Ireland figure down; towns of 5,000+ in England ~25-30%.

activePersonnel.note: Regular army peaked at over 250,000 in 1813 (page); by June 1815 ~220,000-230,000 after the 1814 reductions and Hundred Days re-expansion, plus Ordnance corps (Royal Artillery, engineers) ~25,000 and Royal Navy with marines ~100,000-140,000. COW NMC v7 milper 1816 = 255,000 after demobilisation had begun. East India Company armies (~200,000, mostly sepoys) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Militia (ballot-raised, embodiable), local militia and yeomanry. Volunteers reached ~329,000 in 1806 (page) but were largely disbanded by 1814-15; the regular militia was partly disembodied in 1814. Range spans 1815 militia plus surviving local forces.

supportPersonnel.note: Royal Navy seamen and Royal Marines ~100,000 in mid-1815 (down from ~140,000 voted in 1813-14), Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers ~22,000, commissariat, staff and drivers ~8,000. Reconstruction from the British Army page and Rodger (isbn:978-0-14-102690-9, ch. on 1815 manning).

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak 1809-1813: regular army ~250,000 (British Army page) + navy ~140,000 + militia ~100,000 + local militia/volunteers ~300,000 = ~790,000 of ~18M = 4.4%. Voluntary enlistment, no conscription for the regulars.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Line and Guards battalions incl. the King's German Legion. Whole infantry was 126,677 in 1803 (page); 1813-15 peak army >250,000 with roughly 60% infantry. Includes colonial garrisons (West Indies, Canada, Gibraltar, Malta, Cape, Ceylon).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID), United Kingdom 1815 = 3,489 (2011 int$), a Great Britain-weighted series. Ireland was much poorer (roughly half), so the UK-with-Ireland mean is put near 2,950; high = the GB value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: at war in June 1815; army, navy and ordnance took ~£60-70M of ~£110M public spending at the 1814 peak against a national income of ~£350-400M. Low = 1790s peacetime share; COW milex 1816 = £16.9M (post-war).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Deane and Cole style national accounts put manufacturing, mining and building near 30% of British income around 1811-1821; Ireland lowers the UK share.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/employment-by-economic-sector.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true), United Kingdom agriculture share of employment 1801 = 30.8%, 1841 = 21.1%, interpolated ~27% for 1815 ("about a third" for Britain). The snapshot includes Ireland (~6M of 19.3M), more agrarian; ~0.65 assumed for it (not fetched), giving a ~0.39. s = 1 assumed: grain imports small, Ireland exported food. Mid 1 - 0.39 = 0.61; low a 0.45; high 0.73 if the OWID series already includes Ireland. Grade D. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.3/0.4/0.5, which contradicted the note's own farm share; recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ships of the line launched or captured per year 1803-1815 in Royal and merchant yards.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field-gun output of the Woolwich foundry and contractors (Carron, Walker) per year; naval guns far more numerous.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: turnpike trusts managed ~20,000 miles (~32,000 km) of improved road in Britain by the 1820s; Irish mail roads added.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: London, Liverpool, Bristol, Glasgow, Hull, Leith, Newcastle, Portsmouth, Plymouth, Chatham, Cork, Dublin.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 2,323k tons (United Kingdom 1815, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Peninsular armies operated 150-400 km from sea depots with mule trains; Britain's reach is by sea.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: roughly 1.2-1.5M horses in Britain plus Irish horses and oxen.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified dockyards and population support; insular, no harsh-climate depth.

great-britain-1815.notes: Snapshot = United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland in June 1815 (Hundred Days, Waterloo campaign). Population and territory = Great Britain and Ireland; colonies and the East India Company (its presidency armies of ~200,000) are excluded and includes is empty. Personnel: regular army, Ordnance corps and navy = active; militia, local militia and yeomanry = trainedReserves. Waterloo campaign: Wellington 107,000 (Anglo-allied, of whom ~31,000 British), Bluecher 123,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterloo_campaign). COW data start in 1816, so 1816 values are used as anchors. Branch counts are reconstructions, grade C. Frigates are counted as ships_minor to match france-1805.

areaKm2.note: League of Nations Statistical Year-Book 1939/40, Table 2: Greece 130 thousand km2 (low, mid). world_1938 Greece polygon = 139,209 km2 computed by the pipeline (high). The Dodecanese were Italian.

population.note: OWID population (HYDE/UN) Greece 1940 = 7,310,983 (mid). COW NMC v7 tpop 1940 = 7,319k (high); samlib table (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)) 7.2M for 1940 (low). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 estimate xii.1938 = 7,107k; census 1928 = 6,205k.

urbanization.note: Definitions differ. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_Greece_and_the_Greek_world: the 1928 census counted 45.6% of Greeks in urban or semi-urban places (high; 1920: 36.3%). HYDE 3.5 via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): Greece 1930 = 15%, 1940 = 20% (low, larger towns only). Mid 0.33 = midpoint of the two definitions.

activePersonnel.note: Composite for November 1940, general mobilisation ordered 28 October. Army: 14 infantry divisions x ~14,000 = 196,000 (division size from Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books), MAA 514), 1 cavalry division ~5,000 and 3 infantry brigades ~15,000; corps troops, Metaxas Line garrisons and depots ~60,000; navy 6,300 regulars + 11,000 reservists = 17,300 (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); air force ~3,250 (~250 officers + 3,000 men, same page). Sum ~296,500 -> mid 300,000. Low = divisions only partly mobilised on 28 October (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War). High = the 450,000-man combat strength the small-arms stocks were built for (MAA 514 via the samlib page); by April 1941 the army had 20 divisions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Greek service was 24 months with a long reserve obligation; the veterans of 1912-22 were in their 40s. Men not yet called up in November 1940; reserve classes were drafted through the winter to form 6 more divisions by April 1941.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Everything outside the P roles in the 300,000 composite: artillery (~900 guns), engineers, signals, the pack trains of a mountain army, Metaxas Line fortress artillery, navy 17,300 and air force ~3,250.

mobilizationRatio.note: Reached mobilisation: ~300,000 in November 1940 and 20 divisions (~430,000 with services) by April 1941 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War), of 7.3M population = 0.04-0.06; high 0.07 = 512,000, above the 450,000-man arms stock (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Triangular divisions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); battalion = 58 officers + 1,000-1,100 men, 3 battalions per regiment (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)). 14 divisions x 3 regiments x 3 battalions x ~1,100 = 139,000, plus the 3 brigades (~12,000) = ~150,000. Low = partial mobilisation of 28 October; high = 20 divisions of April 1941.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: most equipment of First World War issue from Belgium, Austria, Poland and France (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); per regiment 2 65 mm mountain guns, 4 81 mm mortars, 8 heavy and 36 light machine guns (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); no tanks and 24 AT guns in all.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 24-month conscription, officers veterans of the Balkan Wars, the First World War and Asia Minor (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); the army beat the Italian invasion and counter-attacked into Albania (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted strength of the one cavalry division: two cavalry regiments of four battalions (squadrons) each, a horse artillery battalion and a mounted machine-gun battalion (structure from Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); squadron sizes not given.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horse cavalry with rifles and machine guns, 12 guns in the division.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regular cavalry cadre; used in the Pindus battle.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox (Clodfelter and army.gr): 940 artillery pieces in October 1940 (high); Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): about 900 guns (low, mid). 315-320 mortars and 24 AT guns not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mixed French, Austrian and Skoda guns of 1910s-1920s designs, 9 batteries per division (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); ammunition down to less than two months by February 1941.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: effective mountain gunnery against Italian columns at Kalpaki and the Pindus (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: the Royal Hellenic Air Force had 45 fighters (mid, high); operational at the outbreak 24 PZL P.24 and 9 Bloch MB.151 (low = 33).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: PZL P.24 gull-wing monoplanes and MB.151 against Fiat CR.42 and G.50 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: PZL P.24 squadrons intercepted escorted Italian bomber raids from 2 November 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: 24 light bombers (low; operational 11 Blenheim IV, 10 Fairey Battle, 8 Potez 633), 12 Dornier Do 22G torpedo bombers (mid = 36); high adds 28 naval cooperation and 9 reconnaissance aircraft (61). ~65 auxiliary aircraft not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Blenheim IV modern; Battle, Potez 633 and Do 22 obsolescent; spare parts cut off when the suppliers were occupied.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: as fighters.

count.note: AA guns at 4 per battery. Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books) (MAA 514): 24 Krupp 88 mm and 162 Rheinmetall 20 mm and 37 mm AA guns bought in Germany (186 / 4 = ~46); ~190 AA guns in all (mid 48); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox: 270 AA guns (high 68). Low allows for unserviceable pieces.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: modern German guns, but few and concentrated at Athens, Piraeus and Thessaloniki.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: new arm formed 1937-39.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: the elderly cruiser Georgios Averof, two modern destroyers (Vasilefs Georgios class), four Italian-built Hydra-class destroyers and four obsolete Aetos-class destroyers = 11 (mid). Low = Averof plus the 6 newer destroyers. High adds the two pre-1914 battleships Kilkis and Lemnos listed by Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books), which the same page rates as of no combat value.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): by the late 1930s all Greek ships larger than a destroyer had lost combat value; only 2 of 4 ordered destroyers delivered.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: escorted the convoys that moved 80,000 men and 100,000 animals by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War: fifteen obsolete torpedo boats and about thirty auxiliary vessels; Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books) gives 13 old torpedo boats and 2 MTBs (mid 17 with the MTBs, low 15). High adds the ~30 auxiliaries (minesweepers, tenders).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 1910s torpedo boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: convoy escort and patrol duty throughout the war.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War and Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books): six old French-built Katsonis-class submarines of the mid-1920s.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1920s French boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: regular crews from the 6,300 long-service personnel of the navy (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); boats kept at sea through the war.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Papagos and the General Staff pre-planned the defence (plans IB, IBa, IBb), shifted the Macedonian divisions to Epirus once Bulgaria stayed neutral and counter-attacked on 14 November (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Greece_during_World_War_II); later the belated withdrawal from Albania in April 1941. About 1,500 Venizelist officers had been purged (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75 (national army) and above. Evidence: national war against an invader; Metaxas regime and its opponents rallied; minorities small after the 1923 population exchange.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0 (highly motivated). Evidence: Greek reservists drove a larger, better-equipped Italian army back into Albania in winter conditions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905) toward 8 (1943). Evidence: Mannlicher-Schoenauer rifles, Hotchkiss and Saint-Etienne M07 machine guns of First World War issue, 81 mm mortars, 65-155 mm Schneider, Krupp and captured Skoda guns (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

armor.note: Anchor: 7. No tanks in service in October 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); value only matters if armour is added.

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnought era). Evidence: 1911 armoured cruiser Averof, 1930s destroyers, 1920s submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 = concrete lines (Maginot). Evidence: the Metaxas Line, 21 concrete forts in Eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Greece_during_World_War_II); field works elsewhere.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: 600 military vehicles (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War infobox); Epirus supplied by pack animals over few roads; lack of motor transport and pack animals made the April 1941 withdrawal impossible.

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telephone and telegraph). Evidence: two signal companies per division (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)), little radio.

isr.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: Hs 126 and Potez 25 observation aircraft, cavalry reconnaissance; no radar.

air.note: Anchor: between 7 (1914) and 8 (1943). Evidence: PZL P.24, MB.151 and Blenheim IV monoplanes alongside Breguet 19 and Potez 25 biplanes (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Greece: 1940 = 3,543 (low, mid), 1939 = 4,205 (high; 1938 = 4,267), 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Greece: 1939 = 4.73% (low, last peacetime), 1940 = 7.68% (mid), 1941 = 11.35% (high). COW milex 1940 = 62,145 thousand current US$ (1938 30,122).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry share of output. Protected industry grew in the 1930s, 1939 industrial output 179% of 1928 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_Greece_and_the_Greek_world), but the economy was dominated by agriculture, shipping and trade; tobacco, textiles and food processing led.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a/s with a = agricultural share of employment (~0.55) and s = grain self-sufficiency (~0.65): 1 - 0.55/0.65 = 0.15. Greece imported a large part of its wheat; the 1941-42 famine followed the blockade of imports. Import-dependent, kept positive per the convention.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age (21) per year: the 1919 birth cohort of ~5M people, depressed by mobilisation 1912-22, half male, ~70% survival; refugees of 1922-23 added older men only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads usable by motor vehicles; Epirus and the Pindus were reached by few roads, and the poor land network made sea transport essential (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War).

railKm.note: CHAT railline Greece 1938 = 2,976 km; no line reached Epirus.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Piraeus, Thessaloniki, Patras, Volos, Kavala and Heraklion; ports carried the 80,000 men and 100,000 animals moved to the front by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)).

merchantTonnage.note: GRT to DWT x 1.5 (low x 1.3, high x 1.6). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 Table 113 (https://www.istmat.org/files/uploads/49915/09_strany_mira_-_transport_torgovlya_platyozhnyy_balans.pdf): Greece 1,889k GRT in June 1938 (low 2,456k, mid 2,834k); CHAT shipton 1938 = 1,930k GRT (high 3,088k). Greek ships lost while neutral in 1939-40 are not deducted.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Mountain front supplied by pack animals from railheads in Thessaly and western Macedonia and from the ports; 600 military vehicles in all.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Low = 100,000 army animals moved by sea (Temezhnikov, Armed forces of Greece 1930-1939 (samlib.ru compilation citing Osprey MAA 514 The Greek Army 1940-41 and Soviet reference books)); national stock of horses, mules and donkeys guessed at 0.5-0.9M.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before July 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: mountain home terrain with a united, mobilised population against an invader (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Italian_War); low 1.2 for the open plains of Macedonia and Thrace and the dependence on sea supply.

greece-1940.notes: Snapshot date November 1940: Italy invaded on 28 October, general mobilisation followed and the Greek counter-offensive began on 14 November. Active personnel is a composite of division strengths (14 infantry divisions, 1 cavalry division, 3 brigades), navy and air force (range 250,000-450,000). Equipment from the Greco-Italian War article (infobox citing Clodfelter and army.gr; air and naval order of battle from MAA 514) and a samlib.ru compilation (Temezhnikov) citing MAA 514. The army had no tanks, so no armour role. No production entries: Greece had little arms industry; heavy equipment came from abroad and the suppliers were occupied by 1940 (Greco-Italian War article). Weakest values: P-role split, trained reserves, food surplus, roads and animals (educated guesses). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: cruiser and destroyers ships_major, torpedo boats and auxiliaries ships_minor.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 15.2% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.15 -> 0.87. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/GRC/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 10.68% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.79 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.78-0.82). Mid 1 - 0.107/0.79 = 0.87. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.78 = 0.82. High: s 0.82 = 0.87. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 79% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Exporter of olive oil, fruit and fish; imports grain and meat.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 5,046,070 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.724% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 57,769. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Domestic yards assist FDI/Constellation work; most hulls built abroad. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Hellenic_Navy_ships)

roadKm.note: As quoted: 117,000 km (2018).

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 2,339 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 1 large + 7 medium = 8.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 53,459 thousand DWT under the Greek flag; Greek owners control the world's largest merchant fleet (~400 million DWT under all flags, educated reading of the same list), high.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. By analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment (truck-based, depots every ~150-200 km).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. FAS lists the five US B61 host states (Belgium, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Turkey); this state is not one of them.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: mountains, fortified islands and Evros, strong population support.

greece-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:GRC. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from the Wikipedia Hellenic Army equipment list, active Greek military aircraft list and active Hellenic Navy ship list; drones = Group 2+ only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Large Cold War stocks in reserve make high/low spreads wide.

areaKm2.note: Infobox: 3.5 million km2 (high, Turchin et al.) and 1.7 million (low, Taagepera). The world_400 Gupta Empire polygon measures 2.48 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_400.geojson, mid). Seshat codes only 0.8-0.9 million for 320 CE, before Samudragupta's conquests.

population.note: Educated guess. The Wikipedia Gupta Empire infobox (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire) gives 75,000,000 for the 5th century (high; a Maddison-type all-India figure). HYDE puts all of India at 90M in 400 (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); Dyson's 15-30M for Mauryan times implies far less. The Guptas held the Ganges plain, Malwa and Gujarat, perhaps 40-50% of the subcontinent; mid 35M is an educated split.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pataliputra ~150,000 (Seshat 388); Faxian (405-411) describes populous towns in Magadha and Mathura.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. No contemporary army figure survives (Wikipedia notes a paucity of sources). Scaled from population (~0.4%) and from the Maurya snapshot.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Feudatory (samanta) contingents and allied kings who paid tribute.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts (2-3 per elephant), siege engineers, river craft crews and commissariat.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Royal army plus contingents of feudatory (samanta) rulers; an agrarian ceiling of a few percent.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured horse archers and sword cavalry, the core of the army (Gupta Empire page; coins of Chandragupta II show mounted archers).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: heavy cavalry archers, a Gupta innovation in Indian warfare

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal household troops

count.note: Educated guess. Light horse and scouts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mixed

count.note: Educated guess. Royal spear and sword infantry; feudatory contingents are in trainedReserves.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mixed royal and feudatory troops

count.note: Educated guess. Archers with the Indian long bow.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: long bow

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mixed

count.note: Educated guess. Light infantry supporting cavalry and elephants (Gupta Empire page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light kit

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: levies

count.note: Educated guess. Elephant corps under a mahapilupati; village patrol units of one elephant, one chariot, three horse and five foot (War elephant page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: trained war elephants with dedicated officers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: standing elephant establishment

count.note: Educated guess. Chariotry was still one of the five arms but obsolescent.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: obsolete

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: ceremonial

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Samudragupta's and Chandragupta II's campaigns; Western Satraps defeated by c. 395-409

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: royal core plus feudatory contingents

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (recent victories). Evidence: conquest of Malwa, Gujarat and Saurashtra

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (300 BCE) plus. Evidence: iron and steel weapons, horse archery, siege engines (Gupta Empire page)

armor.note: Anchor: 3 (mail, cuirass). Evidence: armoured cavalry archers

ships.note: Anchor: between 2 and 3. Evidence: ships named among the five arms (Gunaighar copper plate); coastal trade

fortification.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: walled cities and hill forts

logistics.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: roads and river transport of the Ganges basin

communications.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: courier system

isr.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: spies and scouts on the classical Indian model

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no India value before 1600 (1,264); its year-1 values are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, Belgium/France 956 (2011 int$). Ancient South Asia placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Feudatory system shifted part of the military burden off the treasury.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron metallurgy (Delhi iron pillar of this reign), textiles, guild crafts.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Ganges plain agriculture.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha trade roads.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Tamralipti, Bharukaccha and Saurashtra ports after the Satrap conquest.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Indian Ocean trade to Southeast Asia and the west; no figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ox-cart and river logistics.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen and buffalo of an agrarian population of ~35M.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities, monsoon.

gupta-400.notes: Snapshot 400 CE under Chandragupta II, after the conquest of the Western Satraps. No contemporary army count survives; all force numbers are educated guesses scaled from population and from the Maurya snapshot, so the army block is the weakest part. Kalidasa's claim of 21 kingdoms conquered is poetry. Population convention: directly ruled lands; tributary kings and frontier republics are excluded. Era is iron (classical, before 476) per the schema spans. Personnel: active = the royal army and elephant corps; trainedReserves = feudatory (samanta) and allied contingents; mobilizable = population x ratio.

Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Argentine Republic, Federative Republic of Brazil, Republic of Chile, Republic of Colombia, Republic of Cuba, Republic of Peru, Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela) and graded D. areaKm2.note: world_1700 "Austrian Empire" polygons = 426,621 km2 on the sphere but cover mainly Hungary, Croatia and Transylvania; the hereditary lands, Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia (~200,000 km2) lie inside the Holy Roman Empire polygon of that file and are not drawn. Sum ~600,000 km2. The map border therefore understates the monarchy.

population.note: HYDE via OWID (1700, modern borders): Austria 2.12M, Czechia 3.24M, Hungary 1.50M, Slovakia 1.14M, Croatia 0.66M, Slovenia 0.25M, plus Silesia (~1.0M), Transylvania (~0.8M) and South Tyrol/Trentino (~0.2M) = ~10.9M. The Military Revolution article gives 8M for c. 1650 (before the reconquest of Hungary). Mid 10.5M. Spanish Netherlands and Milan (1714) excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Austria 4.8%, Czechia 4.8%, Hungary 4.8% (1700, de Vries-type). Mid 5%.

activePersonnel.note: Kaiserliche Armee (the Habsburg standing army) averaged ~70,000 in the Great Turkish War (1683-89) and the Nine Years War (Wilson 2016 via the Imperial Army of the Holy Roman Emperor article); Parker gives 110,000-130,000 for c. 1700-10 (Military Revolution article) and 20,000-24,000 for the 1650s. After Karlowitz (1699) regiments were reduced; mid ~80,000 incl. Danube flotilla and artillery. Reichsarmee contingents of the Empire excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Military Frontier border militia (Grenzer, ~20,000-40,000 able to serve), the Hungarian noble insurrectio and Bohemian/Austrian Landesdefension levies. Hochedlinger, Austria's Wars of Emergence (isbn:0-582-29084-8), ch. 6, describes the Grenzer as a part-time militia.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: artillery (Feldzeugamt), pontoniers and Danube flotilla (Tschaikisten), staff and commissariat.

mobilizationRatio.note: Peaks of 110,000-130,000 regulars (Military Revolution article, Parker) plus Grenzer on ~10.5M = 1.5-2%; ceiling ~3-4% with insurrectio levies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Hungarian campaigns followed the Danube. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: Hungarian horse and cattle herds, Bohemian draught animals.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: fortified Danube line, Alps and Bohemian hills; Hungary restive (Rakoczi revolt 1703).

habsburg-austria-1700.notes: Snapshot = 1700, after the Peace of Karlowitz (1699) and before the War of the Spanish Succession. Population: hereditary lands, Bohemian crown lands (incl. Silesia) and Hungary with Croatia and Transylvania; the Spanish inheritance (1714) and Reich contingents excluded. Personnel convention: the Kaiserliche Armee regiments are active; Grenzer, Hungarian insurrectio and Landesdefension levies are trainedReserves. The map border (world_1700 "Austrian Empire") draws only the Hungarian lands; the core lands sit in that file's Holy Roman Empire polygon, so the rendered area understates the monarchy. Habsburg army size in 1700 is uncertain (post-war reductions); range 60,000-100,000.

areaKm2.note: world_1800 polygon "Austrian Empire" = 619,500 km2 on the sphere; Habsburg lands in 1805 also held Venetia, Dalmatia, West Galicia and Further Austria.

population.note: Composite from HYDE/Gapminder (OWID) modern-border totals for 1800: Austria 3.0M, Czechia 5.5M, Hungary 3.25M, Slovakia 2.1M, Croatia 1.2M, Slovenia 0.5M, plus Galicia (~4.5M of Poland/Ukraine), Transylvania (~1.7M of Romania), Banat/Vojvodina (~0.8M), Venetia and Dalmatia (~2.3M), Tyrol/Trentino (~0.3M) = ~25M; low allows for overlap.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) 1800: Austria 10%, Czechia 7.9%, Hungary 7.9%. Habsburg average ~7%.

activePersonnel.note: War footing Sept 1805: Archduke Charles 95,000 in Italy, Archduke John 23,000 in Tyrol, Ferdinand/Mack 72,000 in Bavaria (page, citing Chandler 1966 p. 382), plus the reserve in Bohemia and Inner Austria, Grenz cordon and garrisons. Mack's force at Ulm 74,000 (Ulm campaign page, Fisher and Fremont-Barnes p. 41).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: furloughed men and the Hungarian noble insurrectio; the Landwehr did not exist until 1808.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery corps ~13,000, pioneers, pontonniers, Fuhrwesen train ~8,000, small navy ~2,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: Austria raised ~550,000-600,000 including Landwehr in 1809 from ~22M (2.5-2.7%).

habsburg-austria-1805.notes: Snapshot = Austrian Empire in September 1805 at the opening of the War of the Third Coalition. Territory and population = Habsburg hereditary lands, Hungary, Galicia (incl. West Galicia), Venetia, Dalmatia and Tyrol; includes is empty. Personnel: line, Grenz and cavalry on war footing = active; furloughed men and Hungarian insurrectio = trainedReserves (no Landwehr before 1808). Theatre strengths from the War of the Third Coalition and Ulm campaign pages (Chandler, Fisher and Fremont-Barnes); branch split and artillery count are reconstructions or educated guesses. No COW data before 1816 and no Maddison series for the whole monarchy.

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "Austrian Empire" = 605,200 km2 on the sphere. The 1866 monarchy (without Lombardy, lost 1859, with Venetia until October 1866) was ~650,000 km2; Austrian Empire page infobox gives 698,700 km2 for the pre-1859 empire.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop: 1865 = 37,004k, 1866 = 34,482k (annual value after the cession of Venetia, ~2.5M). In June 1866 Venetia was still Austrian, so mid sits between.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) 1860/1870: Austria 23%/26%, Czechia 15%/17%, Hungary 10%/12%; Galicia and the Balkan lands lower. COW upop 1866 = 1,122k (cities 100k+) = 3%.

activePersonnel.note: Austro-Prussian War infobox: Austria 407,223 deployed (Clodfelter 2017 p. 183). Nordarmee ~240,000 incl. Saxons (Koeniggraetz page: 184,000 Austrians and 22,000 Saxons at the battle), Suedarmee ~75,000, garrisons. COW milper 1865 = 300,000 is a peacetime annual value.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: depot (Ersatz) battalions and recalled reservists still forming in June-July 1866; Austria had no Landwehr comparable to Prussia's.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery ~25,000, engineers and pioneers ~5,000, train ~10,000, navy ~10,000 (Tegetthoff's fleet). Reconstruction.

han--100.notes: Snapshot 100 BCE, late in Emperor Wu's reign, after the Ferghana war. Force sizes follow Chang 2007 (Fall of Imperial China), the only modern quantitative reconstruction found; it is generous. Population convention: everything inside the empire; the 57.7M of the 2 CE census is the high bound. Ships are platform counts; their crews are supportPersonnel. GDP per capita is a regional analogy (grade D). Personnel: active = professionals plus conscripts serving their year (Chang's standing army); trainedReserves = discharged men liable to annual recall; mobilizable = population x ratio.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 250,000-350,000 km2 at 1300 and 300,000-400,000 km2 at 1200 BCE; Taagepera 1978 gives 0.45 million km2 for 1250-1220 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). The historical-basemaps world_bc1500 'Hittites' polygon (central Anatolia to Ugarit and Carchemish; bc1500 is the nearest file at or before 1274) measures ~412,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON.

population.note: Seshat codes 1,300,000-2,000,000 for the New Kingdom of Hatti (1400-1180 BCE). Bryce 2024 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) gives 'more than 200,000' and Zsolt Simon 140,000-150,000 for the kingdom; those figures cover Hatti proper only and are incompatible with the 47,500-man Kadesh army unless the vassal kingdoms are counted, so they are excluded. Range includes the Syrian and western Anatolian vassals inside the border.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Hattusa itself may have held only 2,300-4,600 people (Seeher via Bryce, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites); Seshat codes the largest settlement at 15,000-20,000. Syrian cities (Ugarit, Carchemish, Aleppo) were larger.

activePersonnel.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Mid = the Kadesh army (~47,500 incl. crews) as the standing order of battle at campaign start; low = Holmes' 15,000 infantry plus chariot crews; high adds garrisons against the Kaska and in the west.

trainedReserves.note: Bryce: up to ~100,000 could be called for military service, incl. labour; reserves callable within a month are a fraction of that. Estimate.

supportPersonnel.note: Kadesh: Healy 1993 (pp. 21-22, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kadesh) gives 2,500 chariots with 9,000-11,100 charioteers (three-man crews) and 15,000 (Holmes)-40,000 infantry, the latter not engaged; the Egyptian Poem claims 37,000 infantry and 3,500 chariots (2,500 + 1,000). Bryce 2024 (pp. 130-134, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hittites) puts the Kadesh muster at 47,500 and Hatti's maximum military service at ~100,000. The army included contingents of some 16-19 vassal lands (Arzawa, Carchemish, Aleppo, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna...). Chariot crews: 2,500-3,500 vehicles x 3 men (Healy 9,000-11,100) minus the infantry rider counted nowhere else, plus logistics.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Feudal service obligations of land holders and vassal treaties requiring contingents; Bryce's 100,000 for service against a ~1.6 M empire is ~6%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

holy-roman-empire-1200.notes: Snapshot = 1200, during the throne war between Philip of Swabia (Hohenstaufen) and Otto IV (Welf). The Kingdom of Sicily (Frederick II, a minor) is not counted. No modern total for the imperial army exists; the household-plus-ministeriales active force and the knightly reserve are educated guesses anchored on Legnano (~3,000 imperial heavy horse, Grillo 2024) and Bouvines 1214, where Otto IV fielded 1,300-1,500 knights and ~7,500 infantry, mostly Flemish and Low Country allies (Verbruggen 1997, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Bouvines). Population convention: imperial Germany, Bohemia, the Low Countries, Burgundy-Arles and imperial Italy.

areaKm2.note: Wikipedia infobox gives 282,870 km2 (Hungary proper, low); the world_1200 union of Hungary and Croatia measures 369,753 km2 (high). Mid adds Croatia-Slavonia and Dalmatia to the infobox value.

population.note: Infobox: 2,000,000 c. 1200 (J. C. Russell in the Fontana Economic History of Europe). Engel (Realm of St Stephen, 2001, p. 59) gives a density of 4-5 per km2 (low). HYDE/OWID 1200 country series for Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia and Transylvania sum to ~2.4-2.6M (high). Before the 1241-42 losses of 15-25% (Mohi article).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Esztergom, Szekesfehervar and Pest were the only sizable towns; settler "guest" towns small.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element: royal household and banderium, castle-warrior (varjobbagy) garrisons on duty and the Templar/Hospitaller and episcopal households near the king.

trainedReserves.note: The host that met the Mongols at Mohi (11 April 1241): contemporary sources ~15,000-30,000 cavalry; the Epternacher Notiz reports 10,000 Hungarian dead, "almost the entire army"; other modern estimates 20,000-70,000 (Mohi infobox).
