foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.3 -> 0.97. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/HUN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 4.11% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.28 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.03-1.44). Mid 1 - 0.041/1.28 = 0.97. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.03 = 0.94. High: s 1.44 = 0.97. Net exporter: production is about 128% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net exporter of grain and meat.

inca-empire-1530.notes: Snapshot = 1530, during the Inca civil war between Huascar and Atahualpa (1529-32), two years before Pizarro reached Cajamarca. Personnel convention: the noble guard, officers, garrisons and the veteran field armies under arms are activePersonnel; the mit'a levy is trainedReserves. Civil-war army sizes (Huascar ~400,000, Atahualpa 250,000) come from chronicles via the Inca Civil War article and are not used as mids. No horses, no iron, no gunpowder. Population is disputed (4-37 million; most 6-14 million). D'Altroy (The Incas) not consulted directly. Population convention: all four suyu, both factions.

india-1971.notes: Snapshot date 3 December 1971 (Pakistani pre-emptive air strikes; India-Pakistan war of 1971, 3-16 December). Population convention: everything inside the hb:1960:India polygon (Indian-administered Kashmir included; Sikkim a protectorate, excluded). Main source for the order of battle is the declassified CIA intelligence memorandum of 13 Sep 1971 (https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0000399238), table as of mid-1971; the IISS Military Balance 1971-72 and Sisson and Rose, War and Secession (1990), could not be fetched and are not cited line by line. Theatre deployment for the battle agent (CIA memo): ~200,000 troops opposite West Pakistan, ~100,000 opposite East Pakistan, ~150,000 on the China border, ~600,000 elsewhere. The eastern offensive used nine infantry divisions (war article) plus ~175,000 Mukti Bahini (not counted here; they belong to the Bangladesh provisional government). Paramilitary (BSF, Assam Rifles) excluded from activePersonnel; COW milper 1,560,000 likely includes some of them. Infantry splits are reconstructions from division and battalion counts (grade C). Ratings and tech use the SOURCES.md rubric and anchors.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.25 -> 0.59. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IND/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 41.63% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.02 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.01-1.02). Mid 1 - 0.416/1.02 = 0.59. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.01 = 0.51. High: s 1.02 = 0.59. Net exporter: production is about 102% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food exporter (rice, wheat, sugar) with large buffer stocks; per-capita intake still low.

population.note: OWID (UN WPP) Iran 1980 = 39.84M; COW NMC v7 tpop 1980 = 39,291k; MB 1981-82 = 39,665,000; MB 1980-81 = 38,250,000 (low, older estimate).

urbanization.note: OWID urban share Iran 1980 = 50.7%. COW upop/tpop 1980 = 13,588/39,291 = 0.35 (cities over 100,000 only), not used for mid.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): total 195,000 (army 150,000 incl. 100,000 conscripts, navy 10,000, air force 35,000) + Revolutionary Guards (Pasdaran) ~30,000 in Sep 1980 (40,000 by mid-1981, MB 1981-82 para-military) = ~225,000. IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 240,000 pre-1979. Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 110,000-215,000 soldiers. COW NMC v7 milper 1980 = 305,000 (high). Pasdaran counted inside active because it fought as a combat force from the first week; gendarmerie excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): RESERVES 400,000 (former conscripts, high). Mid discounts for post-revolution disorganisation; Basij volunteers (formed Nov 1979) were untrained in Sep 1980 and are not counted.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: navy 10,000-20,000 and air force 35,000-70,000 (MB 1981-82 vs 1980-81) + army armour, artillery, aviation (~700 helicopters), HAWK battalions and logistics, ~60,000-70,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 600,000-850,000 soldiers in 1988 out of ~52M, plus Basij rotating through the front, so several million served over the war. Ratio of a total-war call-up 4-10% of population; Iran never mobilised to the levels of Iraq (COW milper peak).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): 4 armoured and 4 infantry 'divisions' (at least 2 of each only brigade strength). ~3 infantry divisions and the mech infantry of the armoured divisions at 50-60% strength after desertions = ~60,000 infantry. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: G3 rifles, TOW and Dragon ATGW (MB 1980-81) were modern 1970s Western kit.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 100,000 of 150,000 army personnel were conscripts (MB 1981-82); training collapsed in 1979-80 and 12,000 officers were purged (Iran-Iraq War article).

iran-1980.notes: Snapshot date 22 September 1980 (Iraqi invasion). The IISS Military Balance 1980-81 (data July 1980) reprinted pre-revolution holdings and said present totals were considerably less; the 1981-82 edition shows post-losses holdings. Equipment counts therefore span operable (low, Pollack and Razoux via the Iran-Iraq War infobox) to nominal inventory (high); mid is the operable-plus-repairable fleet. Personnel: active = regular army, navy, air force + Pasdaran (~30,000, fought as combat troops from the start); Basij and gendarmerie excluded; reservists (400,000 ex-conscripts per MB) in trainedReserves. Population and territory: Iran within its 1980 borders; Iraqi-occupied parts of Khuzestan not removed. Logistics bounds come from the 1990 CIA World Factbook and are shifted down for 1980 by judgement (grade D where stated). No domestic production of major platforms in 1980 (production {}).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.78. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IRN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 13.62% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.62 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.57-0.69). Mid 1 - 0.136/0.62 = 0.78. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.57 = 0.69. High: s 0.69 = 0.8. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 62% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large wheat producer but net grain/feed importer; drought-prone.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 46,947,484 x share of males aged 15-19 7.106% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 667,224. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

iran-2026.notes: WARTIME snapshot: 2026 Iran war with the US and Israel since 28 Feb 2026 (Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei killed; Mojtaba Khamenei named successor 8 March), following the June 2025 Twelve-Day War; ceasefires of April and June 2026 collapsed (8 July). asOf 2025 economic data, order of battle adjusted for 2025-26 losses where sources state them (navy table updated for the war; launcher counts per war infobox). All counts uncertain: IISS figures as quoted are often old editions (2009 tank breakdown). Paramilitary Basij (IISS 40,000; 600,000 mobilisable) and Law Enforcement excluded from active; Axis of Resistance proxies (Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi PMF) excluded. Population: everything inside ne:IRN (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-15%). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D).

areaKm2.note: world_1960 Iraq polygon = ~441,200 km2 computed on the sphere (high). CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt): total area 434,920 km2 (low). Mid 438,000 (usual published figure ~438,317). population.note: OWID (UN WPP) Iraq 1990 = 17.58M; COW NMC v7 tpop 1990 = 18,078k; CIA World Factbook 1990 = 18.78M (July 1990, high). OWID 1989 = 17.36M (low). Mid ~17.9M.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): ACTIVE 1,000,000; army 955,000 incl. perhaps 480,000 recalled reserves; navy 5,000; air force 40,000 incl. 10,000 AD personnel. COW NMC v7 milper 1990 = 1,390,000 (annual figure that includes the post-invasion call-up, high); 1989 = 1,000,000. Gulf War infobox (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War): 1,000,000+ soldiers. Paramilitary People's Army excluded (see trainedReserves).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): RESERVES People's Army ~850,000 (paramilitary Ba'ath militia, high). The recalled reservists (~480,000) are already inside active. Mid discounts the People's Army for its poor training; demobilised Iran-Iraq War veterans are the other callable pool.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: navy 5,000 + air force 40,000 (MB 1990-91) + army armour, artillery (3,700 tubes and MRL), air defence (4,000 AA guns), engineers, logistics and staffs of 7 corps, ~475,000. = active 1,000,000 minus ~460,000 infantry.

mobilizationRatio.note: MB 1990-91 active 1,000,000 + People's Army 850,000 = 1.85M of ~17.9M = 10.3% actually under arms or in the militia in 1990; COW peak milper 1,390,000 (1990) = 7.8%. High allows deeper total-war call-up.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): 40 infantry divisions, 7 armoured/mechanised divisions, 6 Republican Guard divisions. Infantry ~8,000 per infantry division x 40 = 320,000, + mech infantry of the 7 armd/mech divisions (~3,000 each) and 3 RG infantry divisions (~10,000 each) = ~370,000-400,000. Reconstruction from division counts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: AK-47, RPG-7, Sagger and Milan ATGW, but most infantry walked or rode trucks; BMP only in mech units (MB 1990-91 eqpt list).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5 (conscripts, many recalled reservists). Evidence: LA Times 13 Aug 1990 (Broder and Jehl, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces): only a third of troops experienced; 21-24 month service.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): 20+ special forces/commando brigades (~2,500 each) plus the Republican Guard special forces brigade. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: standard Soviet-pattern light weapons, heliborne capability (489 helicopters).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: volunteer commando brigades used as the assault spearhead in the 1988 offensives (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): towed artillery some 3,000 (incl. 100 G-5, 200 GHN-45 155 mm), SP ~500 (2S1, 2S3, M-109, 85 AUF-1 GCT), MRL 200 (BM-21, ASTROS II, Ababeel) = 3,700. Gulf War infobox: 3,000 artillery systems (low). Mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: G-5 and GHN-45 155 mm out-ranged Coalition tube artillery; ASTROS MRL; but mostly Soviet towed guns and limited counter-battery radar.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: artillery was the most proficient Iraqi arm; massed fire plans and chemical shell delivery in the 1988 offensives (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): MBT some 5,500 (1,500 T-54/-55/M-77, 1,500 Chinese T-59/-69, 1,500 T-62, 1,000 T-72, 30 Chieftain, M-60, M-47) + 100 PT-76 light tanks. Gulf War infobox: 5,500 tanks. Low allows for unserviceable hulls.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: only 1,000 T-72 (export model, no composite-armour upgrade); 4,500 T-54/55/59/62 a generation behind the M1A1 / Challenger anchor of 1990.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscript crews; Republican Guard armour 0.65). Evidence: RG armoured divisions practised combined-arms offensives in 1988 (Fao, Tawakalna ala Allah).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): AIFV 1,500 BMP-1/-2; APC 6,000 (BTR-50/-60/-152, OT-62/-64, 1,500 MT-LB, 1,000 YW-531, M-113, Panhard M-3, EE-11). quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly wheeled and tracked APCs of 1950s-60s design; BMP-2 few.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mechanised divisions with eight years of war experience but conscript crews.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): fighter 17 sqn with some 40 Chinese J-7, 150 MiG-21, 25 MiG-25, 30 Mirage F-1EQ, 30 MiG-29 = 275. Low allows ~70-75% serviceability.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 30 MiG-29 and Mirage F-1 modern; 190 MiG-21/J-7 a generation behind; 2 Il-76 Adnan AEW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: few flying hours, rigid ground-controlled intercept; Iraqi Air Force rarely contested Iranian air superiority early in the war (Iran-Iraq War article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Mi-24 and HOT-armed Gazelle/Bo-105 era-typical.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: army aviation used extensively in 1980-88.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): frigates 5: 4 Hittin (Italian Lupo) and 1 Khaldoum training frigate; the MB notes the ships bought from Italy remain in the Mediterranean (Iraqi Armed Forces article: the Lupos and Assads were never delivered). Only Ibn Khaldoun was in Iraqi hands (mid); high counts the undelivered Lupos.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Ibn Khaldoun is a lightly armed training frigate.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 5,000-man navy, Basra closed since 1980.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Osa/Styx 1960s Soviet designs.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: small navy with little sea time.

count.note: Launchers. IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): SSM 50 FROG-7, 36 Scud-B, plus Sijil, Abbas and Husayn on the same and indigenous launchers; the MB essay notes at least six Al-Husayn launchers at H-2. High allows the indigenous fixed and mobile launchers; low allows unserviceable FROGs. Gulf War article: 88 Scuds fired at Israel and Saudi Arabia in seven weeks.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Al-Husayn (600 km) and Al-Abbas (900 km) were lengthened Scuds with reduced payload and accuracy (Gulf War article).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: ~190 Al-Husayn fired at Iranian cities in the 1988 War of the Cities; shoot-and-scoot drills that defeated Coalition Scud hunts in 1991.

count.note: Batteries. IISS Military Balance 1990-1991, Iraq entry (full-text transcription at samlib.ru; the edition states the Iraq entry reflects the position before the 2 Aug 1990 invasion): SAM 160 SA-2 (~27 batteries at 6 launchers), 140 SA-3 (~35 at 4), about 300 SA-6/-8/-9/-14 (~75 at 4), 100 Roland (~25 at 4) = ~160 SAM batteries; AD guns 4,000 (23-130 mm) at 6-12 guns per battery = ~350-650 AAA batteries. Conversion is the parent rubric (4-6 launchers per battery).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: French-built KARI computerised IADS linking Soviet and French SAMs; no SA-10.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 10,000 air-defence personnel in the air force; dense but uncoordinated AAA.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: LA Times 13 Aug 1990 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces: senior staff full of incompetents; Saddam purged and micromanaged commanders; but RG staff planned the 1988 Fao and Tawakalna offensives well (Iran-Iraq War article).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscript army with Shia and Kurdish rank and file, Ba'athist political officers; Republican Guard with strong identity; mass desertion and surrender in 1991.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: exhausted after eight years of war and ~1M men under arms, but buoyed by the 1988 victories; little popular enthusiasm for Kuwait.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: T-72, Scud derivatives, Exocet, laser-guided AS-30L, G-5 artillery, chemical munitions; most kit of 1960s-70s Soviet generation (MB 1990-91).

armor.note: Anchor: below 9 (composite armour). Evidence: 1,000 T-72 export models; 4,500 older steel-armoured tanks.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Osa missile boats only; modern Lupo/Assad ships held in Italy.

fortification.note: Anchor: 9 = hardened shelters. Evidence: Yugoslav-built hardened aircraft shelters and deep bunkers; berms and minefields perfected against Iran (Basra defences).

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 (motor transport) and 9 (containerised, airlift). Evidence: large heavy-equipment-transporter fleet, 19-30 Il-76 transports (MB; Factbook notes 30 Il-76 in Iraqi Airways used by the AF), 2,962 km rail.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 (company radio) and 9 (satellite comms, data links). Evidence: Soviet and Western radios, buried fibre and microwave C2 net; no military satellites.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: KARI radar network, 2 Il-76 Adnan AEW (MB); no satellite reconnaissance (satellite launch attempt failed, MB essay).

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: 30 MiG-29, Mirage F-1, Su-24, Su-25; bulk MiG-21/23 generation.

cyber.note: Anchor: cyber 9 = 1990 networks. Evidence: only military network is the French-built KARI air-defence C2 computers; no offensive network capability. Interpolated, grade D.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex 1989 = 11.0bn and 1990 = 8.61bn current US$; World Bank GDP 1989 = 65.8bn current US$ (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD; the 1990 value is distorted by the exchange rate) -> ~17% in 1989. SIPRI series via OWID stops in 1981 (10.8%). High covers estimates of 25%+ during 1988-90.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Iraq 1990 = 16.1% (low end of the share). CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14) labour force, Iraq: 33% agriculture (1987, high end). Mid 25%. Grade C because the two sources disagree; Iraq imported most of its grain, which does not lower this value. Share 25.0% (range 16.1-33.0%) -> 0.75 (0.67-0.839).

annualCohort.note: World Bank 1990 (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y, SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN): male pop 8,656,059 x 11.80% / 5 = ~204,300 males per year. CIA World Factbook 1990: 219,701 males reach military age (18) annually. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 404,000 for both sexes.

artillery.note: Educated guess: guns per year. Domestic 155 mm production (Al-Fao, Majnoon SP prototypes, GHN-45 licence) and Ababeel MRL; mostly imports.

armor.note: Educated guess: tank production. Iraq assembled small numbers of T-72 (Lion of Babylon) from Soviet and Polish kits from 1989; replacement relied on imports.

missiles.note: Educated guess: launchers per year. Indigenous Al-Husayn launchers (MB essay notes 5 more SSM types under development).

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: highways 25,479 km total; 8,290 km paved (low), 5,534 km improved earth (mid = paved + improved), 11,655 km unimproved earth (high = all).

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: railroads 2,962 km total (2,457 km standard gauge, 505 km metre gauge).

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: ports Umm Qasr, Khawr az Zubayr; Shatt al-Arab and Basra closed since September 1980.

merchantTonnage.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iraq entry: merchant marine 44 ships (1,000 GRT or over) totaling 947,721 GRT / 1,703,988 DWT (19 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Iraqi logistics sustained corps offensives 50-150 km deep in 1988 and the 2 Aug 1990 drive to the Saudi border (~150 km from Basra) on a large truck and HET fleet; deeper operations would outrun it.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: donkeys, horses, mules and camels in a mostly motorised economy; no military use.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Iraqi warheads. MB 1990-91 essay: Iraq unlikely to produce a nuclear weapon for several years. Chemical weapons (sarin, mustard) were held but are not warheads in this field.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities and border defences built against Iran, regime-controlled population; open desert and short depth toward Baghdad keep it at 1.2, low 1.1 for the Shia south and Kurdish north.

iraq-1990.notes: Snapshot date 2 August 1990 (invasion of Kuwait); force data from IISS Military Balance 1990-1991 (data as of before the invasion, read in the samlib.ru full-text transcription at http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1990.shtml), cross-checked with COW NMC v7 and the Gulf War infobox. Population and territory: Iraq within its 1990 borders, Kuwait excluded. Navy: the four Lupo frigates and six Assad corvettes bought from Italy never reached Iraq; counted only in the high bounds. Production rates and logistics range are educated guesses. Iraqi chemical weapons are not represented in any field. Coalition deployment (Desert Shield) came later and is not part of this snapshot.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.74. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IRQ/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 8.17% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.32 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.27-0.35). Mid 1 - 0.082/0.32 = 0.74. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.27 = 0.6. High: s 0.35 = 0.77. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 32% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net importer; Tigris-Euphrates water decline.

areaKm2.note: Pre-June-1967 armistice lines: official 20,770 km2 (incl. inland water). The world_1960 Israel polygon computes to ~31,100 km2 on the sphere (coarse outline), used as high.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1967 = 2,715k (mid). OWID/HYDE 2,538,658 (low); World Bank 1967 male+female = 2,745,000; high allows for the CBS mid-year figure incl. East Jerusalem after June. Pre-war lines only.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share 1967 = 58.2% (low). Israel CBS national definition (towns of 2,000+) was ~80% in the 1960s, used for high; mid between. Grade C.

activePersonnel.note: Standing force = conscripts + career regulars. CIA/DIA memo 26 May 1967: army average peacetime strength ~55,000; plus air force (~8,000) and navy (~3,000-4,000). COW NMC v7 milper 1967 = 75,000 (high). Mobilised reservists are counted in trainedReserves, not here.

trainedReserves.note: Reservists mobilised by 5 June 1967. CIA/DIA 26 May: 158,000 already mobilised, maximum 280,000 (army) -> up to ~225,000 reservists. Stone 2004 p. 217 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War: total strength incl. reservists 264,000 -> ~193,000 reservists. Reserve brigades formed most of the 1967 ground force.

supportPersonnel.note: Air force, navy, armour and artillery crews, signals, logistics and staff within the ~71,000 standing force. Reconstruction from the CIA army figure plus service strengths; grade C.

mobilizationRatio.note: Achieved: 264,000 under arms (Stone 2004 p. 217 via Six-Day War article) / ~2.7M population = 9.8%; 1973 reached ~12.5%. A total-war ceiling of ~15% is the high.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Standing (conscript/regular) infantry only: Golani, Givati remnants and Nahal line units, ~5-6 battalions-equivalent of 4,000-man brigades (CIA: brigades of ~4,000). Reserve infantry brigades (the bulk) arrive via trainedReserves. Reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: FN FAL and Uzi, but many units on mixed WWII-era kit and M3 half-tracks.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75 (professional standing army). Evidence: CIA 26 May 1967 credits high quality of training and operational proficiency.

count.note: Educated guess: paratroop and reconnaissance (Sayeret) conscript units; 55th Paratroop Brigade (reserve) not counted here. Grade C reconstruction.

israel-1967.notes: Snapshot date 5 June 1967 (Operation Focus). Territory and population: pre-war armistice lines, no occupied territories. Personnel convention: activePersonnel = conscripts + career regulars (~71,000); trainedReserves = reservists, already mobilised on 5 June (~190,000-225,000). The P roles hold only standing infantry; reserve infantry and armoured brigades (most of the IDF in battle) enter through trainedReserves. Key sources: CIA/DIA intelligence memorandum "Military Capabilities of Israel and the Arab States", 26 May 1967 (archive.org CIA reading room copy; table: Israel 55,000 prior to mobilisation, 280,000 at M+15, 1,123 tanks, 274 SP AT/assault guns, 256 jet fighters, 2 destroyers, 2 submarines); Six-Day War article infobox (Stone, Oren, Tucker, Pollack citations). IISS Military Balance 1967-68 could not be fetched (paywalled; archive.org copies access-restricted); its Israel entry was not used. Weakest values: half-track count, helicopter and air-defence battery counts (educated guesses).

israel-1973.notes: Snapshot date 6 October 1973 (Egyptian-Syrian surprise attack on Yom Kippur). Territory: hb:1960:Israel is the pre-1967 polygon; Sinai, Golan, West Bank and Gaza were occupied but have no separate basemap polygon (areaKm2 high counts them). Population excludes the Palestinians of the occupied territories. Personnel convention: activePersonnel = conscripts + career regulars (~115,000); trainedReserves = reservists mobilised from 6 Oct (~275,000). P roles hold standing infantry only. Key sources: Yom Kippur War infobox (1,700 tanks, 3,000 APCs, 945 guns, 440 aircraft; Rabinovich, Sunday Times Insight), Israeli Air Force and Battle of Baltim articles, COW NMC v7, SIPRI via OWID, Maddison 2023. IISS Military Balance 1973-74 and Dupuy, Elusive Victory could not be fetched; activePersonnel mid relies on recalled IISS order of magnitude (grade C). US airlift (Operation Nickel Grass, from 14 Oct) replaced losses and is not in the snapshot.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.97. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ISR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 0.76% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.23 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.20-0.26). Mid 1 - 0.008/0.23 = 0.97. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.20 = 0.94. High: s 0.26 = 0.97. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 23% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food importer (grain, feed) but exports fruit/vegetables; small surplus at most.

isr.note: Anchor: 7 (aerial recon). Evidence: no operational radar in 1940; aerial and naval reconnaissance only

air.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: 70% of operational fighters biplanes; SM.79 good; engines weak

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8 (Italy, % of GDP at current prices): 8% (1939), 12% (1940), 23% (1941).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry ~30% of Italian output in the late 1930s; agriculture still ~40% of employment. 1940 steel output 2.1Mt vs Britain's 13Mt (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II). (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). Cited page: "Agriculture still employed 48% of the working population in 1936 (56% in 1921)" (a = 0.48). No calorie self-sufficiency figure could be fetched, so s = 1 is assumed; this overstates the value somewhat (wheat near self-sufficient after the battle for grain, fats and feed imported). Mid 1 - 0.48 = 0.52. High a 0.45; low allows a 0.50 and s ~0.95. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.0/0.03/0.08 (read as a trade balance); recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 3(a): Italy census 21 April 1936, males 20-24 = 1,979k / 5 = ~396k per year.

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6 (Zamagni): 3.0k tanks and SPG in the 38 months June 1940-Aug 1943 (~950/yr); 1940 output only ~250 AFVs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_fighter.note: Harrison Table 1-6: Italian combat aircraft 3.3k (1940), 3.5k (1941), 2.8k (1942), 2.0k (1943, 8 months); fighters ~65% (9,157 of 13,402 Italian aircraft per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_production_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_strike.note: Harrison Table 1-6 combat aircraft minus fighters.

artillery.note: Harrison Table 1-6: 10k guns in the 38 months of war (~3,200/yr).

ships_major.note: 3 battleships and 3 cruisers completed 1940-43 (cited page; column mapping flagged as uncertain there), ~1.5-2 per year.

ships_minor.note: Harrison Table 1-6 (Zamagni): 'major naval vessels' 12 (1940, 6 months), 41 (1941), 86 (1942), 148 (1943, 8 months), mostly small escorts and MAS; destroyers and torpedo boats ~20/yr (educated).

submarines.note: Educated split of Harrison's naval series: ~30 submarines completed 1940-43.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: national (ANAS ~20,000 km), provincial and municipal engineered roads; many southern and mountain roads unsurfaced. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II)

railKm.note: Educated guess: state railways (FS) ~16,500-17,000 km plus ~5,000-6,000 km of concession lines; major lines electrified at 3 kV DC in 1922-39. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II)

majorPorts.note: Genoa, La Spezia, Naples, Taranto, Brindisi, Bari, Venice, Trieste, Palermo, Messina, Cagliari, Livorno.

merchantTonnage.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 113 (Lloyd's Register, June 1938): Italy 3,290k gross tons, x1.5 to deadweight (mid). ~27% of Italian merchant ships were caught in Allied ports and impounded on 10 June 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II), so low = 73% x 3.4M GRT x 1.3.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 6 (North Africa): Axis forces could not be sustained much beyond ~300 miles from Tripoli/Benghazi; the Italian army was short of trucks, so mid 200 km. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Italy's horse stock 942,000 in 1930 (Rich and Wilson p. 653, table 59, via the cited page); with mules and donkeys (~1.2M, educated) ~2.2M equids. The army was largely mule- and horse-drawn.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before July 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar mountainous terrain (Alps, Apennines), Vallo Alpino fortifications and fortified ports; population support lukewarm, no deep strategic depth.

italy-1940.notes: Snapshot date 10 June 1940 (declaration of war on France and Britain). METROPOLITAN Italy: population, GDP, area and cohort exclude Libya, Italian East Africa, the Dodecanese and Albania (in personal union since April 1939). Forces COUNT Italian national troops wherever stationed (Libya ~200,000 incl. Libyan divisions, East Africa ~256,000 incl. ~200,000 native ascari, both per the cited Italian military history page) but EXCLUDE colonial native units. Colonial bases are listed in basesAbroad. Weakest values: artillery and AA counts (educated), L3 tankette count, railKm and roadKm (no fetched source). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries); only 2 of 6 battleships were battle-ready on 10 June. Merchant tonnage converted to deadweight at x1.5.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.2 -> 0.94. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ITA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 3.35% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.56 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.54-0.57). Mid 1 - 0.033/0.56 = 0.94. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.54 = 0.91. High: s 0.57 = 0.94. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 56% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net importer of grain and feed, exporter of wine, olive oil, processed food.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 28,814,684 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.170% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 297,928. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, Japan (proper) agriculture share of employment 1930 = 50.6%, 1940 = 46.7%. The snapshot includes Korea and Taiwan (~30M of 102.9M), which were more agrarian; no fetched occupational figure, ~0.7 assumed for them, giving a ~0.54 for the empire. No calorie self-sufficiency figure for 1941 could be fetched, so s = 1 is assumed: within the empire colonial rice fed Japan proper, but soybeans and some wheat came from Manchukuo and abroad, so the value is somewhat overstated. Mid 1 - 0.54 = 0.46. High = Japan proper alone (1 - 0.467 = 0.53); low allows colonial a ~0.8 and s < 1. Grade D: colonial share assumed. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.0/0.03/0.08 (read as a trade balance); recomputed with the formula.

japan-1941.notes: Snapshot date 7-8 December 1941 (Pearl Harbor, Malaya, Philippines). COUNTED as integral parts: Japan proper, Korea (Chosen), Taiwan (Formosa) and Karafuto (population ~102.9M, area 675,000 km2). NOT counted: Manchukuo (separate puppet state, Kwantung Army forces stationed there ARE counted as Japanese forces), the Kwantung lease, the South Seas Mandate, occupied China, French Indochina. includes is empty because Korea and Taiwan had no separate state in 1941. The border unions the world_1945 Japan, Korea and Taiwan polygons (~620,000 km2): Manchukuo is excluded, Karafuto is missing. (audit 2026-10-30) Forces are the whole armed forces (~27 divisions in China, 13 in Manchuria at the start of the war per Jowett). Weakest values: artillery, AA, tank inventory, army aircraft split, roads and draft animals. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Merchant tonnage converted to deadweight at x1.5. audit 2026-10-30: border changed to the world_1945 Japan, Korea and Taiwan polygons, which exclude Manchukuo (the world_1938 Empire of Japan feature included it); Karafuto is missing from them.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/JPN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 2.81% (2025); s = 0.38 (FY2024 calorie basis, MAFF via https://english.adnkronos.com/2025/10/10/fy-2024-japan-food-self-sufficiency-rate-remains-at-38-pct/). High: s 0.64 (production-value basis, same source) = 0.96, taken as 0.95 since value basis overstates calories. Import dependence: ~62% of calories imported. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.93, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

population.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes 1,500,000 for Classical Angkor in 1100 (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/41, low) but says the empire total is unclear; Greater Angkor alone held 700,000-900,000 in the 13th century (Klassen et al., Khmer Empire page). HYDE 1200: Cambodia 1.2M, Thailand 1.4M, Laos 0.3M, Vietnam 1.3M (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); the empire held Cambodia, much of Thailand and southern Laos, and occupied Champa (1190-1220).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Greater Angkor 700,000-1,000,000 (Klassen et al.; Seshat 750,000-1,000,000) against an empire of 1.5-4M, but at low density sprawled over 1,000+ km2 (Angkor page).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing force only: royal guard, palace and provincial retainers, royal elephants and war galleys; corvee levies are in trainedReserves. No count survives. Zhou Daguan (1296) describes soldiers fighting barefoot with lance and shield; an oral tradition told to Mouhot of 5-6 million soldiers is legend (Khmer Empire page). The Bayon reliefs show large armies on the Champa campaigns.

khmer-empire-1200.notes: Snapshot 1200 under Jayavarman VII, with Champa under Khmer occupation (1190-1220). No army count survives from any source; every force number is an educated guess, the weakest block in the file. Zhou Daguan (1296) is a century later. Population convention: Khmer-ruled lands including the Khorat plateau and central Thailand; occupied Champa partly counted in the high. Elephants and galleys are platforms; mahouts and rowers are supportPersonnel. Personnel: active = royal guard, retainers, mercenaries, royal elephants and galleys; trainedReserves = corvee levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.

areaKm2.note: Wikipedia infobox gives 1,330,000 km2 (c. 1000). The world_1000 polygon measures 1.20 million km2. Low allows for the sparse forest north-east being only nominally ruled.

population.note: Infobox: 5.4 million in 1000 (Urlanis, Rost naseleniya v Evrope). HYDE/OWID 1000-1100 series for Ukraine (0.9-1.4M), Belarus (0.2-0.3M) and European Russia (~60% of 2.5-3.8M) sum to ~3-4M (low). Mid 5.5M with modest growth to 1050.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Kiev ~36,000-50,000 by 1200 and Novgorod 10,000-15,000 in 1000 (Martin 2004, via the Kievan Rus' article); many small gorods.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element: the druzhinas of Yaroslav and his sons in the appanages plus hired Varangians. Ibrahim ibn Yaqub gave Mieszko I of Poland a paid druzhina of 3,000 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druzhina), a comparable neighbour. audit 2026-10-30: date basis: a year without a general muster, so only the household element is active and campaign levies are trainedReserves (france-1415, dated to the Agincourt campaign, counts its assembled army instead).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Town militias (voi) of Kiev, Novgorod, Chernigov and other gorods, and allied Torks and Pecheneg remnants. Franklin and Shepard (The Emergence of Rus 750-1200) give no total.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Boat crews and household officials.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Free townsmen and some peasants could be called for defence.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Princely druzhina: mail, conical helm, lance, sword.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: professional retainers.

count.note: Educated guess. Varangian mercenaries and town core troops on pay.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Scandinavian kit, axes, mail.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75.

count.note: Educated guess. Archers in princely service.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: composite and self bows.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

count.note: Educated guess. Steppe auxiliaries (Torks) and mounted scouts.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: steppe riders.

count.note: Educated guess. Monoxyla river boats (each ~40 men) used for the 1043 sea raid on Constantinople, which ended in disaster.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: dugout-based boats vs Byzantine galleys and Greek fire.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Yaroslav crushed the Pechenegs at Kiev (1036) but lost the 1043 naval expedition.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: appanage system and princely rivalry; druzhinas loyal to their own prince.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: confident state at its height under Yaroslav.

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: sword, lance, composite bow, axe; no crossbow in quantity.

armor.note: Anchor 3 (mail).

ships.note: Anchor 2: oared river boats (monoxyla) able to reach the Black Sea.

fortification.note: Anchor 2-3: timber walls on earth ramparts, the Serpent's Wall frontier ramparts, stone Golden Gate of Kiev (1037).

logistics.note: Anchor 2-3: river transport, winter sledges, portages.

communications.note: Anchor 2: couriers along the rivers.

isr.note: Anchor 2-3: steppe watch posts on the southern frontier.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) Poland 1400 = 956, Turkey 1000 = 768 (2011 int$); river trade wealth concentrated in towns.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Tribute (poliudie) supported the druzhina.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Town crafts, iron working.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Black-earth south vs poor forest north.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. No engineered roads; rivers in summer, frozen rivers and sledges in winter.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Kiev, Novgorod, Staraya Ladoga, Smolensk and Tmutarakan.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River boats of the Varangians-to-Greeks route.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and oxen, ~0.1 per inhabitant.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: forest and marsh depth and harsh winter against steppe and southern invaders; less against northern neighbours, so mid 1.25.

kievan-rus-1050.notes: Snapshot = 1050, near the end of Yaroslav the Wise's reign (died 1054) and before the appanage strife. Army sizes are educated guesses: no modern total for Rus' forces exists in the works consulted, and Primary Chronicle numbers are not used. Population convention: all lands under Rurikid princes, including Novgorod and Tmutarakan; Polotsk counted although its prince was semi-independent. Per the feudal-host convention activePersonnel is the druzhinas only and the town militias are trainedReserves.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.84. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/KWT/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.89% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.11 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.11-0.12). Mid 1 - 0.019/0.11 = 0.84. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.11 = 0.73. High: s 0.12 = 0.84. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 11% of domestic calorie supply. a includes expatriate farm labour. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports nearly all food.

lesotho-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 2.0-2.5 million km2 for 1000-1100 (mid 2.25M). The infobox of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty gives 2.6 million km2 (947 est., Taagepera 1997 and Turchin et al. 2006; high). The world_1000 Liao polygon measures only 0.79 million km2 (low): it leaves out the Mongolian steppe the Liao controlled.

population.note: Seshat codes 3.8 million for the Liao (907-1125). The Liao dynasty article gives a peak of "750,000 Khitans and two to three million ethnic Han Chinese" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty), 2.75-3.75 million (low). High adds about 20% for Bohai, Xi and tribal peoples outside both counts, a judgement.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Five capitals and the walled prefectural towns of the Han south; the Khitan majority of the north lived in camps.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. One ordo of 15,000 households could field up to 6,000 horsemen; Empress Dowager Xiao's own ordo 10,000 cavalry; by the end of the dynasty (1125) all the imperial ordos together held 81,000 Khitan and 124,000 Bohai and Chinese households able to field 101,000 horsemen (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty). In 1004 fewer ordos existed than in 1125, so the ordo cavalry is guessed at 40,000-70,000, plus tribal frontier armies and Han garrisons of the Southern Capital circuit. Chronicle figures (300,000 troops in 947, Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288; 400,000 for the 1010 Goryeo campaign, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty) are not used as counts.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Tribal levies and Han Chinese militia; the high end is the 400,000 claimed for the 1010 Goryeo campaign.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Han siege engineers, herd guards for remounts, courier and staff personnel.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Every Khitan tribesman served as a mounted warrior, while the Han and Bohai farmers were drafted only as militia; below the 0.2 of a pure steppe confederation (xiongnu--200).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured Khitan cavalry, organised in groups of 500 to 700 men (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: armoured riders on armoured horses

training.note: Rubric 0.75: ordo guards bound to the emperor

count.note: Educated guess. Horse archers of the ordos and the tribes, each man with remounts.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: composite bows, several horses per man

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: lifelong riders and hunters

count.note: Educated guess. Han Chinese and Bohai infantry garrisons in the south.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: militia-based

count.note: Educated guess. Han Chinese crossbowmen.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5

training.note: Rubric 0.5

count.note: Educated guess. Traction trebuchets with Han engineers for siege work on the Song frontier.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75

training.note: Rubric 0.5

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: the 1004 campaign under Shengzong and the Empress Dowager reached the Yellow River about 160 km from the Song capital and forced the Treaty of Chanyuan (Song recognition as peers and 200,000 bolts of silk and 100,000 taels of silver a year), though the main general Xiao Talin was killed by a Song crossbow (Wright 2008 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanyuan_Treaty)

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: each emperor's ordo guard was his own household ("heart and belly guard", Atwood 2004 via Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288); Han and Bohai units less bound

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: an offensive war against the Song a decade after the 992 invasion of Goryeo (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty); a dynasty near its height

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: composite bows, lances, crossbows, traction trebuchets.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4 (barding at 4): armoured heavy cavalry and horses.

ships.note: Anchor 1-2: river craft only; no navy.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: walled capitals and prefectural towns built on Chinese models.

logistics.note: Anchor 3: self-supplied cavalry with remounts and foraging; "smashing the pasture and grain" in 947 (Seshat https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/288).

communications.note: Anchor 3-4: mounted courier relays.

isr.note: Anchor 3-4: steppe scouting screens.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (via OWID, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): China 1000 = 1,225 (2011 int$), the high. The Liao economy was pastoral in the north and frontier farming in the south, placed below the Song level.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A militarised dual state; much of the cost fell on tribesmen who armed and horsed themselves.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron working, salt, textiles and ceramics in the Han south.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Millet and wheat farming in the south and Liaodong, pastoral herds in the north.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads linking the five capitals and the passes of the Yan mountains.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Bohai Gulf coast; no seagoing fleet recorded.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Coastal and river craft; trade with the Song went overland through border markets.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry with remounts living off pasture and plunder; less than a pure steppe army because the Han infantry and siege train move slowly.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, oxen, camels; the 1082-83 snowfall killed 60-70% of tribal livestock and a horse shortage was noted in 1043 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liao_dynasty).

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: the Yan mountain passes and walled Southern Capital, steppe depth and a harsh continental winter.

liao-1004.notes: Snapshot = autumn 1004, the Chanyuan campaign under Shengzong and the Empress Dowager Xiao Yanyan, ended by the Treaty of Chanyuan in January 1005. Population and area are Seshat codings. The army is the weakest set of values: the only structured figures (ordo households and horsemen) describe the dynasty at its end in 1125, and chronicle totals of 300,000-400,000 are not used. Border: world_1000 Liao is the file at or before the year; the polygon covers Manchuria, the Liao River and the Sixteen Prefectures but not the Mongolian steppe, so areaKm2 is researched. Population convention: everything the dynasty ruled, Khitan and Han.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 84,293,786,108 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 7,458,555 = 11,302 2011 int$. Range +/-15%. Oil output swings with blockades. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 105,301,419,248 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 84,293,786,108 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Oil output swings with blockades. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 3.57% of GDP in 2023, 2.80% 2022. Two parallel administrations; foreign-funded equipment not counted (high).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 73.2% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings. Oil and gas dominate.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.02 -> 0.53. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/LBY/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 10.00% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.21 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.19-0.23). Mid 1 - 0.100/0.21 = 0.53. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.19 = 0.3. High: s 0.23 = 0.57. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 21% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports ~75% of food.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 3,791,703 x share of males aged 15-19 9.311% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 70,613. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2010: 37,000 km in the road network list; World Bank IS.ROD.TOTL.KM gave 83,200 km (2000) on a broader definition (high). Mid is between them.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook lists no railways; Libyan rail projects stalled in 2011.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 14 ports, 0 large, 2 medium; key ports Tripoli, Benghazi, Misrata, Tobruk, Marsa el Brega.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Coastal road logistics, long desert lines to the Fezzan.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels, donkeys; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Libya is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table. Weapons programme abandoned in 2003.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: vast desert and urban militias; 1.3 high for the Sahara depth.

libya-2026.notes: DIVIDED-STATE snapshot: Libya has two rival armed forces since 2014: the UN-recognised Government of National Unity in Tripoli with its Libyan Armed Forces and allied militias (~32,000 regulars, Turkish-backed), and Khalifa Haftar's Libyan Arab Armed Forces / LNA in the east and south (~90,000, backed by Russia's Africa Corps, the UAE and Egypt), per the Military of Libya article. Forces here are the SUM of both sides (one ne:LBY polygon) and so overstate what either government can use against an outsider; cohesion and command are rated accordingly. Equipment counts are educated guesses (grade D) except the IISS 2020 tank and combat-aircraft totals. Turkish, Russian and other foreign forces are not counted. asOf 2025 economic data.

areaKm2.note: Educated guess. Analogue: the modern Greek region of Macedonia (~34,000 km2) plus Upper Macedonia/Paeonia; high adds directly ruled parts of Thrace. Seshat (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/506) codes only 10,000 km2 for 359 BCE, the core before Philip II's expansion.

population.note: Seshat codes the Macedonian polity at 1,000,000 for 359-336 BCE (single value; range is ours). Macedon proper (Lower and Upper Macedonia, Chalcidice, east to the Nestos) only: Thessaly, Thrace and the League of Corinth members are not counted, although their contingents are in `forces`.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: a mostly rural kingdom; Pella, Aigai, Pydna, Amphipolis were the main towns (Seshat largest settlement 20,000-80,000 for 330-312).

activePersonnel.note: Field and home armies (50,600) + League fleet crews and engineers (34,000) + margin. About half are non-Macedonians: League allies (7,000 infantry, 600 cavalry, the fleet), Greek mercenaries (5,000) and Balkan contingents (7,000+).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Macedonians trained under Philip but not under arms; reinforcements of a few thousand were sent to Asia in 333.

supportPersonnel.note: League fleet 160 triremes x ~200 crew = 32,000 (largely allied Greeks) + ~2,000 engineers, surveyors (bematists), staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy with the Greek total-war call-up of 90% of the year classes 20-49/55 in 480 (Hansen 2006, https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 10), slightly lower for a less urbanised kingdom.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Line = Macedonian phalanx and hypaspists (12,000) + League hoplites (7,000) + mercenary hoplites (5,000) + Antipater's 12,000. audit 2026-10-30: grade B -> C: rests on an ancient chronicler's figure (SOURCES.md: at most C), accepted by modern historians. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

training.note: Allied crews of uncertain loyalty.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 1.0 row (best-in-era command): Alexander, with Parmenion and Philip's trained officer corps; mid 0.9 at the start of the campaign.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: motivated, recent victories (Chaeronea 338, Balkan campaign and Thebes 335).

weapons.note: Anchor 3 exactly (300 BCE: iron weapons, torsion artillery, sarissa).

armor.note: Anchor 3: bronze/iron and linen cuirasses.

ships.note: Anchor 3: triremes; no larger polyremes in the League fleet.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: siege towers and torsion artillery (Philip at Perinthus 340, Diades' engineers).

logistics.note: Anchor 3: Engels (isbn:0520042727) shows minimal baggage, soldiers carrying their own rations and pack horses instead of wagons, and pre-arranged depots.

communications.note: Mounted couriers; no permanent relay system until the Persian one was taken over.

isr.note: Year anchor 3: prodromoi scouts, bematists surveying routes.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Greece year 1 CE = 1,275 (2011 int$). Macedon was less urbanised than southern Greece but rich in timber, horses and Pangaion gold.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: a permanent army on Philip's model; Alexander crossed to Asia in debt (Arrian 7.9.6 / Plutarch, ancient).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: mining (Pangaion), timber and shipbuilding, crafts.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: fertile plains of Emathia and Thessaly; self-sufficient in grain.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: some military roads built under Philip II; no engineered network.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Pydna, Methone, Amphipolis, Therme.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: timber and grain coasting trade; the League's merchant shipping (Athens) is not counted.

supplyRangeKm.note: Engels (ch. 1-2): the army carried its own provisions on soldiers and pack animals and could operate only a limited number of days from water and a supply source; mid assumes ~1 week of marching between depots or the fleet. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: ~0.06-0.1 horses, mules and oxen per inhabitant x population (horse-rich kingdom).

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar mountain terrain and local supply; few fortified cities.

macedon--334.notes: Snapshot = spring 334 BCE, Alexander crossing the Hellespont. Border "none": historical-basemaps has no Macedon polygon near this date. world_bc400 is not available, world_bc323 shows only the "Empire of Alexander" (after the conquests), and world_bc500 lumps Macedon into the shared "Greek city-states" polygon (which also includes southern Greece, Magna Graecia and Massalia). Population is Macedon proper only; League of Corinth allies, Thessalians, mercenaries and Balkan troops are in `forces` but their homelands are not counted (includes = []). Army figures are Diodorus' breakdown as accepted by modern historians; Arrian gives "not much more than 30,000 infantry and over 5,000 cavalry". The siege train (torsion artillery) is not counted: its size at the start is undocumented.

madagascar-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: The world_bc323 Magadha polygon measures 1.276 million km2 (the pipeline area function). It runs from the eastern Punjab to Bengal and Odisha, the "Punjab to Odisha" extent Bronkhorst (2011) gives on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire. Low drops the uncertain margins (Kalinga, the Vindhyan forest belt), a judgement; high rounds up. For scale, Taagepera (1979) gives Magadha 0.5 million km2 in 510 BCE, before the Nanda expansion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires).

population.note: Dyson (2018) via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire: South Asia held 15-30 million in the Mauryan period. The Nanda share (Ganges plain, Bengal, Odisha, eastern Malwa) is taken as 40-60%, a judgement from the plain being the densest farmland of the subcontinent: 0.4 x 15M = 6M (low), 0.45 x 22.5M = 10M (mid), 0.6 x 30M = 18M (high). No modern estimate for the Nanda realm itself was found; the page gives none. The superseded phase-3 formula gave 9.6-24.7M for the same polygon.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pataliputra, Rajagriha, Varanasi, Kaushambi, Shravasti and Champa (the second urbanisation of the Ganges valley); overwhelmingly rural. The Maurya snapshot uses 0.07.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Sum of the force guesses plus crews. Curtius' report to Alexander: 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 2,000 four-horse chariots and 3,000 elephants (Habib and Jha 2004, Singh 2008, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire); Diodorus 4,000 elephants (Raychaudhuri 1988, same page); Plutarch's 80,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots and 6,000 elephants are called inflated there. Worthington (2014, same page) suggests Indian informants exaggerated to deter the Macedonians, so the Curtius totals with crews are the high bound, not the mid; mid ~1.25% of the 10M population, near the 1% of the Maurya snapshot.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Guild (sreni), allied and forest-tribe levies reachable within a month, as for the Maurya snapshot.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts and crews for ~2,000 elephants (2 each), drivers and fighters of ~1,000 chariots, commissariat and river transport.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Salaried standing army plus levies, as in the Maurya snapshot two generations later; a few percent of an agrarian population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Spear and shield infantry of the standing army; Curtius gives 200,000 infantry in all (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), shared here among line, archers and light troops at the high end.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: iron spears and swords, little body armour, as Greek writers describe Indian infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: a paid royal army existed (the dynasty is called militaristic on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), but no drill tradition is recorded

count.note: Educated guess. Archers with the long bamboo bow described by Megasthenes and Arrian (as in the Maurya snapshot); share of the Curtius infantry total.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: powerful but slow long bow

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5

count.note: Educated guess. Javelin men and forest-tribe skirmishers in pay.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light weapons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5

count.note: Educated guess. Horsemen; Curtius 20,000 (high). Indian cavalry was light and secondary to elephants.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: small horses, no stirrups

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Curtius 2,000 four-horse chariots (high, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire); chariots were declining in Indian warfare.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: heavy four-horse chariots, a generation behind

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Curtius 3,000, Diodorus 4,000 (high), both on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire; the largest elephant corps of the age, later inherited by the Mauryas.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: the elephant corps that made Alexander's army refuse to cross the Beas

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal elephant establishment

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: no Nanda battle record survives; the dynasty fell to Chandragupta and Chanakya within about four years (c. 322 BCE), the Milinda Panha recalling a violent war against the general Bhaddasala (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: an unpopular dynasty accused of greed and oppressive taxation in the Sri Lankan tradition (Habib and Jha 2004 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire), and a mix of standing troops and levies

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5 (average). Evidence: no war in progress on home soil; Porus described the king as of "worthless character" (Diodorus, same page)

weapons.note: Anchor 3 (300 BCE iron weapons) minus. Evidence: iron swords and spears, the long bow; no torsion artillery attested.

armor.note: Anchor between 2 (bronze scale) and 3. Evidence: Greek sources describe lightly armoured Indian troops.

ships.note: Anchor between 2 and 3. Evidence: river craft on the Ganges and coastal boats from Tamralipti.

fortification.note: Anchor 3 minus. Evidence: the cyclopean wall of Rajagriha and the timber palisade of Pataliputra (64 gates and 570 towers by the Maurya period, Megasthenes via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire).

logistics.note: Anchor 3 minus. Evidence: the Uttarapatha trunk road and river transport; Jayaswal reads the Hathigumpha inscription as crediting a Nandaraja with a canal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire).

communications.note: Anchor between 2 (couriers) and 3. Evidence: royal couriers; no relay system recorded before the Mauryas.

isr.note: Anchor between 2 and 3. Evidence: scouts and spies; the Arthashastra spy system is Mauryan.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue as in maurya--250: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no India value before 1600; its year-1 values are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, Belgium/France 956 (2011 int$). Ganges Magadha placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A large standing army and elephant corps paid from land revenue; the tradition of a vast Nanda treasury (80 koti in the Mahavamsa, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire) suggests heavy taxation. No budget survives.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron working, punch-marked silver coinage, crafts in a mostly agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Fertile Ganges plain with rice cultivation; as the Maurya snapshot.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. The Uttarapatha along the Ganges and the routes to Avanti; no engineered network.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Tamralipti on the Bay of Bengal and the river ports of the Ganges.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River and coastal craft; no figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ox-cart and elephant trains inside the river and road network, a little below the Maurya snapshot.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, buffalo and some horses; about 0.25 per inhabitant, the Maurya snapshot ratio.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 (familiar terrain, local supply) to 1.2 (fortified Pataliputra and Rajagriha); the monsoon and river crossings hamper invaders.

magadha--326.notes: Snapshot = summer 326 BCE, the last Nanda king (Dhana Nanda, the Agrammes or Xandrames of the Greeks) when Alexander's army refused to cross the Beas; Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the dynasty c. 322 BCE. Every army figure is an ancient report (Curtius, Diodorus, Plutarch) of what Indian informants told the Macedonians; they only bound the high side. Population is the weakest number: Dyson's range for all of South Asia times a judged share. Border: world_bc323 Magadha is the file at the snapshot date. Population convention: everything inside the polygon; Porus and the Punjab kingdoms are excluded. Elephants and chariots are platforms; mahouts and crews are in supportPersonnel. Personnel: active = standing royal troops with the elephants and chariots; trainedReserves = guild, allied and forest-tribe levies.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess for s. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MYS/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 9.18% (2025, includes plantation workers). s = 0.6 educated guess: rice SSR 52.9% (2024, https://www.thevibes.com/articles/news/119453/domestic-rice-production-declines-amid-multiple-challenges-says-agriculture-minister), 23 commodities above 100% SSR in 2025 (https://www.freshplaza.com/asia/article/9878260/malaysia-remains-reliant-on-imports-despite-higher-food-self-sufficiency/), wheat, sugar, beef and dairy imported; palm-oil exports not counted. Mid 1 - 0.0918/0.6 = 0.85. Low: a x 1.3, s 0.5 = 0.76. High: s 0.75 = 0.88. Import dependence: net food importer. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.85, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MLI/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 63.01% (2025). s = 1 assumed: no self-sufficiency figure is fetched for auto-base states, which overstates the value for a net food importer. Mid 1 - 0.630/1 = 0.37. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count) = 0.24. High: kept at mid (no s range).
