mali-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1.7-1.9 million km2 for 1230-1410; Wikipedia gives 1.3 million (1350) and 1.1 million (1380) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali_Empire, low). The world_1300 polygon measures 1.75 million km2.

population.note: Seshat codes 4-5 million for 1230-1410. HYDE/OWID 1300 series for Mali, Senegal, Guinea, Mauritania and parts of Niger and Burkina Faso sum to ~3 million (low). Popular claims of 40-50 million are rejected.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Largest settlement 12,000-17,000 (Seshat); Timbuktu, Djenne, Gao and Walata trade towns.

activePersonnel.note: Standing cavalry of "around 10,000 horsemen by the reign of Mansa Musa" (via the article, drawing on al-Umari) plus the royal slave guard and household. Al-Umari (c. 1337) is a contemporary Arabic account from informants, so grade C.

trainedReserves.note: Provincial and vassal levies: al-Umari's army of ~100,000 (high; the article: "capable of 100,000 regular army", core "may have reached 90,000"). Levtzion (Ancient Ghana and Mali) relays these figures; mid halves them as a chronicler-derived number.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Somono and Bozo boat crews on the Niger, smiths, household officials.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Levy of free men of the Mande clans and vassal states.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Mailed horsemen (farari nobility) on imported North African horses, part of the ~10,000 standing cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: mail and lance on scarce large horses.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: noble warriors.

count.note: Educated guess. Lighter horsemen with javelins and bows, rest of the standing cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75.

count.note: Educated guess. Archers (often with poisoned arrows), the core of Mande infantry.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: self bows, no armour.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

count.note: Educated guess. Spearmen of the royal guard.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

count.note: Educated guess. War canoes on the Niger crewed by Somono and Bozo boatmen.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: dugout canoes.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: Saghmandia took Gao (c. 1325); a functioning provincial system under Musa.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: clan-based levies and tributary vassals.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: expanding empire at its height.

weapons.note: Anchor 3: iron spears, swords, bows and javelins; no crossbow or trebuchet.

armor.note: Anchor 2-3: quilted cotton, leather, some imported mail for the elite.

ships.note: Anchor 1: river canoes.

fortification.note: Anchor 1-2: mudbrick (banco) town walls and palisades (tata).

logistics.note: Anchor 1-2: porters, donkeys, river canoes; tsetse limits horses in the south.

communications.note: Anchor 2: royal messengers.

isr.note: Anchor 2: scouts.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. No Maddison estimate for West Africa before 1950. Subsistence agriculture near the bare-bones line (~600 2011 int$), lifted by the trans-Saharan gold trade; Musa's 1324 hajj gold flooded Cairo.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Tribute and gold revenues paid for the cavalry and horse imports.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Gold mining, iron smithing, cotton weaving.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Niger floodplain rice and millet; Inner Delta surplus fed Timbuktu.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. No engineered roads; caravan tracks and the Niger.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. River ports: Kabara (Timbuktu), Djenne, Gao, Niani on the Sankarani.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River canoes; trans-Saharan trade went by camel.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Foot and canoe armies in the Sahel; seasonal limits in the rains.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys, camels in the north, few horses (imported).

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: Sahel distances, seasonal floods and disease the Saharan or northern invader is not adapted to.

mali-empire-1330.notes: Snapshot = c. 1330, Mansa Musa (r. c. 1312-1337) after his hajj and the annexation of Gao and Timbuktu. All army numbers trace to al-Umari and Ibn Khaldun via Levtzion and the Military history of the Mali Empire article; they are informants' reports, not counts, so grade C at best. Population convention: Mali's directly governed provinces and vassal Gao and Timbuktu; Takrur and Saharan Berber tributaries excluded. The capital site (Niani) is disputed.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 2.1 million km2 for 1260-1348 (high, includes desert margins). No 1260 polygon exists: world_1200 still shows the Ayyubids, so the later world_1279 Mamluke Sultanate polygon is used; it measures 1.24 million km2 (mid). Low reflects that northern Syria was only won after Ain Jalut (September 1260).

population.note: Seshat codes 5-6 million for 1260-1348 and notes ~6-7 million at the 14th-century peak. HYDE/OWID Egypt 1200-1300 = 4.0-4.7 million plus Syria-Palestine ~1.5-2 million.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Cairo 200,000-500,000 (Seshat), Alexandria, Damascus, Aleppo.

activePersonnel.note: Mamluk army at Ain Jalut 15,000-20,000 (Nicolle 1990 p. 116; Waterson 2007 p. 75), including Ayyubid Syrian refugees and Khwarazmians. Baybars later expanded the army from 10,000 cavalry to 40,000 (Asbridge 2010, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamluk_Sultanate), so ~10,000 regular cavalry is the low.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Bedouin tribes, Turkmen and Kurdish auxiliaries and the troops of Syrian Ayyubid princes who submitted after Ain Jalut.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Naffatun, armourers, siege engineers and the few galley crews.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Military service was the preserve of the imported mamluk caste and halqa; the Egyptian peasantry was not levied.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

mamluk-sultanate-1260.notes: Snapshot = September 1260, the Ain Jalut campaign, Qutuz sultan (killed by Baybars in October). The mamluks and halqa were salaried standing professionals paid through iqta, so they are activePersonnel; Bedouin and Syrian allies are reserves. Amitai-Preiss (Mongols and Mamluks, 1995) argues the two armies at Ain Jalut were roughly equal, Kitbuqa having 10,000-12,000 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ain_Jalut). Population convention: Egypt plus the Syria and Palestine won in 1260; Frankish coastal states, Kerak (Ayyubid until 1263) and Lesser Armenia excluded. No 1260 polygon exists; see the territory note.

areaKm2.note: Over 2.5 million km2 at the 1760 zenith, about a third of the subcontinent (Turchin, Adams and Hall 2006 p. 223, via the article) (high, includes chauth-paying tributaries); low for the directly ruled swarajya and sardar domains. The world_1715 Maratha polygon (~87,000 km2) is the Shahu-era homeland and badly understates 1760; world_1783 has a "Maratha Confederacy" polygon (~1.05 million km2) but postdates the snapshot.

population.note: About a third of the subcontinent by area (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire); OWID/HYDE India 1750 = 183M, Pakistan 14.9M, Bangladesh 17.1M (~215M, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). One third = ~72M; the Deccan was less dense than the Ganges plain, so mid 60M. High includes tributaries paying chauth.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pune, Nagpur, Indore, Baroda, Ahmedabad (shared), garrison towns.

activePersonnel.note: The Panipat field army (1760-61) had 55,000 cavalry (11,000 regular) and 9,000 Gardi infantry, while the bulk of the Maratha army stayed in the Deccan with the Peshwa (via the article); over 50,000 regular troops took Delhi in August 1760 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire). Total standing household and silladar horse, infantry and fort garrisons doubled from Panipat.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Pindari irregular horse, local militia, sardar contingents not under arms.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Gunners, artillery train and fleet crews (gallivats and grabs).

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: Mughal Empire 1690 snapshot, Barua (2005 p. 47) via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire: the Ain-i-Akbari count of 4 million armed men equalled ~3% of the Indian population in 1600 (armed peasantry of the same Deccan and north Indian military labour market from which the Maratha silladars were raised). Low 0.02, high 0.035 as in that snapshot. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.004/0.006/0.008 (educated guess, a fifth of the regional peer); replaced by the regional analogy.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high). audit 2026-10-30: recomputed for the new mobilizationRatio.

maratha-confederacy-1760.notes: Snapshot = autumn 1760, Maratha zenith after the recapture of Delhi, before the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761). Personnel convention: household (paga) and contracted silladar cavalry, Gardi and mercenary infantry and fort garrisons under arms are activePersonnel; pindaris and uncalled sardar contingents are trainedReserves. Panipat figures via the Third Battle of Panipat article (Gordon, Roy); Gommans and Roy on Maratha warfare not consulted directly. Border: the nearest file at or before 1760 is world_1715, whose Maratha polygon is the early homeland only. Population convention: Peshwa domains and the great sardar states (Holkar, Scindia, Bhonsle, Gaekwad) plus chauth-paying tracts in the high value.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 4.0 million km2 (high). The historical-basemaps world_bc300 polygon (nearest file at or before -250 holding the polity) measures 1.95 million km2 on the sphere (computed from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_bc300.geojson, low); it predates the Kalinga conquest (c. 261 BCE) and the southern extension. Mid 3.0M is between; older textbook figures of 5M include loosely held periphery.

population.note: Dyson (2018, p. 24, quoted on the page): South Asia in Mauryan times (320-220 BCE) held 15-30 million; Sumit Guha treats 20 million as an upper limit. The empire covered most but not all of that (Tamil south and forest tribes outside), mid 22M; high 35M allows for older estimates (50-60M, e.g. HYDE India year 0 = 75M via OWID) that this file treats as too high. Seshat codes an unusable 15.5-181M range (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/87).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pataliputra 50,000-270,000 (Seshat 87, uncertain), Taxila, Ujjain and other Ganges cities; overwhelmingly rural.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Megasthenes via Pliny gives Chandragupta 600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots and 9,000 elephants (ancient claim, quoted on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_elephant); rejected as a mid. Kalinga alone is credited with 60,000 infantry, 1,000 cavalry and 700 elephants (same page). ~1% of a 22M population is the mid.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Guild (sreni) militias, allied and forest-tribe contingents reachable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts and crews for ~2,500 elephants (2-3 each), chariot crews, the six war-office boards, commissariat and river transport.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Salaried standing army plus guild (sreni) and forest-tribe levies named in the Arthashastra; a few percent of the population is the ceiling for an agrarian empire of this kind.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Spear and shield infantry of the salaried army; share of the active-force guess.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: iron spears and swords, little body armour

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: paid standing troops under the Arthashastra boards

count.note: Educated guess. Archers with the long bamboo bow described by Megasthenes/Arrian; share of the active-force guess.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: powerful but slow long bow

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: standing archers

count.note: Educated guess. Hired (bhrta) light troops in state pay.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light weapons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: paid troops

count.note: Educated guess. Horse; Pliny claims 30,000 (high). Indian cavalry was light and secondary to elephants.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: small horses, no stirrups

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: standing troops

count.note: Educated guess. Pliny/Megasthenes claim 8,000 (high); chariots were already declining in Indian warfare.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: heavy four-horse chariots, a generation behind

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: board of chariots in the war office

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Ancient claim 9,000 (Megasthenes/Pliny, high) and 500 ceded to Seleucus c. 303 BCE, called a small part of the Mauryan force (both on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_elephant).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: largest elephant corps of the age, superintendent of elephants (gajadhyaksha)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: elephant sanctuaries and specialist trainers per the Arthashastra

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: centralised war office of 30 members in six boards (Megasthenes); Kalinga conquered c. 261

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: salaried standing army paid from the treasury (Arthashastra), allied contingents less cohesive

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: Ashoka renounced conquest after Kalinga; no major war in progress

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (300 BCE iron weapons). Evidence: iron swords and spears, long bamboo bow; no torsion artillery attested in use

armor.note: Anchor: between 2 (bronze scale) and 3. Evidence: Arthashastra lists armour types, but Greek sources describe lightly armoured troops

ships.note: Anchor: between 2 and 3. Evidence: superintendent of ships; river and coastal craft on the Ganges and the Bay of Bengal

fortification.note: Anchor: 3 (ashlar walls, siege towers). Evidence: Pataliputra timber wall with 64 gates and 570 towers (Megasthenes, on the Maurya page)

logistics.note: Anchor: 3 (engineered roads, depots). Evidence: Uttarapatha road Bengal to Taxila, state granaries and storehouses

communications.note: Anchor: 3 (mounted relay posts). Evidence: courier system and edicts posted across the empire

isr.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: extensive spy network prescribed by the Arthashastra audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.1 -> 3.03, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -250 (3.032); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no India value before 1600 (1,264); its year-1 values are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, Belgium/France 956 (2011 int$). Ancient South Asia placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Large salaried army and elephant establishment paid from land revenue; no budget survives.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. State workshops, mining and guild crafts in a mostly agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Fertile Ganges plain with rice double-cropping; state granaries.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. The Uttarapatha ran ~2,500 km from Bengal to Taxila; other roads linked the Narmada basin and the south (Stein, on the Maurya page).

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Tamralipti, Sopara, Bharukaccha.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Coastal and Bay of Bengal trade craft; no figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ox-cart and elephant trains; armies operated within the road network.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, buffalo and some horses across a 22M agrarian population.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 (familiar terrain, local supply) to 1.2 (fortified cities like Pataliputra). Monsoon floods hamper invaders.

maurya--250.notes: Snapshot c. 250 BCE under Ashoka, after the Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE; Ashoka claims 100,000 killed and 150,000 deported, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinga_War). Population convention: everything inside the empire, Dyson's low modern range for South Asia; older figures of 50-60 million are treated as the high end only. All army figures from Megasthenes, Pliny and Plutarch (600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry, 8,000-9,000 elephants) are ancient claims and only bound the high side. Elephants and chariots are platforms; mahouts and crews are in supportPersonnel. Border: world_bc300 is the nearest file at or before the year that contains the polity; it understates the extent (no Kalinga, no Deccan), so areaKm2 mid is researched, not the polygon. GDP per capita is a regional analogy (grade D). Ratings use the rubric in data/SOURCES.md. Personnel: active = the hereditary (maula) and hired (bhrta) troops in state pay with the royal elephants and chariots; trainedReserves = guild (sreni), allied and forest-tribe (atavi) levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 1,957,194 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 1,943,950 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes offshore islands.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 131,946,900). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:MEX.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.433 as quoted: 301,000 active (excludes 136,900 paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025: ~260,000 Armed Forces plus ~110,000 National Guard (low). World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 341,000 (2020, high, includes paramilitary). Navy 92,043 personnel (2025) per Mexican Navy article.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.84. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MEX/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 11.40% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.71 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.70-0.71). Mid 1 - 0.114/0.71 = 0.84. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.70 = 0.79. High: s 0.71 = 0.84. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 71% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large exporter of fruit, vegetables and beef but the largest importer of US maize; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

Occupied Jiaozhi (northern Vietnam, 1407-1427) adds ~0.1 million, not in the polygon.

population.note: William Atwell estimates ~90 million around 1400, citing Heijdra and Mote (mid); the 1393 census gave 60,545,812 (low), revised by Ping-ti Ho to 65 million for areas not counted (Ming dynasty page). Yongle added guards for the Beijing move but abolished most princely guards. Real strength below nominal (by the 16th century 845,000 actual against 3 million registered, Swope 2009); early in the dynasty the gap was smaller, so mid ~85% of nominal.

ming-1420.notes: Snapshot 1420, the year Beijing became the capital and between the fifth and sixth treasure voyages. Border: world_1400 has no Ming polygon (it still shows the Yuan Great Khanate), so the nearest file containing the polity is world_1492. Army: nominal weisuo establishment from Dreyer, with an educated discount; registered strength and real strength diverged more as the century went on. Population convention: registered census is the low, modern reconstructions the mid; Jiaozhi's population is not counted. Malacca is listed as a supply depot of the fleet, not a colony. Personnel: active = registered hereditary weisuo soldiers on duty and the fleet; trainedReserves = military-household men on farm rotation; mobilizable = population x ratio.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 China 1600 = 1,217 (2011 int$); range is the usual uncertainty of the series.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Military costs (frontier silver, the three campaigns) were the largest item in a low-tax state; low = peacetime.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Silk and cotton textiles, porcelain, iron, shipbuilding; silver monetisation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Jiangnan rice surplus shipped north on the Grand Canal.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Courier roads and the Grand Canal towpath.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Guangzhou, Yuegang, Quanzhou, Fuzhou, Ningbo, Dengzhou, Tianjin.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Private junk trade legalised at Yuegang in 1567; no aggregate figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ming armies in Korea depended on supply through Liaodong and Korean granaries.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, water buffalo, horses, mules.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: walled cities and depth; rebellions and unpaid garrisons reduce support.

ming-1600.notes: Snapshot = 1600, Wanli reign, at the end of the Three Great Campaigns (Ordos 1592, Korea 1592-98, Bozhou 1599-1600). Personnel convention: the ~845,000 troops actually under arms (mostly hired) are activePersonnel; the 3 million registered hereditary soldiers not serving, militia and tusi levies are trainedReserves. Army figures come from Swope (A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail, 2009) and Lorge via the Military of the Ming dynasty and Imjin War articles; the split into roles is an educated reading. Population convention: provinces and frontier commands of the Ming; Korea and tributary states excluded.

areaKm2.note: No single 1241 polygon exists. Computed on the sphere from world_1279 polygons: Great Khanate 10.49M (minus Song China ~2-2.5M and Dali, not yet conquered), Golden Horde 5.25M, Chagatai Khanate 3.32M, plus ~2M of the Ilkhanate (northern Iran, Caucasus).

population.note: Educated guess, no modern estimate for the empire at 1241 found. Built from HYDE/Gapminder country series (OWID) for 1200-1300: Mongolia 0.8M, Kazakhstan 0.96M, Uzbekistan 1.04M, Turkmenistan 0.19M, Iran 5.0M (1200, ~half under Mongol rule by 1241), China 103M (1200, of which the former Jin/Xi Xia north after the 1211-34 wars plausibly 20-30M; the 1236 Mongol census registered far fewer households). Adds Uyghur, Qipchaq steppe and Volga Bulgar lands ~2-3M. Excludes tributary vassals (Rus principalities ~6M, Georgia/Armenia, Goryeo) and Song China. (context page: https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true)

urbanization.note: Analogue: HYDE urban share for China 1500 = 6.5% (OWID urbanization-last-500-years); steppe near 0, Transoxiana oases higher. Educated guess.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Anchors: Chinggis Khan left ~129,000 men at his death in 1227 (Rashid al-Din, accepted as order of magnitude by May, Mongol Art of War ch. 2, and Morgan); by 1241 the army had absorbed Turkic (Qipchaq) contingents and Han/Khitan/Jurchen armies in North China. Field forces at once: Batu's western army (40,000-150,000), the Chinese front, Chormaqan/Baiju in Iran and the Caucasus, garrisons.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: adult nomad males outside active tumens (all trained by lifelong riding and the nerge hunt, May ch. 2) plus subject levies callable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: Chinese and Muslim siege engineers, artisans, yam relay staff and baggage handlers attached to the armies (May ch. 4 on siege specialists).

mobilizationRatio.note: Mongol nomads mobilised nearly every adult male (decimal levy, ~1 soldier per 4-5 people of the nomadic population, cf. May, Mongol Art of War ch. 2), but the sedentary majority supplied only levies and auxiliaries. Applied to the whole subject population this gives a few percent. Educated guess.

mongol-empire-1241.notes: Border: hb:1279:Great Khanate chosen over hb:1200:Mongol Empire. The 1200 polygon (5.4M km2) is the pre-1206 Mongol homeland only and misses North China, Central Asia and the western steppe; 1279 is also the closer file in years (38 vs 41). The Great Khanate polygon holds Karakorum, Mongolia and North China but wrongly includes Song South China and Dali (conquered 1253-79) and omits the western ulus (Golden Horde polygon) from which the 1241 invasion came. A union of world_1279 features with SUBJECTO = "Mongol Empire" minus Song and Tibet would be the honest border. Army sizes are the weakest part. Western (Batu/Subotai) army: Rashid al-Din gives ~40,000 horsemen for the 1241 invasion of Central Europe, read by Sverdrup (J. Medieval Military History 8, 2010, p. 115) as a nominal force of at least 30,000; Khrustalev puts the 1237-40 Rus campaign at ~60,000; older modern estimates run 120,000-150,000 (all via the Battle of Mohi and Kievan Rus' invasion articles as pointers, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mohi). Medieval chroniclers' 200,000-500,000 are rejected. Empire-wide totals are educated guesses. Population convention: directly ruled lands only; tributary Rus principalities, Georgia, Armenia and Goryeo excluded (includes is empty). All ratings use the rubric in data/SOURCES.md.

mongol-empire-1279.notes: Snapshot 1279, the year of Yamen, when Kublai's Yuan held all of China. Scope: the Yuan realm only (the Great Khanate polygon of world_1279: China, Mongolia, Manchuria, Tibet and Dali). The other khanates are excluded from population, forces and territory: after 1264 the Golden Horde, Chagatai Khanate and Ilkhanate were functionally autonomous (Rossabi 1988, Allsen 1994 via the Yuan dynasty page); only the Ilkhans truly recognised Kublai as Great Khan, and Kaidu with the Chagatayids was at war with him. None of them exists as a snapshot, so includes is empty. Goryeo was a vassal, not counted. Army totals are the weakest part: no fetched source gives a Yuan order of battle, so the active total and its split are educated guesses anchored on the 1274/1281 Japan expeditions and the Military of the Yuan dynasty page. Ship counts from Yuan records (900 in 1274, 4,400 in 1281) are claims; Conlan argues the 1274 landing force was only ~3,000. Personnel: active = hereditary military-household soldiers on service (Mongol, Tammachi, Han, Newly Adhered), guards and fleets; trainedReserves = household men not on service, steppe herders and Goryeo levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.42. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MAR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 27.89% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.48 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.40-0.61). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 3.2-4.5 million km2 for 1700. The world_1650 polygon measures ~2.73 million km2 and predates the 1686-87 annexation of Bijapur and Golconda, so it understates 1690.

population.note: Seshat codes 110-150 million for 1700. High extended to 160M: OWID/HYDE gives India 165M, Pakistan 13.6M and Bangladesh 15.4M for 1700 (whole subcontinent ~194M, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); the Mughals did not rule the far south, Assam or the Maratha hill country.

urbanization.note: Habib and Moosvi put the urban share at ~15% (1600-1700, 23M urban by 1700); Tim Dyson considers this exaggerated and puts it under 9%. Mid splits the two.

activePersonnel.note: Lahori (1647) lists 200,000 stipendiary cavalry, 185,000 other cavalry and 40,000 garrisoned musketeers and gunners (~425,000); Rosen uses 550,000 for the Mughal military; Aurangzeb took ~170,000 cavalry to the Deccan (Eraly 2007 p. 300). All via the article. Counted: mansabdari contingents (paid via jagirs, standing), ahadis, walashahi guards, imperial infantry and gunners, fleet crews.

trainedReserves.note: Zamindari retainers and local militia: the Ain-i-Akbari census gives ~4.4 million (Barua 2005 p. 47, Rosen considers it pragmatic); Kolff reads it as an inventory of military labour available for hire rather than an army. Raychaudhuri/Eraly 26 million raw pool rejected. Counted as levy per the convention.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Artillery corps under the Mir-i-Atish, elephant drivers, Bengal fleet crews (Dhaka fleet: 768 boats with 933 Portuguese crew and 8,112 artillery personnel, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire), engineers and staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Barua (2005 p. 47): the Ain-i-Akbari 4 million soldiers equalled ~3% of the Indian population in 1600.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Lahori 1647: 200,000 stipendiary (mansabdari) cavalry; Mughal heavy horse in mail, lamellar or half-plate on Turki and Arab horses (Gommans 2002 p. 114-120 via the article).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: mail-and-plate, composite bow, lance, two horses per trooper; among the best cavalry of the era.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: professional troopers of the mansabdars.

count.note: Lahori 1647: 185,000 other cavalry (princes, faujdars, Rajput and Afghan contingents); scaled down for those on campaign or at garrisons. Range up to the 1647 figure.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: era-typical horse archers and lancers, lower-grade horses (tattus).

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75.

count.note: Lahori 1647: 40,000 garrisoned musketeers and gunners (low); plus banduqchi matchlockmen raised by mansabdars (educated scaling).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: matchlocks; Mughals paid insufficient attention to firearm quality (Roy, via the article).

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: ill-paid, ill-equipped, lacking discipline (article on the ahsam infantry).

count.note: Educated guess. Shamsherbaz swordsmen, Mridha archers, sebandi revenue infantry with field forces.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: militia-grade.

count.note: Akbar kept 5,000-7,000 in the fil-khana; Moosvi estimates 5,000, Sukumar 12,000-40,000 under Jahangir (all via the article). Count = war-capable elephants with field armies; most were baggage animals.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: armoured (bargustawan-i-pil), some carrying swivel guns (gajnal).

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75.

count.note: Educated guess. Heavy siege guns, bronze light field guns, zamburak camel guns and rockets under the Mir-i-Atish; Bernier saw Aurangzeb take 200-300 camel guns to Kashmir (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire). Field and siege pieces, swivel guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: heavy guns hard to move, some burst; light bronze pieces useful.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: specialised corps, many European gunners.

count.note: Bengal river fleet (nawara): the Dhaka fleet held 768 vessels (UNESCO via the article); ghurabs of 14 guns and 50-60 crew. Mid allows for the Indus and Gujarat flotillas being small.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: river craft, effective against Ahom and Arakanese.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: officers often hired Europeans.

count.note: Educated guess. Seagoing warships of the Siddi admirals of Janjira (Mughal naval arm on the west coast) that blockaded Bombay in 1689 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: outclassed by English and Portuguese ships.

training.note: Rubric 0.5.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Aurangzeb and his generals took Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687) and captured Sambhaji (1689), but could not end Maratha guerrilla war.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mansabdar contingents loyal to their commanders; jagir shortage after the Deccan conquests strained loyalty.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: recent victories offset by a decade of attritional campaigning in the Deccan.

weapons.note: Anchor 5 (1600): matchlocks, heavy bronze and iron guns, mortars, rockets; no flintlocks or bayonets yet.

armor.note: Anchor 4-5: mail-and-plate (chahar-aina), lamellar, horse barding.

ships.note: Anchor 4-5: river ghurabs and armed merchantmen up to 1,600 t (Ganj-i-Sawai, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire).

fortification.note: Anchor 4-5: massive masonry forts (Agra, Lahore, Daulatabad, Golconda) without bastioned trace.

logistics.note: Anchor 5 minus: banjara grain convoys, camp markets financed by hundi credit (Gommans 2002 p. 105 via the article), river transport.

communications.note: Anchor 5: dak chowki relay posts and imperial newswriters.

isr.note: Anchor 4-5: waqia-navis newswriters and harkara spies.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 India 1650 = 1,189, 1700 = 1,162 (2011 int$); 1690 interpolated.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Most of the jama (Aurangzeb ~450 million rupees a year, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurangzeb) was assigned to mansabdars to maintain troops; low = peacetime, mid = Deccan war.

industrialShare.note: Moosvi: late-16th-century secondary sector 18% of the economy (via the article).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. High land revenue (a third or more of the crop) fed large towns and armies.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Grand Trunk road (Kabul-Lahore-Agra-Bengal) and the Agra-Burhanpur-Deccan and Agra-Ajmer-Ahmedabad highways with sarais.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.03 -> 0.61. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/MMR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 44.95% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.15 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.12-1.22). Mid 1 - 0.450/1.15 = 0.61. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.12 = 0.52. High: s 1.22 = 0.63. Net exporter: production is about 115% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Traditionally a rice exporter; war, displacement and the 2025 Sagaing earthquake reduced output.

myanmar-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. Population inside the ne: border (World Bank 2025). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. CIVIL WAR: the junta (the State Administration Council was dissolved on 31 Jul 2025 when the state of emergency ended, power passing to the National Defence and Security Council and the State Security and Peace Commission, before the December 2025-January 2026 elections; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Administration_Council) is fighting the NUG's People's Defence Force and ethnic armed organisations (Arakan Army, KIA, MNDAA, TNLA). After Operation 1027 (October 2023) it lost much of the north and Rakhine; China-brokered deals returned Lashio (2025) and the junta retook Kyaukme (October 2025) and Mogok/Momeik (January 2026). Territory under firm junta control is well under half (estimates under 40% in 2024). This snapshot covers the Tatmadaw only; ne:MMR border overstates its reach, and population is the whole country. Equipment is paper strength discounted for losses (grade D). Doctrine: archetype-modern-regional (conventional force fighting a counter-insurgency). Militia (Pyusawhti) and police excluded. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: SAC "rebranded after the election" -> dissolved 31 Jul 2025, before the vote.

mycenaean-greece--1250.notes: Snapshot = c. 1250 BCE, LH IIIB palatial peak (Ahhiyawa of the Hittite texts). Mycenaean Greece was a set of palace kingdoms, not one state; this snapshot aggregates them, so commandQuality and cohesion are low. Capital = Mycenae as the leading centre. All force numbers are reconstructions from Linear B (Pylos rower and o-ka tablets, Knossos chariot tablets) and are grade D; Homer is not used. Population convention: mainland palatial regions, Crete and the Aegean inside the border.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1,400,000 km2 for 911-612 BCE; Taagepera 1978 and Turchin 2006 give 1.4 million km2 at 670 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). The historical-basemaps world_bc700 file has only a core 'Assyria' polygon (174,000 km2), so the border unions Assyria + Babylonia + Arameans + Kingdom of David and Solomon (Levant) = ~877,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON (low side); western Iran, Cilicia and Lower Egypt (conquered 671) are missing from the polygon and Susa (Elamite) is wrongly included.

population.note: Seshat codes 5,000,000-7,000,000 for 670 BCE (mid = midpoint). High allows Lower Egypt, held 671-669.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes the largest settlement (Nineveh) at 120,000 for 700 BCE; Assyrian capitals were very large, the periphery rural.

activePersonnel.note: Dalley 2017 (p. 531, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire): the number of soldiers was likely several hundred thousand at the empire's height; Healy 1991 (p. 23, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_Neo-Assyrian_Empire): capable of 120,000+ (Shalmaneser III's boast of 120,000 men). Composition anchor: Qarqar 853 BCE, Gabriel 2002-2003 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Qarqar) gives the Assyrian side 35,000 incl. 20,000 infantry, 12,000 cavalry (sic) and 1,200 chariots. Army = central standing army (kisir sarri) plus provincial contingents raised by governors and vassal troops (Dalley 2017 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire). Mid = standing army, garrisons and provincial contingents in service in 670 (Egyptian and Median frontiers active); high toward Dalley's 'several hundred thousand'.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Provincial levies callable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Chariot crews (3-4 per vehicle), engineers and sappers, interpreters, guides, supply train, scribes.

training.note: Specialist engineers.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: trained staff (turtanu, rab shaqe), intelligence networks, campaign planning; Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional core with strong identity, large share of deportee and vassal troops.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: imperial confidence, recent conquest of Egypt.

weapons.note: Near anchor 3: iron weapons in general use, siege engines; no torsion artillery. audit 2026-10-30: mid 2.8 -> 2.66, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -670 (2.664); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

armor.note: Between 2 and 3: iron scale armour, iron helmets, horse armour.

ships.note: Between 2 and 3: relied on Phoenician vassal galleys.

fortification.note: Near anchor 3: massive walled capitals (Nineveh 12 km circuit), siege towers. audit 2026-10-30: mid 2.8 -> 2.66, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -670 (2.664); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

logistics.note: Near anchor 3: royal roads with stations, depot provisioning before campaigns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire). audit 2026-10-30: mid 2.9 -> 2.66, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -670 (2.664); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

communications.note: Anchor 3: state relay-post system and fire signals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire). audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.0 -> 2.66, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -670 (2.664); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

isr.note: Between 2 and 3: interpreters, guides, spy reports from governors.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Iraq, Iran, Israel 1 CE = 1,116 (2011 int$); Iraq 730 CE = 1,466. Applied ~670 years earlier.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Highly militarised tributary empire; tribute and booty financed much of it.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Large palace workshops, iron working, monumental building.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Rain-fed northern plains plus irrigated Babylonia; drought stress in the heartland late in the period.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; Bronze Age life expectancy was if anything lower, so this is not an underestimate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Royal roads (harran sharri) with stations linking the provinces; engineered stretches, total length undocumented.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Phoenician and Philistine vassal ports (Sidon/Kar-Esarhaddon, Arwad, Byblos, Gaza).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Phoenician merchant shipping under Assyrian control.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Pre-stocked campaign depots and vassal provisioning; Esarhaddon's march to Egypt crossed the Sinai with Arab camel supply.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (imported in thousands), mules, donkeys, camels, oxen; ~0.08-0.2 per inhabitant.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: fortified capitals, local supply; subject provinces disloyal.

neo-assyria--670.notes: Snapshot = 670 BCE, Esarhaddon after the conquest of Memphis (671); Taharqa retook it in 669. Forces = standing army plus provincial contingents in service. Royal inscriptions (Shalmaneser's 120,000; deportation totals) are not used as mids; scholarly totals are qualitative ('several hundred thousand'), so counts are grade C reconstructions. Population convention: everything inside the empire per Seshat; the border union understates the empire's real extent.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.3 -> 0.96. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NLD/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.70% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.42 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.41-0.42). Mid 1 - 0.017/0.42 = 0.96. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.41 = 0.94. High: s 0.42 = 0.96. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 42% of domestic calorie supply. s is depressed by imported feed and by imports processed for re-export (cocoa, soy, palm oil); the result is insensitive to s because a is small. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. World second-largest agri-food exporter by value; imports much feed.

niger-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 910,770 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 923,768 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 237,527,782). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~2.5%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.509 as quoted: 143,000 active (Army ~100,000, Navy ~25,000, Air Force ~18,000 in earlier editions). CIA Factbook 2025 ~140,000 (low). High is World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 223,000 (2020), which adds the 80,000 paramilitary.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 as quoted lists no organised reserve (0). High is an allowance for recallable ex-servicemen (educated judgement). Paramilitary (80,000, NSCDC etc.) excluded.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 143,000 (IISS 2024) minus infantry P roles (25,000 + 55,000) = 63,000: Navy ~25,000, Air Force ~18,000, armour/artillery crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: very large youthful population but no conscription, no reserve system and no stocks to equip mass levies; scaled well below 20th-century total-war ratios (8-15%). Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry of the mechanised and armoured brigades (1 Mech, 3 Armd, 81 Div elements); Army ~100,000 (IISS as quoted on the personnel list). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mixed BMP/Saurer/MRAP fleet, poor maintenance (Nigerian Army article: "exceptionally poor standard of maintenance").

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteer regulars with long COIN experience (Boko Haram/ISWAP since 2009) but weak combined-arms training.

count.note: Educated guess. Motorised/light infantry and COIN brigades (Operation Hadin Kai deployed up to ~70,000 troops in the northeast at times, CIA Factbook 2025). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/ni.json)

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.63. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NGA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 33.53% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.91 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.91-0.92). Mid 1 - 0.335/0.91 = 0.63. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.91 = 0.56. High: s 0.92 = 0.64. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 91% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food importer (rice, wheat) with large subsistence agriculture; most surplus feeds the cities. Not computed from FAO balance sheets.

nigeria-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Equipment counts from Wikipedia equipment lists (Army, Air Force, Navy; many Army entries from deliveries, not IISS active figures) cross-checked with the IISS-derived main battle tank list; serviceability is poor and counts are grade C. Population convention: everything inside ne:NGA (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. ships_major = frigates (incl. ex-Hamilton cutters); drones = Group 2+ only. Appleman (South to the Naktong, CMH 1961, ch. 2) gives the older US estimate ~135,000 (low). ROK MND figure also in the Operation Pokpung infobox.

The North held most of the Japanese-built heavy industry and hydropower (Hungnam chemicals, Supung dam) but had suffered Soviet dismantling and the 1945-50 emigration; taken equal to the South, range 0.7-1.4 x.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: COW milex for PRK 1950 is missing (-9). The DPRK had mobilised for an invasion for over a year (Pokpung article); arms came largely as Soviet credit, so the budget share understates the effort. Low = 1949 level, high = wartime.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Northern Korea held most of colonial Korea's heavy industry, mining and electricity; agriculture still the largest employer.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) North Korea 1960 = 64.0% (the series starts in 1960, so it is the floor for 1950); CIA World Factbook 1990: 36% (1987). 1950 share extrapolated to ~72% (64-80%) on the 1960-70 trend of ~0.9 points a year. Grade C. Share 72.0% (range 64.0-80.0%) -> 0.28 (0.2-0.36).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess: Males reaching 18 per year: ~9.6M population, ~2.1% per single-year cohort, halved.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Mostly unpaved roads north of the 38th parallel; few could bear tanks, so the T-34 axes followed the main roads to Seoul.

railKm.note: Educated guess: Colonial Korea had ~6,000+ km of railway in 1945, the larger share in the north (Kyongui, Kyongwon, Hamgyong and Manpo lines); T-34s were light enough for Korean rail bridges (Pokpung article).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Chinnampo, Haeju, Wonsan, Hungnam, Chongjin, Rajin.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Small coastal merchant fleet; most seaborne trade was with the USSR in Soviet hulls.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: KPA advanced ~300 km to the Naktong in six weeks and its supply failed there under US air interdiction (Korean War article: forced to move only at night).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: Cattle (ox-carts) and some horses of the northern farm economy; ox-carts and A-frame porters carried KPA supplies.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS via OWID: no Korean nuclear weapons in 1950.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar mountainous terrain, local supply and population support; harsh winter but no great strategic depth.

north-korea-1950.notes: Snapshot date 25 June 1950 (invasion of South Korea, Operation Pokpung). Territory and population: the DPRK north of the 38th parallel (border ref hb:1945:Korea (USSR), the nearest basemap at or before 1950). Main source for the order of battle: ROK MND Institute for Military History compilation (2004) of KPA strength on 25 June 1950 (198,380 men incl. 34,000 Interior Ministry troops; 242 T-34; 552 howitzers; 1,728 mortars; 211 aircraft of which 170 combat), fetched from the web.archive.org copy of 1K29.pdf. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (CMH 1961) and history.army.mil could not be fetched (HTTP 403; archive.org copy is lending-only), so Appleman figures are cited from memory and only as low ends. activePersonnel includes the 38th Border Constabulary (paramilitary, but it fought in the invasion); other police excluded. No domestic arms production: all heavy equipment came from the USSR, so production is empty. Weakest numbers: GDP per head (no Maddison value), reserves and the fighter/attack split.

weapons.note: Anchor 8-9 mix: ICBMs/hypersonic IRBM and KN-23 are anchor-10-class; bulk of guns and small arms anchor 8.

armor.note: Anchor 8: T-55/T-62 derivatives; few Chonma-20 with modern features. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.8 -> 8.3: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; T-55/T-62 derivatives (1958-61 designs, interpolated ~8.4 between the 1943 and 1985 anchors) are above the 1950 T-34/85 (7.9).

ships.note: Anchor 8: small craft, Romeo submarines; new Choe Hyon destroyers anchor 9.

fortification.note: Anchor 9: massive hardened artillery sites (HARTS), tunnels, underground air bases.

logistics.note: Anchor 7-8: rail-dependent, chronic fuel shortage. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.4 -> 7.6: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; the rail net and truck park exceed those of 1950 (7.5); fuel shortage is a supply limit, not equipment.

communications.note: Anchor 8: wire/radio, limited data links.

isr.note: Anchor 8 plus: first reconnaissance satellite (Malligyong-1, 2023), few drones.

air.note: Anchor 8: MiG-17/19/21 copies; MiG-29 anchor 9. audit 2026-10-30: mid 7.4 -> 8.4: the tech scale is absolute equipment level, so it may not fall within a lineage; MiG-17/19/21 copies (1950s designs, ~8.3-8.5 by year) and a few MiG-29 (anchor 9) are above the 1950 Yak-9 and Il-10 (7.8).

cyber.note: Anchor 10 minus: Lazarus/Reconnaissance General Bureau - among the most active state cyber forces.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRK/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 54.1% (2025). s = 4.78 Mt 2024 crop (RDA, https://koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2025/03/103_393434.html) / 5.76 Mt FAO requirement (https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2024/08/103_380552.html) = 0.83. Mid 1 - 0.541/0.83 = 0.35. Low: a 0.60, s 0.78 (flood year) = 0.23. High: a 0.50, s 0.84 (4.82 Mt 2023) = 0.40. This surplus is what state procurement takes for the PDS and the army. Import dependence: chronic deficit of ~1 Mt a year. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.35, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

ottoman-empire-1453.notes: Snapshot = April 1453, start of the siege of Constantinople. Per the feudal-host convention the timariot sipahis, azabs and akincis of the siege army sit in trainedReserves; activePersonnel is the salaried kapikulu and the fleet. Siege-army estimates: 50,000-80,000 (recent studies, Ottoman archival), Runciman 100,000 (incl. non-combatants), western contemporaries 160,000-300,000 (rejected), all via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople. Agoston (Guns for the Sultan) is the standard modern source on artillery but was not consulted directly. Population convention: directly ruled Rumelia and Anatolia; vassal Serbia, Wallachia and Byzantine remnants excluded.

areaKm2.note: world_1530 Ottoman Empire polygons = 5,280,075 km2 on the sphere (includes the Arabian and North African claims and Hungary). Directly administered area was smaller; mid allows for the desert hinterlands of Arabia and Libya being nominal.

population.note: Sum of HYDE country values (OWID population.csv, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) interpolated to 1566 for the directly ruled lands: Anatolia (Turkey 6.25M in 1500, 8.0M in 1600), Egypt (4-5M), Greater Syria and Iraq (~3.5M), Balkans (Greece, Bulgaria, Bosnia, Albania, Macedonia, Serbia ~4.5M), Ottoman Hungary (~0.6M), North African regencies (~3M), Hejaz/Yemen (~1M) = ~24M; Barkan-type tax-register estimates for c. 1580 are 17-22M without North Africa. Vassal Wallachia, Moldavia, Transylvania and Crimea excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Turkey 2.3% (1500), 2.4% (1600) (de Vries-type, likely too low for the empire), Egypt 3.0-3.2%. Istanbul ~400,000, Cairo ~200,000, plus Edirne, Bursa, Aleppo, Damascus give a 5,000+ share around 8%.

activePersonnel.note: Standing salaried forces only: kapikulu (Janissaries 12,131 in 1547 and 13,599 in 1574, kapikulu sipahi 5,957, other kapikulu 9,619 = 29,175 in 1574) plus ~30,000 salaried fortress guards (Military of the Ottoman Empire, Ottoman Army Strength table, after Agoston 2014). 1566 sits between the 1547 and 1574 rows. Timariot cavalry is counted in trainedReserves.

trainedReserves.note: Provincial forces called for the campaign season: timariot sipahis ~40,000, ~90,000 with their cebelu retainers (1574 estimate), akinci raiders ~15,000, azab infantry ~20,000, yaya/musellem ~8,000 (same table). Tatar and Danubian vassal contingents excluded.

supportPersonnel.note: Other kapikulu corps (gunners topcu, gun-carriage arabaci, armourers cebeci, miners) 9,619 in 1574, plus galley fighting crews and arsenal seamen (~6,000-10,000 non-oarsmen). Galley oarsmen excluded.

mobilizationRatio.note: The 1574 total establishment of ~192,000 (same table) on ~22M population = 0.9%; with fortress militias and emergency levies the ceiling is ~1.2-1.6%. The timar system, not conscription, set the limit.

count.note: Janissaries ~12,500-13,000 (paper strength 12,131 in 1547 and 13,599 in 1574, Janissary article after Agoston 2014 p. 113) plus ~28,000 salaried fortress-guard infantry (Military of the Ottoman Empire table, 1574 estimate 30,000).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: janissary matchlocks (tufek) and archery; among the best infantry firepower of the 1560s (Agoston, Guns for the Sultan ch. 1); fortress guards lower

Personnel convention: kapikulu household troops and salaried fortress guards are active; timariot sipahis with retainers, akinci, azab and yaya are trainedReserves, because they served only when called for a campaign. Janissary figures are paper strengths from treasury pay registers (Agoston 2014); effective field strength was lower. The 1574 establishment table (Military of the Ottoman Empire) is the anchor; 1566 numbers are interpolated with 1547.

ottoman-empire-1914.notes: Snapshot date November 1914 (entry into the war 29 Oct-2 Nov 1914; mobilisation began 2 Aug). Territory = the empire after the Balkan Wars: Anatolia, Constantinople and eastern Thrace, Syria, Palestine, Iraq, Hejaz and Yemen (nominal); Egypt and Cyprus (British-occupied) and Libya excluded. Forces are the whole army; the Third Army in the Caucasus had ~100,000-150,000 men. Aircraft in aircraft_strike (no fighters). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Many values are reconstructions or educated guesses because Ottoman statistics are thin (Erickson is the main modern source, not fetched online).

pakistan-1971.notes: Snapshot date 3 December 1971 (PAF pre-emptive strikes, Operation Chengiz Khan). Population and territory include BOTH wings: West Pakistan and East Pakistan (today Bangladesh); hb:1960:Pakistan contains both polygons. includes is empty because Bangladesh had no state of its own until 16 December 1971. Main order-of-battle source: declassified CIA intelligence memorandum of 13 Sep 1971 (https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0000399238), table as of mid-1971; the IISS Military Balance 1971-72 and Sisson and Rose, War and Secession, were not fetchable and are not cited line by line. Theatre split for the battle agent: East Pakistan ~91,000 regular troops of all arms (Cloughley via the Bangladesh Liberation War article; CIA mid-1971 ~70,000, one corps of 3 divisions, later 2 ad hoc divisions), 16 F-86 and no submarines bar Ghazi; the rest in the West, 8+ divisions near Kashmir. Paramilitary (~280,000 incl. East Pakistan Civil Armed Forces and ~35,000 Razakars) excluded from active. Pakistan had no domestic production of major platforms in 1971 (Heavy Industries Taxila and the Kamra aircraft factories came later), so production is empty; resupply came from China, plus France for aircraft and submarines. Infantry splits are reconstructions (grade C/D).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.15 -> 0.62. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PAK/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 36.23% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.95 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.93-0.98). Mid 1 - 0.362/0.95 = 0.62. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.93 = 0.53. High: s 0.98 = 0.63. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 95% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Wheat/rice producer, food-insecure population, rice exporter; 2022 floods showed fragility.

pakistan-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. Population convention: inside ne:PAK (World Bank), i.e. Pakistan-administered Kashmir as the World Bank counts it. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Pakistan fought a short conflict with India in May 2025 and border clashes with Taliban Afghanistan in October 2025 and February-March 2026 (PAF airstrikes on Kandahar, Bagram and Paktika per the PAF article); losses disputed and not modelled. Equipment counts from Wikipedia equipment/aircraft/vessel lists quoting IISS for many lines (grade B/C). ships_major = frigates only; drones = Group 2+. Infantry splits, missile launchers, air-defence batteries are educated guesses. Paramilitary 291,000 excluded.

papua-new-guinea-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Commonwealth of Australia, New Zealand) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "Paraguay" = about 348,900 km2 on the sphere (pre-war Paraguay with its Chaco and Misiones claims; the polygon is unchanged in world_1783 and world_1800). Low: the post-war world_1878/1880 polygon, about 270,400 km2, after the cessions of 1872-76. Basemap borders are approximate and the pre-war frontiers were disputed.

population.note: Pre-war (1864) estimates: Whigham and Potthast 1999 420,000-450,000 (mid); Reber 1988 about 300,000 (low); Williams 1976 about 407,000, range 373,000-575,000 by assumed growth rate (high). Salles 2003 p. 18 gives about 450,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguayan_War). The traditional 1.3 million rests on an 1857 census Reber shows never took place and is not used.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: Asuncion was the only town of any size; the rest of the population lived in rural partidos and small river towns.

activePersonnel.note: Mid: over 60,000 trained men, 38,000 of them under arms, at the start of the war (Scheina 2003 pp. 315-317, via the article). Low: the Cerro Leon camp was set up in March 1864 to train 30,000 men (George Thompson); high: about 64,000 men aged 16-50 in training by August 1864 (Velazquez Seiferheld), both via https://www.lanacion.com.py/gran-diario-domingo/2024/06/23/un-monumento-historico-que-lucha-contra-el-olvido/. The peacetime army before the February 1864 call-up was only about 7,500 (note 40 of the war article).

trainedReserves.note: Trained but not under arms: Scheina's 60,000 trained minus 38,000 under arms = 22,000 (mid). High: Salles 2003 p. 18 puts the army at 70,000-100,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguayan_War), 70,000 - 30,000 active (low) = 40,000. Low allows for recruits still untrained.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: two artillery regiments (907 men in peacetime, note 40 of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguayan_War) expanded to four by 1864, crews of the 28 river steamers, arsenal and shipyard troops.

mobilizationRatio.note: Salles 2003 p. 18 (army of 70,000-100,000, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguayan_War) over the 420,000-450,000 population of Whigham and Potthast = 0.16-0.24. The militia took every able-bodied man, then boys and old men (note 40 of the article); Paraguay's mobilization was among the most complete of any 19th-century state.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Combat personnel (active - support, 34,000 at mid) x the infantry share at Cerro Leon in late December 1864: 10,958 infantry and 4,266 cavalry = 72% infantry (museum figures after von Horoch, https://www.lanacion.com.py/gran-diario-domingo/2024/06/23/un-monumento-historico-que-lucha-contra-el-olvido/). Low: the Cerro Leon infantry alone; high: 72% of 64,000.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly old flintlock muskets against Allied percussion and rifled arms; the article calls the army poorly equipped (Salles 2003 p. 18).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training). Evidence: most men called up in February 1864 and drilled for months at Cerro Leon and the regional depots; officers without training or experience (Salles 2003 p. 18).

count.note: Combat personnel x the 28% cavalry share at Cerro Leon in late December 1864 (4,266 of 15,224, https://www.lanacion.com.py/gran-diario-domingo/2024/06/23/un-monumento-historico-que-lucha-contra-el-olvido/). Low: the Cerro Leon cavalry alone; high: 28% of 64,000. Lancer and sabre regiments, counted as light horse.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: lances, sabres and few carbines.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: born horsemen of a cattle country, new to formation drill.

count.note: 400 cannons at the start of the war (Scheina 2003 pp. 315-317, via the article), many of them old smoothbore fortress guns at Humaita and the river batteries; low allows for unserviceable pieces.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: mostly obsolete smoothbores; a few modern pieces were cast later at the Asuncion arsenal.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regular artillery regiments existed before the war (907 men in peacetime).

count.note: The purpose-built paddle gunboat Tacuari (named in the article); high counts one converted steamer as a line warship.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: an unarmoured wooden paddle steamer against Brazilian steam warships and, from 1865, ironclads.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 minus. Evidence: small river navy with some foreign engineers.

count.note: 23 steamboats and five river-navigating ships (Scheina 2003 pp. 315-317, via the article) = 28, less the Tacuari counted as major; most were armed merchant river steamers. Low allows for unarmed transports.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: converted merchant steamers with a few guns each.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: river crews, no naval tradition; the fleet was destroyed at Riachuelo (June 1865).

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Lopez took every decision himself and his officers had no training or experience (Salles 2003 p. 18, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguayan_War); the 1865 offensives into Corrientes and Rio Grande do Sul were lost piecemeal.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: units fought on surrounded and to destruction for five years; draconian discipline.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: national war against invasion; the population followed the army to the end (175,000-300,000 Paraguayan dead, war article infobox).

weapons.note: Anchor: 6 (1805, flintlock musket, field guns). Evidence: flintlock muskets and smoothbore cannon, a generation behind the percussion and rifled arms of 1864.

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none). Evidence: no body armour, as in every army of the period.

ships.note: Anchor: 6-7. Evidence: steam paddle river craft, no ironclads.

fortification.note: Anchor: 6 (Vauban-type) toward 7 (trenches). Evidence: Humaita river batteries with a chain boom and long earthwork lines; the Allies needed until 1868 to take it.

logistics.note: Anchor: 6 (magazines + requisition). Evidence: river steamers on the Paraguay and a 72 km railway Asuncion-Paraguari; ox-carts elsewhere.

communications.note: Anchor: 6 (semaphore). Evidence: couriers and river steamers; whether the electric telegraph along the river was working in 1864 was not checked, hence grade D.

isr.note: Anchor: 5-6. Evidence: cavalry patrols and observation posts; no balloons (the Allies used them from 1867).

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 has no Paraguay value before 1939 (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). Analogues from the same file: Brazil 1864 = 971 (mid about that, Paraguay being a poor agrarian state); Latin America regional 1850 = 1,068, 1860 = 1,588 (high, scaled down for a landlocked economy); low 850 below Brazil. 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Mid is the 1864 mobilization year (wartime convention), low the peacetime share of a state that kept a small army but built an arsenal, shipyard and fortress from state yerba mate and timber monopolies.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. State arsenal and shipyard at Asuncion, the Ybycui ironworks and crafts; an agrarian and pastoral economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Self-sufficient in food (cattle, manioc, maize) with state estancias feeding the army; the army ate the herds down by 1868.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: cart roads around Asuncion and to the southern depots; the rivers carried most traffic.

railKm.note: Asuncion-Paraguari line, Paraguari at km 72, reached 6 October 1864 (uncited on the page). Low: the line to Pirayu/Cerro Leon opened in 1864 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_rail_transport_in_Paraguay); service was suspended in 1865. Grade D, not C: the 72 km figure is uncited on the wiki mirror it comes from.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: river ports only (Asuncion, Pilar, Concepcion, Humaita landing); no sea coast, all trade passed Argentine waters on the Parana.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: the 28 river steamers and sailing craft were mostly taken into the navy; a few hundred tons each.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. The Corrientes and Uruguay River offensives of 1865 broke down at 200-400 km from the depots.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: oxen and horses of a cattle-raising country; no count found.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: fortified river line, full population support, and marsh and disease that cost the Allied armies heavily; no great strategic depth, so below the full 1.3 row.

paraguay-1864.notes: Snapshot = December 1864, the mobilized Paraguayan army on the eve of the invasion of Mato Grosso that opened the War of the Triple Alliance. Personnel: men under arms (Scheina's 38,000 at mid) are activePersonnel, trained men at home are trainedReserves; the levy of every able man (boys and old men later) is the mobilizable pool. Population follows the post-1988 scholarship (Whigham and Potthast, Reber, Williams), not the old 1.3 million. Infantry/cavalry split from the Cerro Leon muster of late December 1864. Weakest values: GDP per capita (no Maddison series before 1939), the force split outside Cerro Leon, and the economy and logistics guesses. Territory = the world_1815 Paraguay polygon; includes is empty.
