Light cavalry = Tarentines (at Panium, Polybius 16.18.7), Dahae horse archers (1,200 at Magnesia), Galatian horse, Arab camel archers.

quality.note: Horse archers and javelin cavalry, era-typical to good.

training.note: Mercenary and steppe riders.

count.note: Polybius 11.34.12 (https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/11*.html): after the anabasis (206) Antiochus' elephants "amounted now to a hundred and fifty" (high). Raphia 217: 102 (Polybius 5.79.13); Magnesia 190: 54 (Livy 37.39-40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37, low end allows for this decline). Elephants were used at Panium (Polybius 16.18.7). Indian elephants. Mahouts in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Indian elephants with towers, larger than the African forest elephants of the Ptolemies (Polybius 5.84, Livy 37.39); among the era's best (rubric 0.75-1.0).

training.note: Professional Indian mahouts; elephants stabled and trained at Apamea.

count.note: Livy 33.19 (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_33): in spring 197 Antiochus sailed with "a hundred decked ships and two hundred smaller vessels" after calling up "the whole strength of his kingdom" (high). Livy 37 (https://www.gutenberg.org/files/44318/44318-h/44318-h.htm, Polyxenidas 190): seventy decked ships (mid). Low allows for ships not yet built in 200. Quadriremes, quinqueremes and a few larger polyremes (Livy 37.23-24, Side 190).

quality.note: Era-typical to good Hellenistic polyremes, Phoenician-built; defeated by the Rhodians and Romans in 190.

training.note: Phoenician crews; less experienced than the Rhodian navy.

count.note: Livy 33.19 (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_33): 200 smaller vessels "including swift pinnaces and Cyprian barques" in 197 (high); mid and low allow for the 200 BCE fleet being smaller.

quality.note: Light galleys, era-typical.

training.note: Phoenician and Cilician crews.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Antiochus III "the Great", proven by the anabasis (212-205) and the cavalry victory at Panium; but he lost Raphia (217) by an over-long pursuit, and the officer corps was court-based rather than a trained staff.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: Macedonian-armed core with strong identity (0.75), large allied and subject contingents (0.25).

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: motivated, recent victories (anabasis, Panium 200, conquest of Coele-Syria).

weapons.note: Anchor 3 (300 BCE: iron weapons, torsion artillery, sarissa) plus war elephants and cataphract lances.

armor.note: Anchor 3 (bronze/iron cuirass, mail) plus full cataphract armour for horse and rider; still well short of anchor 4 plate-and-mail. audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.2 -> 3.06, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -200 (3.065); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

ships.note: Anchor 3 (triremes, quinqueremes) with larger polyremes (hepteres at Side 190). audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.2 -> 3.06, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -200 (3.065); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: ashlar city walls and citadels (Antioch, Apamea, Dura-Europos); siege trains reduced Sardis (214) and Bactra (208-206).

logistics.note: Anchor 3: inherited Achaemenid road and depot system, royal granaries; the anabasis marched to Bactria and India and back.

communications.note: Anchor 3: mounted relay posts on the former Achaemenid royal roads.

isr.note: Year anchor 3: mounted scouts and Tarentine light horse.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: year 1 CE values for Iraq, Iran, Israel and Jordan 1,116, Turkey 897 (2011 int$). Applied two centuries earlier to a Syria-Mesopotamia-Iran core; western Iran and Anatolian holdings poorer.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Standing guard, mercenaries, elephants and fleet paid in coin from a royal revenue Livy and Polybius describe as vast; the military-settler phalanx was paid largely in land. Similar order to Ptolemaic Egypt (army and navy ~34% of the royal budget per Fischer-Bovet).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Agrarian empire with craft centres in Syria, Phoenicia and Babylonia.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Irrigated Mesopotamian agriculture and the Syrian plains produced large surpluses (Seleucia on the Tigris supplied by Babylonian grain).

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Inherited Achaemenid royal roads (Sardis-Susa ~2,500 km and branches to Ecbatana, Bactra, Persepolis) plus Syrian routes; no engineered network on the Roman scale. Same order as persia-achaemenid--480.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Seleucia Pieria, Laodicea-on-Sea, Tyre, Sidon, Ptolemais-Akko (taken 200) and the Cilician ports; Ephesus only from 197. Count by analogy with persia-achaemenid--480.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Phoenician and Cilician merchant shipping; below the Achaemenid total since Egypt and the Aegean are outside the empire.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pack-animal and wagon-supplied Hellenistic armies operated about one to two weeks' march from a depot or navigable river; elephants added large fodder needs.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.07 / 0.09 / 0.11 draft and pack animals (oxen, mules, camels, horses) per inhabitant x population.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: familiar terrain, local supply and fortified Greek cities in Syria and Mesopotamia; native and Iranian loyalty weaker, so below 1.2 mid.

seleucid-empire--200.notes: Snapshot = late 200 BCE, Antiochus III after Panium, at the height of his reconquests. Forces are the royal field army at Raphia/Panium/Magnesia scale (Bar-Kochva treats these musters as the effective maximum of the Seleucid army); garrisons are only in activePersonnel. Ancient figures (Polybius, Livy) used for composition and as bounds, graded C. Scythed chariots (Magnesia 190) and the siege train are not counted: no number survives for 200. Bactria (Euthydemus) and Parthia (Arsaces II) were vassal kingdoms after the anabasis; inside the Seshat extent but not counted in the mid population. Population convention: Seshat range.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes Late Shang Polity Territory at 1,000,000 km2; Taagepera 1978 gives 1.25 million km2 at 1122 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). Low = a royal domain plus close allies only (educated guess). Border = historical-basemaps world_bc1500 polygon 'Zhoa' (sic), which contains Anyang and Zhengzhou and measures ~1,170,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON, consistent with the Seshat/Taagepera sphere of influence rather than direct rule.

population.note: Seshat codes Late Shang (1250-1045 BCE) population at 5,000,000 (single value). OWID/HYDE (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) gives 12.9 M for all of present-day China in 2000 and 1000 BCE, an upper envelope. Range is wide because Shang direct control vs allied fang states is unclear.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Yinxu was a large dispersed settlement (Seshat codes the largest settlement at only 4,000, which reflects one ward); most people lived in villages.

activePersonnel.note: Sawyer and Sawyer 1994 (pp. 33-34, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_dynasty): the Shang king kept about 1,000 troops at the capital; oracle-bone inscriptions show musters of 3,000-5,000 for border campaigns and up to 13,000 for suppressing rebellions (Wu Ding era; Fu Hao led such levies). From Wu Ding on, standing warriors increased and commoners (zhongren) were conscripted (Sawyer 2011 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty). The Shiji's 700,000 Shang troops at Muye (1046 BCE) are rejected. Mid = royal troops, lineage forces and one rebellion-scale muster plus border garrisons.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Commoner (zhongren) levies of royal and lineage estates.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Chariot crews (3 per vehicle), dog and horse officers, supply carriers.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Lineage armies plus conscripted commoners; the 13,000 musters suggest a low share of the population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Sawyer and Sawyer 1994 (pp. 33-34, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_dynasty): the Shang king kept about 1,000 troops at the capital; oracle-bone inscriptions show musters of 3,000-5,000 for border campaigns and up to 13,000 for suppressing rebellions (Wu Ding era; Fu Hao led such levies). From Wu Ding on, standing warriors increased and commoners (zhongren) were conscripted (Sawyer 2011 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty). The Shiji's 700,000 Shang troops at Muye (1046 BCE) are rejected. Split: archers ~27% ('Many Archers' office; officials trained archery).

quality.note: Reflex bows of 60-70 m effective range (Shaughnessy via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty); bone arrowheads outnumber bronze 20 to 1.

training.note: Trained archers among the levies.

count.note: Sawyer and Sawyer 1994 (pp. 33-34, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_dynasty): the Shang king kept about 1,000 troops at the capital; oracle-bone inscriptions show musters of 3,000-5,000 for border campaigns and up to 13,000 for suppressing rebellions (Wu Ding era; Fu Hao led such levies). From Wu Ding on, standing warriors increased and commoners (zhongren) were conscripted (Sawyer 2011 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty). The Shiji's 700,000 Shang troops at Muye (1046 BCE) are rejected. Split: skirmishers and allied Yi archers ~13%.

quality.note: Light kit.

training.note: Levies and allies.

count.note: Chariots reached Shang China c. 1200 BCE from the northern steppe (Wu 2013, Rawson 2020 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shang_dynasty); under the Shang they were ornate command and archery platforms with a chariot-to-foot ratio of about 1:30 (Lee 2016 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty), so a 13,000 muster implies at most ~400. At 1250 the chariot was just arriving, so mid is low. Crews in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Ornate, heavy-wheeled early chariots; few and used mainly by commanders.

training.note: Aristocratic crews new to the weapon.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: king as commander, defined posts (ma, ya, she, shu), divination-driven decisions, left/centre/right formations, ambush and reconnaissance in use.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: clan-based armies, unstable allied fang states.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: Wu Ding's long successful campaigns against the Guifang, Tufang and Qiang.

weapons.note: Between anchors 1 and 2: bronze dagger-axe, reflex bow; the war chariot just arriving.

armor.note: Between 1 and 2: leather armour and shields, bronze helmets for elites.

ships.note: Anchor 1: river boats only.

fortification.note: Between 1 and 2: rammed-earth city walls (Zhengzhou, Yanshi); Yinxu itself unwalled.

logistics.note: Between 1 and 2: state granaries, carriers, river transport.

communications.note: Between 1 and 2: reporting network of boats, chariots, runners and drums (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Shang_dynasty).

isr.note: Between 1 and 2: reconnaissance and divination.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: China 1000 CE = 1,225 (2011 int$), the earliest Chinese value; Bronze Age millet agriculture with stone and wooden tools scaled down by ~40%.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Royal bronze foundries produced weapons and chariot fittings; frequent campaigns.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Large bronze, bone and jade workshops at Yinxu; agrarian base.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Millet and wheat farming on the North China loess plain.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). roadKm.note: Educated guess. No engineered road system attested.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. River landings only.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. River boats.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Short-range campaigns from the capital region.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, pigs used for transport little; horses rare until the chariot.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: home plain, local supply; capital unwalled.

shang--1250.notes: Snapshot = c. 1250 BCE, Wu Ding's reign at Yinxu. The chariot-archetype doctrine overstates Shang chariot use: infantry with dagger-axes and bows dominated and chariots were few elite platforms. Army sizes come from oracle-bone muster figures as summarised by Sawyer; traditional texts (Shiji: 700,000 at Muye) are rejected. sierra-leone-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: Infobox 520,000 km2 in 1839; text: over 200,000 sq mi at its zenith (Amarpal Singh 2010, Barczewski 2016 p. 89, Khilnani 1972 p. 251, via the article). Low: the conservative 260,124 km2 the article cites; Lafont 2003 gives 390,000 km2. High: the world_1800 Sikhs polygon (about 526,000 km2 on the sphere), which covers Lahore, Peshawar and Kashmir; no later basemap draws the Sikh state.

population.note: Mid: about 12 million (Pashaura Singh, The Encyclopedia of Empire 2016, via the article). Low: about 5.35 million in 1838 (Herrli, The Coins of the Sikhs p. 10). High: 15 million (Lafont 2003 p. 131). Amarinder Singh 2010 p. 23 gives 3.5 million for 1831, so the estimates span a factor of four; no census was taken. Cross-check: OWID Pakistan 1840 = 14.6M for all of modern Pakistan, which includes Sindh and Baluchistan outside the empire.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: Lahore, Amritsar, Multan, Peshawar, Srinagar and Jammu were large trading and garrison towns in an agrarian province; no city counts were found for the 1840s. Close to the Maratha 1760 snapshot (0.09).

activePersonnel.note: Standing Khalsa army in late 1845. Mid: Amarpal Singh's breakdown (Sidhu 2010 p. 36, via the article) 53,576 regular infantry + 6,235 regular cavalry + 16,292 irregular cavalry + 10,698 gunners = 86,801. Low: over 80,000 in 1845 (Hernon 2003 p. 547). High: Smith 2019 pp. 45-50 gives about 153,000 regular and irregular, of which 55,000 jagirdari levies (counted as trainedReserves), leaving about 98,000.

trainedReserves.note: Jagirdari fauj (feudal levies of the jagirdars, raised on call): 55,000 (Smith 2019 pp. 45-50, via the article) (high); the Sikh Khalsa Army article gives 50,000-52,000 irregulars for 1838-39 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_Khalsa_Army). Fort garrisons (Fauj-i-Kilajat, 50-250 men per fort) are not counted; no total was found.

supportPersonnel.note: 10,698 gunners (Amarpal Singh, Sidhu 2010 p. 36, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Anglo-Sikh_War) plus a few hundred engineers and staff; high adds elephant, camel and bullock drivers of the gun train (educated guess, no count found).

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: Mughal Empire 1690 and Maratha 1760 snapshots, Barua 2005 p. 47 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire: the armed peasantry of the north Indian military labour market was about 3% of the population. Low 0.02, high 0.035 as in those snapshots.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Fauj-i-Ain regular infantry battalions (about 800 men each, drilled on French and British lines): 53,576 in 1845 (Amarpal Singh, Sidhu 2010 p. 36, via the article). Low: 45,000 in 1838-39 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_Khalsa_Army, uncited there). Smith 2019 puts the whole Fauj-i-Ain (infantry, cavalry, artillery) at 70,000.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: smoothbore flintlock muskets on the British pattern, made in Punjab arsenals; level with East India Company sepoys, behind percussion and rifled arms.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75 (professional standing army). Evidence: long-service paid regulars drilled by Ventura, Allard and Court in battalions and brigades since the 1820s.

count.note: Regular cavalry (dragoons, lancers and Allard's cuirassiers): 6,235 in 1845 (Smith 2019 pp. 45-50 and Sidhu 2010 p. 36, via the article). High: 10,000 regular cavalry in 1838-39 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_Khalsa_Army).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: European-style sabres, lances and carbines; smaller horses than British dragoons.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: drilled regulars, but the cavalry was the weak arm of the Khalsa and did little at Mudki and Ferozeshah.

count.note: Irregular cavalry (ghorchurras, Fauj-i-sowar): 16,292 (Amarpal Singh, Sidhu 2010 p. 36) to 22,000 (Smith 2019 pp. 45-50), both via the article.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: own horses and mixed arms (matchlocks, swords, lances).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: experienced horsemen of the misl tradition, not drilled in formation.

count.note: 381 guns plus 388 swivel guns (zamburaks) in 1845 (Smith 2019 pp. 45-50, via the article); swivel guns are not counted as pieces. Low: 182 heavy guns, 20 howitzers and 60 light guns in 1838-39 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_Khalsa_Army). The British took 69 guns in the four battles of the war (infobox).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era's best). Evidence: Lahore-cast guns, many of heavier calibre than the British horse and field batteries they faced at Ferozeshah and Sobraon.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: gunners trained under Court and Gardner; accurate fire at Mudki and Ferozeshah.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: after Ranjit Singh's death (1839) the army was run by regimental panchayats; the commanders Lal Singh and Tej Singh failed to press the advantage at Ferozeshah and are widely held to have betrayed it.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75 (professional with strong unit identity). Evidence: Khalsa religious and regimental identity; the Sobraon entrenchment held until it was overrun.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: army that forced the war on the Durbar and crossed the Sutlej in December 1845; offset by pay arrears and distrust of its own commanders.

weapons.note: Anchor: 6 (1805, flintlock musket, 12-pdr gun). Evidence: flintlock muskets and smoothbore field and siege guns; no percussion or rifled arms in quantity.

armor.note: Anchor: 5-6 (half-armour to none/cuirass). Evidence: Allard's cuirassiers and some mail in the irregular horse; infantry unarmoured.

ships.note: Anchor: 3-4 (oared river craft). Evidence: river boats and ferries on the Indus and the five rivers only; no warships.

fortification.note: Anchor: 5 (trace italienne) to 6 (Vauban-type). Evidence: Lahore and Multan forts, Mughal-era walled towns, field entrenchments at Ferozeshah and Sobraon.

logistics.note: Anchor: 5 (magazines). Evidence: arsenals and magazines at Lahore; elephant, camel, horse and ox draught for the guns; no railway.

communications.note: Anchor: 5 (couriers). Evidence: mounted couriers and newswriters; no telegraph in Punjab.

isr.note: Anchor: 5. Evidence: irregular-cavalry scouting and spies.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 India 1841 = 944, 1850 = 947 (2011 int$). Punjab has no own series (Pakistan starts 1950); the India value is used, band about +/-10%.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. State revenue in 1844 was about Rs 3.49 crore (land revenue 3.25 crore incl. 0.95 crore of jagirs, customs 0.24 crore; Cunningham 1849 p. 424, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_Empire), and the paid Khalsa took most of the treasury's cash; the share of output is not documented.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Textiles (Kashmir shawls), arms and craft production; the Maratha 1760 snapshot's 0.15 (Mughal-era structure, Moosvi 18% for the 16th century) assumed.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Inundation-canal and well-irrigated grain farming of the doabs; the army was fed from local markets.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. The Mughal imperial road (Grand Trunk route) Lahore-Attock-Peshawar and the Lahore-Multan road; the rest were unmetalled tracks.

railKm.note: The first passenger railway in India ran in 1853 (Bombay-Thane, 34 km); none existed in Punjab in 1845.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: landlocked; Indus river landings only (Sindh and Karachi were British from 1843).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: no seagoing merchant fleet.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. A magazine-supplied regular army with a heavy gun train, operating close to its own frontier on the Sutlej.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess, about 5% of the population (Maratha 1760 snapshot ratio ~6.7%): plough bullocks, camels, horses and the army's gun elephants.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: familiar terrain, local supply and fortified Lahore and Multan; a ruling Sikh minority over a mostly Muslim population limits population support, so below the full 1.2 row.

sikh-empire-1845.notes: Snapshot = December 1845, when the Khalsa crossed the Sutlej and the First Anglo-Sikh War began. Personnel: the paid Fauj-i-Ain regulars (infantry, regular cavalry, artillery) and the irregular ghorchurra cavalry are activePersonnel; jagirdari levies are trainedReserves; fort garrisons are not counted. Army figures via the First Anglo-Sikh War article (Smith 2019, Sidhu 2010/Amarpal Singh, Hernon 2003); the sources differ by 10-20% and the 1838-39 figures of the Sikh Khalsa Army article are uncited there. Population is the weakest value: estimates run from 3.5 million (1831) to 15 million, mid 12 million. Territory = everything inside the world_1800 Sikhs polygon (Punjab, Multan, Peshawar, Kashmir, Jammu); includes is empty. Economy and logistics values other than GDP per capita are educated guesses.

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 725 km2 (World Bank AG.LND.TOTL.K2); high adds ~3% for inland water.

population.note: asOf 2025: 6,111,175 (World Bank). Range allows for 2026 change.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 as quoted: 51,000 active; CIA Factbook 2025 ~55,000. High counts ~20,000 more full-time NSmen in training at any time (educated).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 252,500 reserves (Operationally Ready NSmen, trained annually); high adds MINDEF-cited ~312,500 total (educated).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 51,000 minus infantry P roles 19,000 = 32,000. Air Force (~13,500), Navy (~9,000), armour/artillery/signals, logistics.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Universal male National Service (2 years) and reservist liability to age 40-50; a full call-up raises ~300,000 within days. 8% is ~490,000.

count.note: Educated guess. Active army ~37,000 (mostly full-time NSmen) with infantry battalions; NSmen battalions form the bulk on mobilisation. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore_Armed_Forces)

Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 853,074,881,927 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 682,886,442,983 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SGP/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 3.05% of GDP in 2025. Factbook: 3.0% (2024).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 22.7% of GDP (World Bank).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SGP/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 0.10% (2025). s ~0.05 (0.03-0.10): local shares 2024 eggs ~34%, vegetables ~3%, seafood ~6% (https://www.sfa.gov.sg/news-publications/newsroom/singapore-food-statistics-2024). Mid 1 - 0.001/0.05 = 0.98. Low: a x 1.5, s 0.03 = 0.95. High: s 0.10 = 0.99. The value is a share, not a quantity: production is tiny. Import dependence: over 90% of food imported. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.98, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 3,156,466 x share of males aged 15-19 5.297% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 33,441. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 2,233,000-2,367,000 km2 for 1100 (mid 2.3M); the world_1100 Song Empire polygon measures 3.0 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1100.geojson, high); the Song dynasty infobox gives 2.1 million for 1127.

population.note: The Northern Song census recorded 20 million households; an estimated 90 million people (Song dynasty page); infobox 80-110 million for the 1120s (Chaffee 2015). HYDE China 1100 = 90.2M (OWID). Seshat codes 60-100M. Mid 95M for 1100.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Kaifeng ~1,000,000 (Seshat 425); Hangzhou and many large commercial towns.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. The army had 378,000 men in 960, about 1,000,000 by 1022 and well over 1,250,000 by 1041 (Ebrey, Gernet via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_Song_dynasty; high). Wang Anshi's reforms of the 1070s aimed to cut the standing army; the 1100 total is not documented in fetched sources, so mid 900,000 is a guess below the 1041 peak.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Baojia militia: 19-30% of households in Kaifeng, Hebei, Hedong and Shaanxi were drilled (Smith 2006 via the New Policies page).

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Ship and trebuchet crews, armory and transport troops, staff. Prefectural (xiangjun) labour troops are partly here.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Mercenary standing army recruited from the poor plus baojia militia; total war on the scale of 1126-1141 drew a few percent.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Crossbowmen and archers: an infantry company had 8 swordsmen, 16 spearmen and 70+ crossbowmen (Smith 2015 via the Military history of the Song page), i.e. ~75% missile troops.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: mass-produced crossbows; a 1068 crossbow pierced a tree at 140 paces

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mercenary regulars of uneven quality

count.note: Educated guess. Sword and spear infantry, ~25% of companies.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 32,000 suits of iron armour a year from the Kaifeng armories (Chaffee 2015)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mercenary regulars

count.note: Educated guess. Salaried tribal auxiliaries (fanbing) on the northwest frontier.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: militia

count.note: Educated guess. Horse archers; chronic horse shortage: 150,000 state horses under Shenzong against 700,000 at the Tang height (Military history of the Song page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: few and poor horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regulars

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured lancers; a cavalry company had 13 spear and flag men and 80+ archers (Smith 2015), so true shock cavalry was scarce.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: good armour, poor horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: regulars

count.note: Educated guess. Traction trebuchets in sixteen known varieties (Gernet via the Military history of the Song page); city walls and arsenals held many.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: largest traction trebuchets of the era, incendiary and early gunpowder projectiles (100,000 and 250,000 gunpowder arrows sent to two garrisons in 1083, Andrade 2016)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: specialist crews

count.note: Educated guess. River war junks and paddle-wheel boats; the permanent navy came only in 1132.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: compass, watertight bulkheads

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: no standing navy yet

count.note: Educated guess. Patrol and transport craft on the rivers and canals; in 1090 the Mingzhou/Wenzhou yards were tasked with 600 ships a year and Liangzhe/Huainan with 300 (Schottenhammer 2015), mostly transports.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: era-typical

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mixed

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: civil control of generals by design, frequent rotation; costly defeats by the Xi Xia (1040s, 1081-82)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mercenary recruits from the destitute, low social standing of soldiers

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: long peace with the Liao since 1005, poor record against the Xi Xia

weapons.note: Anchor: 4 (1250: crossbow, trebuchet). Evidence: mass crossbows, traction trebuchets, gunpowder arrows and bombs (Wujing Zongyao 1044) audit 2026-10-30: mid 4.0 -> 3.9, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1100 (3.903); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

armor.note: Anchor: about 4. Evidence: mass-produced iron lamellar

ships.note: Anchor: about 4 (galleys, cogs). Evidence: compass navigation, watertight bulkheads, paddle-wheel warships

fortification.note: Anchor: 4. Evidence: Hebei water-and-polder defences, multi-wall cities audit 2026-10-30: mid 4.0 -> 3.9, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1100 (3.903); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

logistics.note: Anchor: 4 (river transport, granaries). Evidence: Grand Canal, state granaries, camel/horse/porter ration tables (Chaffee 2015) audit 2026-10-30: mid 4.0 -> 3.9, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1100 (3.903); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

communications.note: Anchor: about 4. Evidence: post-relay system, printed manuals

isr.note: Anchor: between 3 and 4. Evidence: frontier watch posts; little deep scouting for lack of cavalry

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 China 1090 = 1,222 (mid) and 1150 = 1,181. Range is the usual uncertainty of the series.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. The military consumed three-quarters of state revenue (Ebrey via the Military history of the Song page); with state revenue at roughly 8-15% of GDP this is ~6-11%.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Iron, ceramics, silk, printing; the most commercialised economy of the era.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Champa rice and Yangtze delta agriculture.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Post roads; canals carried most bulk.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Guangzhou, Quanzhou, Mingzhou, Hangzhou, Mizhou.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.25 -> 0.95. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ZAF/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 5.41% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.00 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.97-1.03). Mid 1 - 0.054/1.00 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.97 = 0.93. High: s 1.03 = 0.95. Net exporter: production is about 100% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net exporter of maize, fruit and wine; commercial farming sector. Not from FAO balance sheets.

south-korea-1950.notes: Snapshot date 25 June 1950 (KPA invasion). Territory and population: the ROK south of the 38th parallel (border ref hb:1945:Korea (USA), the nearest basemap at or before 1950). activePersonnel = ROK armed forces 105,752 per the ROK MND Institute for Military History (fetched via web.archive.org, 1K29.pdf, compiling the 2004 official history); US Military Advisory Group (KMAG, ~500 men) and the National Police are excluded. The ROK had no tanks and no combat aircraft (20-22 trainers and liaison aircraft only), so those roles are omitted; aircraft counts are in the notes only. All equipment was US-supplied; no domestic arms production, production empty. Appleman (CMH) could not be fetched (HTTP 403; archive.org copy lending-only), so the M8 count is an educated guess. Weakest numbers: infantry share of the army, trained reserves and logistics infrastructure (educated guesses).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.82. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/KOR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 5.10% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.29 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.28-0.29). Mid 1 - 0.051/0.29 = 0.82. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.28 = 0.76. High: s 0.29 = 0.82. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 29% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Food self-sufficiency ~45%; rice self-sufficient, imports grain/feed.

areaKm2.note: world_1530 polygons on the sphere: Spain 490,467 + Habsburg Netherlands 61,054 + Naples 68,817 + Sicily 24,017 + Sardinia 21,927 + Milan 26,972 = 693,254 km2. The Netherlands polygon covers all 17 provinces, half of which were in revolt; low subtracts the rebel north. Americas and Portugal excluded.

population.note: Crowns of Castile and Aragon ~8.1M (HYDE via OWID population.csv: Spain 6.5M in 1500, 8.5M in 1600, interpolated; https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) + Kingdom of Naples ~3.0M, Sicily ~1.0M, Duchy of Milan ~1.1M, Sardinia ~0.25M + the Netherlands provinces under royal control in 1580 (~1.5M of ~3M). Portugal (conquered Aug 1580) and the American viceroyalties are excluded. Low drops half the Netherlands and uses lower Italian figures.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share (de Vries based): Spain 13.8% (1500), 17.1% (1600); Italy 18.4% (1600); Belgium ~29%. Bairoch 5,000+ convention runs a little higher; mid 16%.

activePersonnel.note: Salaried forces under arms in 1580: Army of Flanders ~30,000-45,000 after the 1577-79 withdrawal of the Spanish tercios (Dutch States Army article: Parma had 93 infantry companies in late 1579; Army of Flanders peaked at 86,000 paper in 1574 and 63,455 effectives in 1588), Alba's army for Portugal ~35,000-40,000, Italian garrisons of Milan, Naples and Sicily ~15,000-20,000, North African presidios and Spanish guards ~8,000, galley infantry and crews ~10,000-15,000. Parker (Military Revolution p. 24, quoted at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Revolution) gives ~200,000 paper for the Spanish Monarchy in the 1590s; effective is lower.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Neapolitan and Sicilian militia (battaglione) and Castilian urban and seigneurial levies callable within a month; the general Castilian militia was only organised in 1590-98.

supportPersonnel.note: Galley sailors and gunners (~100 galleys x ~60-80 non-rowing seamen = 6,000-8,000), artillery trains and engineers (~2,000), Atlantic squadron crews (~3,000), administration and staffs. Galley oarsmen (convicts, slaves, buonavoglia, ~20,000) are not counted as military personnel.

mobilizationRatio.note: Parker: Philip IV claimed 300,000 regulars and 500,000 militia (paper) in 1625 for a monarchy of ~20M (Military Revolution article); real wartime peaks under Philip II ~200,000 incl. foreign mercenaries, i.e. ~3-5% of the subject population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Tercios and regiments of Spanish, Italian, Walloon and German pike and shot (Army of Flanders infantry; Alba's Portuguese army ~20,000 Spanish/Italian/German foot; Italian garrisons). Reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: arquebus and heavy musket (introduced by Alba 1567) with pike; best infantry kit of the 1580s

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: veteran Spanish tercios the best infantry of the era (Parker, Army of Flanders); Walloon and German regiments weaker

count.note: Lancers and men-at-arms of the Guardas de Castilla and Italian companies; the Army of Flanders discharged its heavy cavalry in 1572 (Army of Flanders article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: lance and plate, being replaced by pistol-armed cuirassiers elsewhere

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional companies

count.note: Light horse, mounted arquebusiers and herreruelos; the Army of Flanders cavalry was mainly light cavalry until the 1630s (Army of Flanders article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical light horse; chronic horse shortage in Flanders

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: professional but small arm

count.note: Educated guess: field pieces with the Army of Flanders and Alba's Portuguese campaign plus Italian trains; fortress guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Spanish foundries at Malaga and Mechelen, standardised calibres under Philip II

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: contract gunners

Atlantic galleons were few before the Portuguese fleet was taken over.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Mediterranean galleys with bow batteries, the Lepanto-winning type

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: veteran galley squadrons of Naples and Sicily

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mixed

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders). Evidence: Alba (Portugal 1580) and Alessandro Farnese of Parma, the era's leading generals; Council of War administration; slow centralised decision making from Madrid

armor.note: Anchor: 5 (half-armor, cuirass). Evidence: morion and corselet for pikemen

ships.note: Anchor: 5 (galleons, ships of the line) vs 4 (galleys). Evidence: Mediterranean galley fleet, first Atlantic galleons; 1580 is before the galleon squadrons of the 1588 Armada

logistics.note: Anchor: 4.7 between river transport and magazines. Evidence: the Spanish Road and its etapas (Parker, Army of Flanders) were the first planned military supply corridor

communications.note: Anchor: 4.8 between relay horses and early postal. Evidence: Taxis imperial postal service Madrid-Brussels; dispatches ~2 weeks

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Castilian textiles (Segovia, Toledo), Basque iron and Milanese and Flemish crafts; agrarian economy ~70% of output.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: Castile imported Sicilian and Baltic grain in bad years; Sicily and Apulia were grain exporters.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. The Spanish Road etapas supplied marching tercios over 1,000 km from Milan to Flanders. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: mules dominated Castilian transport; horses, oxen across 15M people.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row in Iberia and Italy (fortified cities, familiar terrain, popular support); 1.1 or less in the rebel Netherlands.

spain-1580.notes: Snapshot = 1580, the year of the conquest of Portugal (Alba enters Lisbon Aug 1580), before the Portuguese fleet and empire are merged. Population and forces: Castile, Aragon, the Italian possessions (Naples, Sicily, Milan, Sardinia) and the royal-controlled Netherlands; Portugal and the Americas are excluded (Americas as bases only). Personnel convention: salaried troops (Army of Flanders, Italian garrisons, presidios, Alba's army, galley infantry) are active; Italian and Castilian militia are trainedReserves. Army of Flanders strength in 1580 is uncertain because the Spanish tercios had left in 1577-78 and returned in 1582. Parker's paper figures (Military Revolution) are wartime ceilings, not effectives.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.25 -> 0.95. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 3.37% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.63 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.55-0.74). Mid 1 - 0.034/0.63 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.55 = 0.91. High: s 0.74 = 0.95. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 63% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess: large net exporter of fruit, vegetables, olive oil and pork but imports feed grain; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

spain-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:ESP (peninsula, Balearics, Canaries, Ceuta, Melilla); World Bank figures. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from IISS Military Balance 2025 as quoted on Wikipedia, Wikipedia inventory tables (World Air Forces 2025), and the active-ships list; ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = LPD/LSD, corvettes, OPVs, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). basesAbroad empty: Spain has no permanent overseas bases; ~3,000 troops deployed on EU/NATO/UN missions (CIA Factbook 2025). Guardia Civil (87,450) is paramilitary and excluded. US Naval Station Rota and Moron Air Base are on Spanish soil but belong to the US basing network.

areaKm2.note: Laconia + Messenia ~8,500 km2 (Cartledge, Sparta and Lakonia, 2nd ed., intro/ch. 1; not fetched, figure from memory of the book, hence grade C). audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: figure from memory, not read from a fetched source.

population.note: HELOTS INCLUDED. Cartledge, Agesilaos and the Crisis of Sparta (1987) p. 174: helots of both sexes 170,000-224,000. Spartiates: Herodotus 7.234 (Demaratus) gives ~8,000 adult men in 480, i.e. ~25,000-30,000 persons with families (x3.5, Hansen 2006 ratio of adult males to all citizens). Perioikoi: educated guess 30,000-60,000 (they fielded 5,000 hoplites at Plataea). Older helot estimates span a wider range (Figueira 2003, in Luraghi & Alcock, Helots and their Masters, tabulates them; not fetched). Grade C: no census. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

urbanization.note: Educated guess: Sparta was an unwalled cluster of five villages holding the Spartiates; helots and most perioikoi lived on the land.

activePersonnel.note: Hoplites (10,000) + helot light troops (20,000) + fleet crews (3,200).

trainedReserves.note: 8,000 Spartiates (Herodotus 7.234) less the 5,000 sent to Plataea (Herodotus 9.10): the older and younger year classes kept at home.

supportPersonnel.note: Trireme crews: 10-20 ships x ~200 (perioikoi and helots).

mobilizationRatio.note: At Plataea (479) Sparta fielded 5,000 Spartiates + 5,000 perioikic hoplites + 35,000 helots (Herodotus 9.10-11, 9.28; ancient figure) = 45,000, ~18% of a 250,000 population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Spartiate hoplites (5,000 at Plataea, Herodotus 9.10; 8,000 adult Spartiates per 7.234) + perioikic hoplites (5,000 at Plataea, 9.11). Modest figures accepted by Lazenby 1993; ancient source, hence C. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

sparta--480.notes: Snapshot = 480 BCE (Thermopylae, Salamis). Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SDN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 39.77% (2022). s proxied by cereal self-sufficiency (sorghum, millet, wheat are the staples): 2025 cereal output 5.2 Mt, 22% below 2024, and 2026 import requirement 2.8 Mt (FAO GIEWS, https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=SDN&lang=en): s = 5.2/8.0 = 0.65. Mid 1 - 0.398/0.65 = 0.39. Low: a x 1.2, s 0.60 (2026 drought) = 0.2. High: s 0.70 (2024 output 6.67 Mt, same imports) = 0.44. a is 2022, the latest World Bank year. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 65% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. sudan-2026.notes: WARTIME snapshot (civil war since 15 April 2023), asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. This snapshot represents the internationally recognised state and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF, led by Gen. al-Burhan) with the forces fighting under it. The Rapid Support Forces (RSF, Gen. Hemedti), a paramilitary created in 2013 that turned on the SAF, hold most of Darfur (El Fasher fell Oct 2025) and parts of Kordofan and declared a rival "Government of Peace and Unity" (2025); RSF manpower (100,000+ pre-war) and equipment are excluded and would need their own snapshot. The SAF retook Khartoum in March 2025. Population convention: whole internationally recognised territory (World Bank), although roughly a third is RSF-held; displacement exceeds 10 million. All equipment counts are pre-war IISS-derived or delivery-based figures discounted for unknown losses (grade C/D). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-25%). milSpendShare low = last peacetime figure, mid = wartime educated guess. Doctrine archetype-insurgent because irregular and militia forces dominate both sides of the fighting. UN arms embargo on Darfur since 2005.

sweden-1632.notes: Snapshot = 1632, Gustavus Adolphus in Germany (Alte Veste, Lutzen). Population counts Sweden proper, Finland, Estonia, Livonia and Ingria; occupied German lands excluded. Personnel convention: all regiments in Swedish pay (native conscripts and German/Scottish mercenaries) are active because they were salaried and under arms; allied armies (Saxony, Brandenburg, Hesse) are excluded; the next levy and the lantvarn are trainedReserves. This makes active larger than a native mobilization ratio would allow, so mobilizationRatio includes the subsidised mercenary market (stated there). The 140,000-150,000 headline totals are paper strengths mixing Swedish-paid and allied forces.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.98. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SWE/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.77% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.76 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.70-0.80). Mid 1 - 0.018/0.76 = 0.98. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.70 = 0.96. High: s 0.80 = 0.98. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 76% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Roughly self-sufficient in cereals and dairy; imports fruit/vegetables.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CHE/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 2.24% (2025). s = 0.46 (net self-sufficiency 2022, https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/lebensmittelproduktion-so-steht-es-um-die-selbstversorgung-der-schweiz). Mid 1 - 0.0224/0.46 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.5, s 0.42 = 0.92. High: s 0.50 (gross rate is higher than net) = 0.96. Import dependence: about half of calories imported; compulsory stockpiles. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.95, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.03 -> 0.73. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SYR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 16.30% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.59 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.53-0.69). Mid 1 - 0.163/0.59 = 0.73. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.53 = 0.6. High: s 0.69 = 0.76. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 59% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Wheat output collapsed by drought (2025) and war; WFP food aid ongoing.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share (proxy: agricultural employment share), s = calorie self-sufficiency. taiwan-2026.notes: Modern snapshot asOf mid-2026. Taiwan is not in World Bank data: population from the Ministry of the Interior (June 2026), GDP from the CIA Factbook PPP series rolled forward with DGBAS growth (grade C), urbanisation/area/rail/ports from the CIA Factbook. Population convention: Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu (ne:TWN polygon may not include Kinmen/Matsu). Doctrine: archetype-modern-small-state, because the doctrine profile names Taiwan's newer whole-of-society/asymmetric concept explicitly, although Taiwan's force is larger than most small states. Counts from Wikipedia ROC Army equipment list (IISS 2024/2026 as quoted for several lines), ROC Navy ship list, ROCAF article; fighter count is a composite (grade C). Personnel sources disagree (IISS 170,600 vs 230,000 incl. conscripts). US weapons backlog (F-16 Block 70, Harpoon CDS, MQ-9B) means 2026-27 strength will rise.

tang-750.notes: Snapshot 750, five years before the An Lushan rebellion and one year before Talas. Census figures are registered persons; the mid allows for under-registration. Army: Benn's ~500,000 for 742 is the anchor; the frequently quoted 490,000 frontier troops and 80,000 horses of 742 could not be fetched and is not used. Border: world_700 is the nearest file at or before 750; its China polygon is mislabelled "Sui Empire" and is used as is. Population convention: registered Tang subjects plus the under-registration allowance; protectorates in the Tarim count in territory but add little population. Doctrine archetype-feudal-host per the coverage plan, although the Tang army was a professional standing force. Personnel: active = professional frontier armies, capital guards and fubing units on rotation; trainedReserves = fubing men off duty and nomad allies; mobilizable = population x ratio.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.36. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/TZA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 64.57% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.01 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.99-1.03). commandQuality.note: Rubric 1.0: Timur never lost a major battle (Kondurcha 1391, Terek 1395, Delhi 1398, Ankara 1402); best-in-era.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: loyalty to Timur personally; tribal amirs reorganised under his household (Manz), fragile without him.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: thirty years of victories and plunder.

weapons.note: Anchor 4 plus: composite bow, counterweight trebuchet, naphtha; little gunpowder artillery.

armor.note: Anchor 4: lamellar, mail and brigandine.

ships.note: Anchor 1-2: river craft only; no navy.

fortification.note: Anchor 4 minus: walled Samarkand and Herat citadels, little new building.

logistics.note: Anchor 4 plus: herds and remounts gave strategic reach from Delhi to Ankara.

communications.note: Anchor 4: yam-type relay stations.

isr.note: Anchor 4 plus: merchants and spies ahead of every campaign.

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) Iraq 1150 = 1,084, Iran 1 CE = 1,116, Turkey 1348 = 743 (2011 int$). Plunder from Delhi, Persia and Syria flowed to Samarkand.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A state organised around permanent campaigning.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Deported artisans in Samarkand, textiles, metalwork.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Oasis irrigation and pastoralism; Iran's agriculture damaged by the conquests.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Caravan routes of the Silk Road; few engineered roads.

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Persian Gulf ports via vassal Hormuz; Caspian landings.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. No merchant marine of its own.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Herds and remounts let armies range far beyond bases where pasture existed; Timur campaigned 2,000+ km from Samarkand. Comparable to mongol-empire-1241.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (several remounts per rider), camels and oxen.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: steppe and desert depth and a harsh continental climate around Transoxiana; conquered Iran gives less.

timurid-empire-1400.notes: Snapshot = 1400, Timur's invasion of Syria (Aleppo, Damascus) between Delhi (1398) and Ankara (1402). Army size anchored on Nicolle's 140,000 at Ankara (an Osprey-level source, so grade C); Manz (The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane, 1989) describes the army's tribal structure but no total was found to quote. Chronicle figures (Ibn Arabshah 800,000; a German witness 1.6 million) rejected (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ankara). Population convention: directly ruled Transoxiana, Khwarazm, Khurasan, Iran, Iraq and the southern Caucasus; vassal Georgia, Delhi and the Golden Horde excluded. Population is the weakest number: HYDE (~11M) and Seshat (49M) disagree by a factor of four.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/TGO/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 37.59% (2025). s = 1 assumed: no self-sufficiency figure is fetched for auto-base states, which overstates the value for a net food importer. togo-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 295,000 km2 for 1603-1868 (Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu; Ezo excluded). The world_1600 polygon measures ~280,000 km2.

population.note: OWID/HYDE Japan 1600 = 17.0M (mid); Seshat codes 22M for 1603 (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/152) (high). Farris argues for lower 1600 totals (~15-17M); low 14M allows for that.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Kyoto, Osaka, Sakai and castle towns; Edo still small in 1600 (Seshat: 570,000 only by 1678).

activePersonnel.note: Sekigahara (21 Oct 1600): Eastern Army 75,000-89,000, Western Army 82,000-120,000 (Davis 1999, Bryant 1995, via the article), plus 38,000 under Hidetada at Ueda, 15,000 Western troops at Otsu and the Tohoku and Kyushu campaigns. The Korea invasions used 158,800 men in 1592 and ~320,000 over the war (Hawley, Strauss via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imjin_War). Counts samurai retainers and ashigaru, hereditary and stipended.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Rural jizamurai and temple forces partly disarmed by the 1588 sword hunt; retainers of daimyo not under arms.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Porters, labourers, sailors and engineers; the 1592 total of 158,800 included labourers and sailors (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imjin_War).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Hideyoshi's quotas set men per 100 koku of assessed land; Shimazu's quota is preserved (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imjin_War).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Ashigaru arquebusiers and pikemen plus samurai on foot, the bulk of the 1600 armies.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: veterans of the Sengoku wars and Korea.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5.

count.note: 300 warships in 1592 and 1,000 ships (some with cannon) in 1597 (Hawley 2005 pp. 116, 446 via the article); 450 lost in the war (Turnbull 2002 p. 227). Sekibune and kobaya counted here.

armor.note: Anchor 5: tosei gusoku plate armour, some bullet-tested.

ships.note: Anchor 4: atakebune and sekibune, few cannon.

fortification.note: Anchor 5 minus: Azuchi-Momoyama castles on high stone bases (Osaka, Fushimi), no bastioned trace.

logistics.note: Anchor 4-5: Hideyoshi's supply organisation for Kyushu and Korea, coastal shipping.

communications.note: Anchor 4-5: couriers and relay horses.

isr.note: Anchor 4-5: scouts and shinobi.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A fully militarised society after a century of war; samurai stipends were most of daimyo revenue.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Silver mining (Iwami), swords and guns (Sakai, Kunitomo), textiles.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Rice tax in kind of ~40-50% of the crop.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Tokaido, Nakasendo and other trunk roads (formalised as the Five Routes from 1601).

railKm.note: No railways before 1825.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Sakai, Osaka, Hakata, Nagasaki, Hirado, Kagoshima.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Coastal shipping of the Inland Sea; red-seal ships to Southeast Asia from 1600.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Short campaigns along trunk roads; sea transport for Kyushu and Korea.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and oxen.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: island position, mountains, castles and an armed population against any landing.

tokugawa-japan-1600.notes: Snapshot = autumn 1600, the Sekigahara campaign (21 October 1600) that made Tokugawa Ieyasu master of Japan; the shogunate was formally founded in 1603. The snapshot counts all of Japan (both Sekigahara coalitions), as the polity Ieyasu ruled after the battle. Personnel convention: samurai retainers and ashigaru of the daimyo are activePersonnel (hereditary and stipended); disarmed rural fighters are trainedReserves. Battle figures via the Battle of Sekigahara article (Davis, Bryant, Turnbull); Farris and Berry not consulted directly. Population convention: Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and islands; Ezo (Hokkaido) and Ryukyu excluded.

Weakest values: the P-role split, APC and artillery counts, AA batteries (composite), roads in 1974 and animals (educated guesses or later-year bounds). foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.2 -> 0.82. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/TUR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 14.22% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.77 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.73-0.80). Mid 1 - 0.142/0.77 = 0.82. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.73 = 0.75. High: s 0.80 = 0.82. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 77% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Near self-sufficient; large fruit/vegetable/flour exporter, imports grain.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.4 -> 0.94. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/UKR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 14.12% (2021). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 2.18 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.94-2.32). Mid 1 - 0.141/2.18 = 0.94. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.94 = 0.91. High: s 2.32 = 0.94. Net exporter: production is about 218% of domestic calorie supply. World Bank series for Ukraine stops at 2021 (pre-invasion); occupation and mined fields since then cut output, not captured in s. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Large grain and oilseed exporter even in war (Black Sea corridor); output down vs 2021.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.94. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ARE/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.44% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.26 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.22-0.33). Mid 1 - 0.014/0.26 = 0.94. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.22 = 0.9. High: s 0.33 = 0.96. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 26% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports ~90% of food.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, United Kingdom agriculture share of employment 1911 = 11.8%, 1920 = 8.6%. s: "Before the War about 60 percent of the energy value of the British diet was derived from foodstuffs that were imported" (Gazeley and Newell 2010, IZA DP 5297, p. 11, https://repec.iza.org/dp5297.pdf); 58% of calories in 1913 (Offer, as summarised in https://www.habselstree.org.uk/boys/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2024/06/OP65StJohnFoodSupplyandWorldWarOne.pdf); 64% (https://shipwreckedmariners.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Why-Britain-Wasnt-Starved-into-Surrender-in-WW1.pdf). Mid 1 - 0.118/0.40 = 0.70. Low a 0.125, s 0.36 = 0.65; high a 0.11, s 0.42 = 0.74. Grade C: two sources combined. Import dependence: ~60% of calories imported, four fifths of wheat. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.87/0.88/0.9 (s = 1 assumed); fetched s applied.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, United Kingdom agriculture share of employment 1935 = 6.8%, 1937 = 6.1%, 1938 = 5.9%. s: "At the beginning of the war Britain produced 33 percent of the calories its people consumed" (44% by 1945), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeding_Britain_in_the_Second_World_War. Mid 1 - 0.059/0.33 = 0.82. Low a 0.068, s 0.30 = 0.77; high a 0.055, s 0.36 = 0.85. Grade C: two sources combined. Import dependence: two thirds of calories imported (Harrison 1998: Britain relied heavily on imported food and fuels). audit 2026-10-30: was 0.0/0.0/0.02 (read as a trade balance); recomputed with the formula and the fetched s.

annualCohort.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 3(a): males aged 20-24, England and Wales 1,611k (est. June 1937), Scotland 210.2k, Northern Ireland 52.5k (1926) = 1,874k / 5 = ~375k per year.

draftAnimals.note: UK national horse stock 1.2M in 1930 (Rich and Wilson p. 653, table 59, via the cited page), declining through the 1930s with mechanisation. The army itself used very few horses.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified naval bases, strong population support; the Channel acts as a moat (high 1.3) though there is no strategic depth or harsh climate.

united-kingdom-1939.notes: Snapshot date 3 September 1939 (declaration of war). United Kingdom ONLY: home islands (Great Britain and Northern Ireland). includes is empty: forces, population and GDP of India, the Dominions and the colonies are NOT counted; Dominion warships (RAN, RCN, NZ Division) were subtracted from the naval-history.net totals. united-kingdom-1982.notes: Snapshot date April 1982: Argentina invaded the Falklands on 2 April, the task force sailed on 5 April, the war ended on 14 June 1982. British losses 255 killed, 2 Type 42 destroyers, 2 Type 21 frigates, 1 LSL, Atlantic Conveyor, 10 fighters, 24 helicopters. Population convention: UK only; dependencies excluded and listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = regular forces; reserves (regular reserve, TA, UDR, RNR, RAuxAF) = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles reconstructed from battalion counts; all else supportPersonnel. BAOR 55,000 and Berlin 3,100, RAF Germany 10,800, Hong Kong 7,100 and Cyprus garrisons were abroad and largely stayed in place during the war. united-kingdom-1989.notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-1990, data as at 1 June 1989), before the fall of the Berlin Wall and Options for Change (1990). Population convention: UK only (OWID); Hong Kong, Gibraltar, Falklands and other dependencies excluded, their garrisons listed as basesAbroad. Personnel: active = regular forces 311,650; TA, regular reserve, UDR and RN/RAF reserves = trainedReserves. Infantry P roles are reconstructed from battalion counts; everything else is supportPersonnel. Deployed abroad (MB 1989-90): FRG 69,700 (BAOR 55,700, Berlin 3,000, RAF Germany 11,000), Cyprus 3,900, Hong Kong 8,200, Falklands ~1,600, Belize 1,500, Gibraltar 1,800, Brunei ~900, so not all forces are at home on day one. The MB edition was read from a full-text transcription at samlib.ru (cited URL); the printed volume is Brassey's for IISS, 1989. Equipment in store is in high only. Weakest values: merchant tonnage, road length and wartime production rates (educated guesses).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.99. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/GBR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 0.85% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.69 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.67-0.70). Mid 1 - 0.009/0.69 = 0.99. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.67 = 0.98. High: s 0.70 = 0.99. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 69% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. UK imports ~40% of food; production mostly consumed domestically.

united-kingdom-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:GBR (World Bank); overseas territories and Crown dependencies excluded. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from Wikipedia inventory tables (British Army equipment list, active aircraft list with in-service/total columns, July 2026 active ships list) and IISS as quoted; ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = OPV, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). No ground-launched missiles; the Trident force is carried by the 4 SSBNs counted under submarines. Army in transition: Challenger 3, Boxer and Ajax replacing older fleets, AS-90 gone, so armour and artillery counts are unusually uncertain for 2026.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/URY/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 8.07% (2025). s = 1 assumed: no self-sufficiency figure is fetched for auto-base states, which overstates the value for a net food importer. Mid 1 - 0.081/1 = 0.92. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count) = 0.90. High: kept at mid (no s range).
