uruguay-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Argentine Republic, Federative Republic of Brazil, Republic of Chile, Republic of Colombia, Republic of Cuba, Republic of Peru, Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: The world_1815 "United States" polygon (5.53M km2 on the sphere) spans the contiguous US incl. the South, so the map overstates the Union and overlaps the Confederacy. Union area 1863 = contiguous US ~8.0M km2 minus the 11 seceded states ~1.95M = ~6.1M km2 incl. western territories.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1863 = 34,026k for the whole United States; 1860 census: free states ~18.9M, loyal slave states (MD, DE, KY, MO) ~2.6M, West Virginia ~0.38M, territories ~0.25M = ~22.1M in 1860, grown to ~23M by 1863. Excludes the 11 seceded states. audit 2026-10-30: grade B -> C: derived:snapshot-composite is at most C.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) United States 1860 = 19.8% (places of 2,500+); the free states were more urban (~25%) than the South.

activePersonnel.note: Livermore, Numbers and Losses (1900) p. 47: 918,121 on the Union army rolls on 1 January 1863 (present and absent). Union army page: ~700,000 peak present. Mid = present army ~700,000 plus ~34,000 in the navy; high = rolls plus navy.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: state militia callable for emergencies (Pennsylvania and New York militia in June-July 1863) and the first draftees of the March 1863 Enrollment Act.

supportPersonnel.note: Field and heavy artillery ~45,000, engineers, signal corps, quartermaster and medical ~20,000, navy ~34,000 in 1863 (84,415 served over the whole war, Union navy page). Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Union army page: 2,128,948 enlisted over the war (~9.6% of the Union population cumulatively); peak strength ~1.0M on the rolls in May 1865 (Livermore) = 4.4% at one time.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry present, all departments, mid-1863: ~80% of the ~700,000 present (Livermore's returns). Army of the Potomac at Gettysburg ~94,000 present.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Springfield and Enfield rifle-muskets; first Spencer repeaters

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: volunteer regiments, veteran by 1863, new regiments raw

count.note: Union cavalry present, mid-1863 (all US cavalry fought as mounted infantry and light horse; Brandy Station June 1863).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: breech-loading carbines (Sharps, Burnside), Spencers from 1863

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: improving after 1863 reorganisation under Pleasonton

count.note: Educated guess: field guns in ~400 light batteries; the Army of the Potomac had ~370 guns at Gettysburg.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Parrott rifles, 3-inch Ordnance rifles, 12-pdr Napoleons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Hunt's artillery reserve broke Pickett's Charge

count.note: Seagoing ironclads (Passaic-class monitors, New Ironsides, Roanoke) and screw frigates and sloops, mid-1863. The page: the fleet grew more than fifteen-fold to 671 vessels by 1865.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: turreted monitors with 15-inch Dahlgrens

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: expanded with merchant officers

count.note: Gunboats, converted steamers and river ironclads (Eads gunboats) of the blockading and Mississippi squadrons; the page gives 671 vessels at the end of the war; the mid-1863 count is interpolated.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: converted merchant steamers and purpose-built double-enders

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: blockade duty experience

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: Meade at Gettysburg, Grant at Vicksburg; uneven corps commanders; no general staff

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: state volunteer regiments with local identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Gettysburg and Vicksburg in July 1863 after Fredericksburg and Chancellorsville; draft riots

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: rifle-muskets, rifled artillery, early repeaters

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: no body armour; armoured trains and river ironclads

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: turret monitors, the first fleet of them audit 2026-10-30: mid 6.7 -> 6.58, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1863 (6.580); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Washington defences (~68 forts), field entrenchment

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: US Military Railroad, river steamers, 590 ocean-going chartered vessels (Union army page) audit 2026-10-30: mid 6.8 -> 6.58, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1863 (6.580); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: US Military Telegraph, signal corps flag and torch audit 2026-10-30: mid 6.7 -> 6.58, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1863 (6.580); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Union Army Balloon Corps (to August 1863), cavalry, Bureau of Military Information

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID) United States 1863 = 4,734 for the whole country; the free states had ~10-15% higher income per head than the national mean (Engerman), so the Union is put at ~5,200.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1860 = 7,060 (~0.8% of GNP, low), 1863 = 119,662 (~$580M). Against a Union GNP of ~$4.5bn that is ~13-15%.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: manufacturing about a fifth to a quarter of northern output in 1860.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: large grain exporter (wheat to Britain during the war).

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. Young population, the true share was probably at the high end.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field and siege guns per year from West Point Foundry, Fort Pitt, Watervliet and contractors.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: monitors and seagoing warships completed per year 1863-64.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: gunboats built or converted per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: turnpikes, plank and macadam roads in the northern states.

railKm.note: CHAT (https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) railline United States 1863 = 52,388 km; about 14,500 km (9,000 miles) lay in the Confederacy in 1861 (McPherson, isbn:0-19-503863-0, ch. 10), part of it Union-held by 1863.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Portsmouth NH, Hampton Roads, New Orleans, San Francisco, Port Royal, Key West.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 4,225k tons (United States 1863, incl. coastal, lake and river tonnage; flight from the flag reduced it during the war, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: armies tied to railheads and rivers, wagon trains beyond.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: about 70% of the 1860 US stock of ~6.2M horses and 1.1M mules.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 rows: familiar terrain and population support; Washington ringed with forts.

usa-1863.notes: Snapshot = the Union in July 1863 (Gettysburg, Vicksburg). Population = loyal states incl. Maryland, Delaware, Kentucky, Missouri, West Virginia and territories; the seceded states are the confederate-states snapshot; includes is empty. Border caveat: no basemap file separates the Union from the Confederacy; hb:1815:United States covers both and overlaps the confederate-states area. Personnel: army present and navy = active; militia and draftees = trainedReserves. Strengths from Livermore (1900, Internet Archive text) and the Union army and Union navy pages. Branch split and artillery count are reconstructions (grade C/D).

areaKm2.note: Contiguous United States ~7.84M km2 (B&H Table 1: 7.8M); the world_1914 United States polygon (incl. Alaska) computes to ~9.25M km2 (high).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1917 = 103,268k (high); OWID/HYDE 1917 = 99.55M (low); US Census Bureau estimate for 1917 ~103M (mid). Continental United States; territories (Philippines, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, 9.8M per B&H Table 1) excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share USA 1910 = 45.6%, 1920 = 51.2%; interpolated 1917 ~0.49. Low = COW upop/tpop 1917 = 25,310/103,268 = 0.25 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Coffman, The War to End All Wars ch. 1: on 1 April 1917 the Regular Army had ~127,500-133,000 men and ~80,000 National Guardsmen were in federal service; Navy ~65,000-69,000 and Marine Corps ~13,700. COW milper 1917 = 644k is a wartime annual average. Snapshot date: 6 April 1917 (declaration of war).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. National Guard not in federal service (total Guard ~180,000) plus Naval Militia and reserves; draft (Selective Service Act, 18 May 1917) registered 24M men later.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Navy (~69,000), Coast Artillery Corps (~20,000), field artillery, engineers, Signal Corps (incl. the Aviation Section), quartermaster and medical troops.

mobilizationRatio.note: Cited page: 4,355,000 mobilised (US War Dept 1924) by November 1918 = 0.042 of the population (low, war ended early); high 0.12 from the 1941-45 mobilisation of ~16M of ~132M (WWII production article). Mid is the potential with a longer war.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Regular infantry regiments (~1,000-1,500 men each in April 1917) and federalised Guard infantry; Marines (~13,700) included.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M1903 Springfield excellent, very few MGs (Lewis/Benet-Mercie)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: small regular army with Mexican border experience; Guard part-time

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. 17 regular cavalry regiments (Punitive Expedition 1916) plus Guard cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: rifle-armed mounted infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regulars with Mexican campaign experience

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. ~900 field guns and howitzers (3-inch M1902, 4.7-inch, 6-inch howitzers) in April 1917; the AEF later used French 75s and 155s. Coast-defence guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 3-inch gun adequate, no heavy field artillery in quantity

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: no indirect-fire experience at scale

count.note: Educated guess. Qualitative statement read from the Aviation in WWI page; counts recalled from Coffman, not read from a fetched source. Cited page: US air services were far behind in 1917 and almost totally dependent on French and British combat aircraft. The Aviation Section had ~55 serviceable aircraft and fewer than 250 machines including trainers (Coffman ch. 8). Trainers and observation types; no combat aircraft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25 (a generation behind). Evidence: Curtiss JN-4 trainers

usa-1989.notes: Snapshot date mid-1989 (IISS Military Balance 1989-90 basis, data as of 1 July 1989), before the fall of the Berlin Wall and the Panama intervention. Population convention: 50 states + DC; Puerto Rico and Guam excluded from population, Guam listed as a base. About 320,000 personnel were stationed in Europe (~250,000 in West Germany) and ~45,000 in Korea, so part of forces is forward-deployed. Ship counts come from the NHHC-based 600-ship Navy table; aircraft, armour, artillery and helicopter totals are reconstructions from memory of the IISS Military Balance 1989-90 (not fetchable) and are grade C/D; Guard and Reserve equipment is included in forces, Guard and Reserve personnel in trainedReserves. P-role splits are reconstructions from division structure. ships_major includes LHA/LPH amphibious assault ships; other amphibious ships are ships_minor. Cyber is rated by tech-anchor interpolation below the 1990 anchor.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.35 -> 0.99. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/USA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.52% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.18 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.15-1.21). Mid 1 - 0.015/1.18 = 0.99. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.15 = 0.98. High: s 1.21 = 0.99. Net exporter: production is about 118% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess: world's largest food exporter by value (grains, soy, meat); not computed from FAO balance sheets.

usa-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: 50 states + DC (World Bank); territories (Puerto Rico, Guam) excluded from population but Guam listed as an overseas base. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2024-2026 as quoted on Wikipedia, Wikipedia aircraft list (Air & Space Forces almanac 2024, Flight Global 2023 - F-35 counts dated), and the Naval Vessel Register-based fleet totals table. ships_major = carriers/LHA/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = LCS, MCM, LPD/LSD, LCC; drones = Group 3-5 UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Coast Guard (42,000) counted inside IISS active but its cutters are not in forces. About 200,000 personnel are deployed abroad on permanent or rotational basis (CIA Factbook 2025), so not all of forces is available at home on day 1. basesAbroad: 24 major installations (coordinates approximate to the main gate/airfield).

areaKm2.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2: USSR in Europe and Asia 21,176 thousand km2 (pre-1939 frontier, mid). The 1939-40 annexations (Baltic states, eastern Poland, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina, Karelian Isthmus, ~0.45-0.5M km2) were Soviet in June 1941; high includes them (educated). Border: the world_1945 USSR polygon (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1945.geojson, ~21.75M km2) contains the annexations (Riga, Lviv, Chisinau, Vyborg inside) but also Tuva (1944), Kaliningrad, southern Sakhalin, the Kurils and Transcarpathia (1945), none Soviet in June 1941. audit 2026-10-30: border changed from hb:1938:USSR, which left out the annexed lands counted in the population.

population.note: Andreev, Darski and Kharkova demographic balance: 196.7M in June 1941 (incl. territories annexed 1939-40); Rybakovsky's review range 191.8-200.1M (both via the cited page). COW NMC v7 tpop 1941 = 196,659k agrees. The 17 Jan 1939 census (old frontier) gave 170,467k (LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2).

urbanization.note: Cited page: 1939 census 170.5M, of which 55.9M urban = 32.8% (mid; pre-annexation territory). High: HYDE via OWID Russia 1940 = 35.3% urban (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true; the USSR as a whole was less urban). foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). The loss of Ukraine after June 1941 is outside the snapshot date. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.03/0.08/0.15 (educated guess about margins); recomputed with the formula.

ussr-1941.notes: Snapshot date 22 June 1941 (Operation Barbarossa). Population (196.7M), forces, rail and GDP are for the June 1941 USSR INCLUDING the 1939-40 annexations (Baltic states, eastern Poland, Bessarabia, Karelian Isthmus, ~20-23M people), and the border hb:1945:USSR contains them (it also contains Kaliningrad, southern Sakhalin, the Kurils, Transcarpathia and Tuva, Soviet only from 1944-45). (audit 2026-10-30) Mongolia (MPR) not included. Force counts are for the whole USSR (Askey, operationbarbarossa.net); the five western districts held 2,691,674 men, 12,842 tanks, 8,336 combat aircraft and 23,633 guns (sum of Askey's district figures), which a battle agent should use for the frontier battles. P-role personnel are reconstructions from division counts (grade C). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, patrol ships and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Merchant tonnage converted to deadweight at x1.5. audit 2026-10-30: border changed to hb:1945:USSR, which includes the 1939-40 annexations counted in the population (plus Kaliningrad, southern Sakhalin, the Kurils and Transcarpathia, gained in 1945).

areaKm2.note: Border hb:1945:USSR = ~21.75M km2 computed on the sphere; it contains the 1939-40 annexations and Tuva (Oct 1944) but also Kaliningrad, southern Sakhalin, the Kurils and Transcarpathia (1945). Low 21.13M = the world_1938 polygon (pre-1939 frontier); mid/high = that plus the 1939-40 annexations (eastern Poland, Baltic states, Bessarabia, Karelian Isthmus, ~0.7M km2) and Tuva = ~22.1-22.4M km2. In June 1944 Belorussia, the Baltic and part of Ukraine were still German-occupied. audit 2026-10-30: border changed from hb:1938:USSR (6 years off, without the annexations) to hb:1945:USSR (1 year off).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.68. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/UZB/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 25.20% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.79 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.78-0.80). Mid 1 - 0.252/0.79 = 0.68. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.78 = 0.61. High: s 0.80 = 0.69. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 79% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Irrigated wheat self-sufficiency, cotton and horticulture exports; dependent on Amu/Syr Darya water. Not from FAO balance sheets.

vatican-city-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2024-2026. Vatican City has no armed forces: the Pontifical Swiss Guard (135 men, 2024) is its de facto military (CIA Factbook) and is modelled as light infantry; the Gendarmerie (police) is excluded. Not covered by World Bank data, so population, area and urbanization come from the CIA World Factbook and all economy values are educated guesses (grade D); GDP and per-capita figures are notional. Border ne:VAT exists in Natural Earth 1:50m. Defence in practice is guaranteed by Italy under the Lateran Treaty.

gdp.note: World Bank has no PPP GDP for Venezuela. Mid: IMF WEO PPPGDP 2025 $260.133 bn current int$ (https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PPPGDP) x US GDP deflator 2011/2025 (FRED GDPDEF 91.478/128.885 = 0.710, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=GDPDEF&fq=Annual) = 184.6 bn 2011 int$. Low: CIA Factbook real GDP PPP 2023 $110.943 bn (2015 dollars, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/south-america/ve.json) x 91.478/97.315 = 104.3 bn. High +10% over mid. milSpendShare.note: CIA Factbook: 0.6% of GDP (2024), 0.5% (2023), 1.6% (2020); SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS 2.23% (2017, last value) as high. Opaque budget; mid an educated middle.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.86. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/VEN/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 8.87% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.62 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.60-0.62). Mid 1 - 0.089/0.62 = 0.86. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.60 = 0.81. High: s 0.62 = 0.86. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 62% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food importer since the 2000s; domestic agriculture collapsed; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 14,082,985 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 9.976% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 280,996. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-15%.

venezuela-2026.notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025-26. Situation at snapshot date: on 3 Jan 2026 the US (Operation Absolute Resolve) struck air-defence and military targets across northern Venezuela and captured President Nicolas Maduro; vice president Delcy Rodriguez was sworn in as acting president on 5 Jan 2026 and the government remains in place under heavy US leverage (2026 United States strikes in Venezuela article). Equipment counts are IISS Military Balance 2025 as tabulated in the List of equipment of the Venezuelan Armed Forces; only one destroyed Buk-M2E is documented from the raid, so other losses are not subtracted. Readiness is far below paper strength across all services. GDP: World Bank lacks PPP data; IMF and CIA Factbook disagree (grade C). Population convention: everything inside ne:VEN (Esequibo claim excluded). ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = OPVs, missile/patrol boats, LSTs; drones = Group 2+ UAVs. Infantry P-role split is an educated guess (grade D). Bolivarian Militia (paramilitary, 220,000 per IISS) excluded from P roles.

areaKm2.note: world_1960 has ONE Vietnam polygon covering north and south (~333,000 km2 computed on the sphere, used as high only); the DRV north of the 17th parallel was ~158,000 km2 (standard figure), used as mid. The border ref therefore overstates DRV territory.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop DRV 1968 = 20,280k. OWID (HYDE/UN) all-Vietnam 1968 = 39.73M, of which the North was roughly half. Excludes the population of VC-controlled areas of the South.

urbanization.note: COW upop/tpop DRV 1968 = 1,620/20,280 = 0.08 (cities over 100,000 only) as low; OWID urban share all Vietnam 1968 = 17.4% (high, the South was more urban). Hanoi and Haiphong were partly evacuated under bombing 1965-68.

activePersonnel.note: Main forces only: PAVN regulars in the North, Laos and the South plus VC (PLAF) main-force units. Hanoi official history (Military History Institute of Vietnam, Victory in Vietnam p. 182, quoted in the Vietnam War article): "By the end of 1966 the total strength of our armed forces was 690,000"; growth through 1967 for Tet. COW milper DRV 1968 = 447k counts only forces in the North. Vietnam War infobox ~860,000 (1967) is the high. A CIA/DIA March 1968 figure of ~475,000 regulars in the North could not be fetched (CIA reading room blocks automated access). Regional/local forces and guerrillas are in trainedReserves.

trainedReserves.note: Regional and local forces and guerrillas (PAVN/VC convention: active = main force, reserves = regional and local forces). MACV Jan 1968: 72,605 guerrillas plus 84,000 infrastructure; MACV revised total 287,465 minus 155,945 regulars = 131,520 non-regular (low); CIA argued VC irregulars, self-defence and cadre could reach 430,000 (Tet Offensive article, Dougan and Weiss p. 22). Plus DRV militia and self-defence forces in the North (several hundred thousand; not fetched, educated part of the high).

supportPersonnel.note: Air defence and AAA troops (25+ SAM battalions, 5,000-7,000 guns), Group 559 on the Ho Chi Minh Trail (up to 43,000 operating the system, Ho Chi Minh trail article), MACV Jan 1968 37,725 service and support troops in the South, navy, air force, artillery, engineers, rear services and staffs. Remainder of activePersonnel after the P roles.

mobilizationRatio.note: Hanoi fielded 690,000 regulars (end 1966) from ~19M plus militia, and kept expanding to ~1M by the 1970s: 0.04-0.05 under arms plus losses replaced; 0.10 total mobilisable is consistent with ~200,000 males reaching draft age per year sustained over a decade.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: PAVN regular infantry. South: MACV Jan 1968 55,744 in PAVN units plus 10,000-12,000 North Vietnamese in VC units; MACV later revised regulars in the South to 155,945 (PAVN and VC combined). Laos and the DMZ front ~30,000-40,000 (Khe Sanh siege force alone 20,000-40,000). North: home-defence and training divisions ~120,000. Reconstruction: ~90k South + ~35k Laos/DMZ + ~120k North + fillers. Excludes AAA and support troops.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: AK-47, RPD, RPG-2/RPG-7, 82 mm mortars; no armour or air cover in the South; light infantry kit era-typical, heavy support weak.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: conscripts with months of training in the North, then a 2-3 month march down the trail; veteran cadres, but heavy 1967-68 losses filled with recruits.

count.note: VC (PLAF) main-force units: MACV revised regulars 155,945 in the South minus ~75,000-80,000 PAVN = ~75,000-80,000 VC main force incl. sapper battalions. South Vietnamese JGS estimate 130,000 regulars (PAVN+VC). Regional forces and guerrillas excluded (trainedReserves).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: re-equipped with AK-47 and RPGs from 1965-67; still mixed captured and Chinese weapons.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: full-time chu luc fighters promoted from regional forces (Pike via NLF/PAVN organisation article); strong small-unit and sapper skills, weak in conventional combined arms.

count.note: Educated guess: Field guns, howitzers and rocket launchers: 130 mm M-46 and 152 mm across the DMZ, 122 mm and 85 mm guns, 105 mm captured pieces, 122 mm DKB and 140 mm rockets in the South; mortars excluded. No fetched count.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M-46 130 mm out-ranged most US tube artillery; rockets inaccurate but portable.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: effective siege fire at Con Thien and Khe Sanh; limited fire-direction communications.

count.note: Educated guess: PAVN tanks (T-34/85, T-54/Type 59, PT-76, Type 62/63 light tanks) in the 202nd Armoured Regiment and training units in early 1968; first PAVN tank attack was Lang Vei, 7 Feb 1968, with PT-76s. No fetched count.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: PT-76 amphibious light tanks and WWII-generation T-34/85 plus some T-54; era best is M60/T-62.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: armour arm small and inexperienced; poorly coordinated tank-infantry action at Lang Vei and later in 1971-72.

count.note: Educated guess: BTR-40/BTR-152/K-63 class carriers in training and armoured units; tiny force, none committed to Tet.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 1950s Soviet and Chinese wheeled carriers.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little mechanised experience.

count.note: VPAF had 36 MiG-17s in 1965, rising to 180 MiGs and 72 qualified pilots by 1968 (VPAF article, via acepilots/Russian sources); many airframes were held in Chinese bases and lost 85 MiGs April 1965 to November 1968, so ~100-150 on hand in January 1968. MiG-17, MiG-21F-13/PF; J-6 regiment only from 1969.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: MiG-21 competitive with the F-4 in GCI hit-and-run attacks; MiG-17 subsonic but agile.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: only 72 qualified pilots for 180 MiGs; strong GCI ground control, short pilot training in USSR/China.

count.note: Educated guess: A handful of Il-28 light bombers delivered 1965, never used offensively; An-2 biplanes raided Lima Site 85 on 12 Jan 1968 (VPAF article) but are not combat aircraft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Il-28 obsolete and could not survive US air superiority.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: no operational bomber missions flown.

count.note: Educated guess: Mi-4 transport helicopters of the 919th transport regiment; liaison and supply only.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 1950s piston Mi-4, unarmed.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: small transport arm, no air-assault doctrine.

count.note: Vietnam People's Navy article: before 1975 the navy operated fewer than forty patrol boats (P-4 torpedo boats, Swatow gunboats, Shanghai-class) plus a coastal junk force for sea infiltration (759th Transport Unit / Group 125). Many lost to US strikes after August 1964.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: P-4 and Swatow craft obsolete against US destroyers and carrier air.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: aggressive but ineffective in the Tonkin Gulf; skilled covert sea-transport crews.

count.note: Batteries. Rolling Thunder article (Thompson 2002 pp. 40-41): by 1967 an estimated 150 SAM launchers in 25 battalions (~25-30 SA-2 batteries); AAA grew from ~1,500 weapons (1965) to over 5,000 guns, US high estimate 7,000 in early 1967, incl. radar-directed 85 and 100 mm. At ~6-8 guns per AAA battery: ~650-1,150 gun batteries plus ~25-30 SAM battalions. 200 radar facilities coordinated SAMs, AAA and MiGs.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: SA-2 Guideline with repeatedly upgraded ECM-resistant radars; densest AD system of its time.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: three years of continuous combat; Soviet-trained SAM crews, dummy sites and passive-guidance tactics against Shrike.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced command from Dien Bien Phu; strategically effective (Tet broke US political will) but the Tet plan was too complex, attacked everywhere at once and was defeated piecemeal (Willbanks via Tet Offensive article).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: party cadre chain at every level down to company, three-man cells and self-criticism (NLF/PAVN organisation article); units fought on despite heavy losses.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: national reunification cause, bombing of the North; strained by 1967-68 losses and VC morale fell after Tet.

weapons.note: Anchor: 8 (1943) moving toward 9 (guided missiles). Evidence: AK-47, RPG-7, 130 mm M-46, SA-2 SAMs; no precision munitions, little heavy armour.

armor.note: Anchor: 8 (rolled homogeneous armour). Evidence: T-34/85, PT-76, some T-54; no composite armour.

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (steam navy) to 8. Evidence: only torpedo boats and gunboats, junks; no major warships or submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 (concrete lines). Evidence: tunnel complexes, bunker systems, bomb shelters for the population, dispersed and camouflaged depots.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways) to 8 (motor transport). Evidence: Ho Chi Minh Trail truck convoys, pipelines (later), but bicycles, porters and river drums still carried much; rail lines to China under constant attack.

communications.note: Anchor: 8 (radio at company level) not fully met. Evidence: radios at regiment and battalion, wire and couriers below; good secure signals discipline.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar. Evidence: 200 radar facilities in the Red River delta air defence net; human intelligence networks in the South; no aerial reconnaissance over the South.

air.note: Anchor: air 8 (1943) to 9 (1985). Evidence: MiG-21F/PF second-generation jets under GCI, MiG-17; no attack aviation.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (OWID CSV): Vietnam 1968 = 1,114 (2011 int$) for the whole of Vietnam. The North was poorer per head than the aid-fed South and its industry was bombed 1965-68; ~0.85 x national used as mid. Scaled estimate, grade C.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Vietnam (whole country) 1968 = 77.7%; the DRV alone was at least as agrarian (high 82%). Grade C because the series covers north and south. Share 77.7% (range 74.0-82.0%) -> 0.223 (0.18-0.26).

roadKm.note: Educated guess: DRV road net (mostly unpaved) plus the Ho Chi Minh Trail corridor in Laos: a June 1966 DIA estimate credited ~1,000 km (600 mi) of passable roads within the corridor (Ho Chi Minh trail article).

railKm.note: Educated guess: Hanoi-Lao Cai, Hanoi-Dong Dang (to China), Hanoi-Haiphong and Hanoi-Thanh Hoa-Vinh lines, ~1,000 km total, repeatedly cut by bombing.

majorPorts.note: Haiphong (two-thirds of imports came by sea through Haiphong and other ports, Rolling Thunder article), Hon Gai, Cam Pha; Haiphong was not mined until 1972.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Small coastal steamers and junks; DRV imports came in Soviet bloc and Chinese ships. Deadweight guess.

supplyRangeKm.note: The Ho Chi Minh Trail sustained divisions 800-1,200 km from Hanoi (Binh Tram relay system, 30 trucks a day in 1965 rising sharply; Ho Chi Minh trail article), but at low tonnage; conventional offensives beyond the trailheads ran short within days.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: Water buffalo and oxen of the DRV farm economy plus porters and ~tens of thousands of cargo bicycles on the trail.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS via OWID: the DRV never had nuclear weapons.

homeDefense.note: 1.2-1.3 rows: familiar jungle and mountain terrain, dense population support and shelters, deep sanctuaries in Laos and China; monsoon climate US forces were not adapted to. No US ground invasion of the North was ever attempted.

vietnam-1968.notes: Snapshot date 30 January 1968 (Tet Offensive). Nation = Democratic Republic of Vietnam (North Vietnam) and the forces it commanded: PAVN in the North, Laos and the South plus VC (PLAF) main-force units, treated as one force as Hanoi's official history does. Force convention (insurgent archetype): activePersonnel = main force (PAVN regulars + VC main force); trainedReserves = regional and local forces, guerrillas and the northern militia/self-defence forces. Population, economy and territory are the DRV only (COW tpop 20.28M); VC-controlled areas of the South are excluded. Border: the world_1960 basemap has a single Vietnam polygon covering north and south, so hb:1960:Vietnam overstates the DRV; areaKm2 mid is the DRV figure. Order of battle in the South from MACV Combined Intelligence Center OB summaries as quoted in the Tet Offensive article (Jan 1968 estimate 225,346; revised in 1972 to 287,465 incl. 155,945 regulars). Weakest numbers: tanks, artillery and AAA batteries (no fetched OB of PAVN heavy equipment; CIA reading-room documents could not be fetched). Most heavy equipment was Soviet and Chinese aid, so production is empty; China also kept up to 170,000 support troops (engineering and AAA) in the North in 1968 (Vietnam War infobox), not counted here. Pike, PAVN: People's Army of Vietnam (1986) is the background reference for structure.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.69. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/VNM/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 25.04% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.81 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.80-0.83). Mid 1 - 0.250/0.81 = 0.69. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.80 = 0.62. High: s 0.83 = 0.7. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 81% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. World's 2nd-3rd largest rice exporter; net food exporter.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.05. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/YEM/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 31.62% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.21 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.19-0.23). Formula gives below 0 (1 - 0.316/0.21 = -0.51): farm employment exceeds calorie self-sufficiency, so farm households also eat imported wheat and part of a is qat, a non-food crop. Educated guess: mid 0.05 (0.02-0.10), the share of local grain, fruit, vegetables and fish that still reaches town markets. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 21% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports ~90% of staple food; famine conditions.

yemen-2026.notes: DIVIDED-STATE WARTIME snapshot: Yemen has two rival authorities: the Houthi (Ansar Allah) Supreme Political Council holding Sanaa, the north-west and Hudaydah, and the internationally recognised Presidential Leadership Council seated in Aden with Saudi- and Emirati-backed forces; the STC was dissolved de jure on 9 Jan 2026 (STC article) and its forces absorbed into PLC structures. Forces here are the SUM of both sides on one ne:YEM polygon and overstate what either can field against an outsider. The Houthis are at war: Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab attacks (Sept 2026 crisis) and missile/drone waves on Saudi Arabia (Oct 2026). Capital is Sanaa (Houthi-held, de facto); the government sits in Aden. Almost every number is an educated guess (grade D) with wide ranges; GDP is the IMF estimate rebased (grade C). One-way attack drones excluded from drones per the role convention.

count.note: AA guns at 4 per battery. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: 940 AA guns (mid 235 batteries), of which 360 were 15 mm and 20 mm; the 580 heavier guns alone = 145 batteries (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mixed Czech and Italian models without common spares (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Belgrade defences failed to stop the 6 April raid.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: flotilla leader Dubrovnik and three Beograd-class destroyers = 4 (mid; Ljubljana in dry dock, low 3). High adds the old training cruiser Dalmacija.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Dubrovnik (1931) and the Beograd class were modern 1930s destroyers.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: the British rated the commander-in-chief as having little technical knowledge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy); the fleet was captured almost intact.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: 8 Orjen-class and 2 Uskok-class MTBs (low 10); plus 6 Galeb-class and 5 Malinska-class minelayers and 6 250t-class torpedo boats (mid 27); high adds the 4 Danube river monitors (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Orjen-class MTBs modern; minelayers and 250t boats of First World War origin.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: as ships_major.

count.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy: four submarines, of which only the two French-built boats were fully combat-ready (low 2).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1920s British and French boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: as ships_major.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mobilisation delayed to 3 April, only ~11 divisions in position, a cordon along the whole frontier; the 6 April bombing of Belgrade cut communications between the high command and the field forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); 150 of 167 generals were Serbs, and the 1937 manoeuvres exposed an incompetent General Staff (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25 (divided). Evidence: resistance collapsed largely because many non-Serbs, Croats in particular, would not fight (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army); ethnic German and Hungarian conscripts were released by the Germans after capture (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Serbian units motivated after the 27 March coup, others not; 254,000-345,000 captured by the Germans in 11 days (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905) toward 8 (1943). Evidence: First World War rifles and machine guns with some modern Czech equipment, 1,600 modern 81 mm mortars, 812 37 mm and 47 mm AT guns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

armor.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: 54 Renault R35 (cast armour, 37 mm gun), the rest Renault FT.

ships.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: modern destroyers Dubrovnik and Beograd class, Orjen-class MTBs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Navy); no cruisers of value.

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: 16 regiments in frontier fortifications (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); no continuous concrete line comparable to the Czechoslovak or Maginot works.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: heavily reliant on animal-powered transport; 1,000 US trucks imported in the months before the invasion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telephone and telegraph). Evidence: the bombing of Belgrade destroyed nearly all means of communication with the field forces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

isr.note: Anchor: 7 toward 8. Evidence: seven reconnaissance groups with 130 Breguet 19 and Potez 25 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); no radar.

air.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Bf 109E, Hurricane I, IK-3, Do 17K and Blenheim I, most aircraft modern types (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Yugoslavia: 1939 = 2,072 (mid, high), 1938 = 1,991 (low), 2011 int$. No 1940-41 value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Yugoslavia: 1940 = 7.43% (low, last peacetime; 1939 6.85%), 1941 = 15.0% (mid, high: at war). COW milex 1940 = 121,456 thousand current US$.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry and mining share of output. Three-quarters of the workforce was in agriculture and more than half of industrial workers were seasonal worker-peasants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed: Yugoslavia exported grain and livestock in the 1930s). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia: three-quarters of the workforce in agriculture -> 1 - 0.75 = 0.25; mostly subsistence peasants, poor in the south.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age (21) per year: the 1920 birth cohort of ~12M people at ~35 births per 1,000 = ~420,000, half male, ~65% survival.

aircraft_strike.note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia: about 40 Do 17K and some 40 Blenheim I licence-built in Yugoslavia, mostly 1939-41: ~40 a year.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Hurricanes under licence and IK-3 fighters under construction at the invasion (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia); IK-3 output was a dozen.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roads of all classes, few paved; the 1987 network of 120,747 km (CIA World Factbook 1990, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt) was mostly built after 1945.

railKm.note: Educated guess. Standard and narrow-gauge lines of the Yugoslav State Railways; the 1987 network was 9,270 km (CIA World Factbook 1990) after post-war additions and closures.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Split, Sibenik, Susak, Dubrovnik (Gruz) and the Bay of Kotor naval base; Belgrade on the Danube.

merchantTonnage.note: GRT to DWT x 1.5 (low x 1.3, high x 1.6). League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 Table 113 (https://www.istmat.org/files/uploads/49915/09_strany_mira_-_transport_torgovlya_platyozhnyy_balans.pdf): Yugoslavia 387k GRT in June 1938.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Animal-powered trains from the railheads; ~1,000 trucks in all (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Yugoslavia).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. National stock of horses (and oxen used for transport) in a peasant economy of 16M; the army relied on requisitioned animals.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before July 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row for the Dinaric mountains, reduced to 1.1 because much of the population did not support the defence (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Yugoslav_Army) and the Danube plain in the north is open; low 1.0.

yugoslavia-1941.notes: Snapshot date 6 April 1941, the first day of the Axis invasion, with mobilisation ordered on 3 April and incomplete. Active personnel spans the 600,000 mobilised on 20 March to the 1.2M of full mobilisation (mid 900,000). Equipment from the Invasion of Yugoslavia article (Tomasevich, Zajac, Shores, Cull and Malizia) and the Royal Yugoslav Navy article (Vego, Niehorster). Weakest values: the P-role split, support personnel, roads, railway length and animals (educated guesses; no interwar railway or road total was fetched). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: destroyers ships_major; MTBs, minelayers, torpedo boats and river monitors ships_minor.

areaKm2.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: Yugoslavia 255,800 km2 (mid, high). world_1960 Yugoslavia polygon = 253,152 km2 computed by the pipeline (low).

population.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: population 22,130,000 (mid). OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) Yugoslavia 1980 = 21.62M (low); COW NMC v7 tpop 1980 = 22,304k (high).

urbanization.note: World Bank WDI Database Archives, version 1991 Apr, Yugoslavia (code YUG, then the SFRY) urban share 1980 = 42.3% (mid). HYDE 3.5 via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) present-day republics 1980: Bosnia 35.5%, Slovenia 48.0%, Croatia 50.1%, North Macedonia 53.5% (Serbia missing); range 0.36-0.46 brackets the federal value.

activePersonnel.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: total armed forces 264,000 (145,000 conscripts): army 190,000, navy 30,000 (incl. 15,000 marines), air force 44,000 (mid). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 252,500 (low; navy 17,500). High adds the 16,000 frontier guards.

trainedReserves.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 500,000 reservists (low, mid); plus 1,000,000 in the Territorial Defence Force (high). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1-3 million Territorial Defence (Partisan) and 2,000,000 Civil Defence on mobilisation, not counted.

supportPersonnel.note: Active strength outside the P roles: army 190,000 minus ~90,000 infantry = 100,000 (armour, artillery, AA, engineers, logistics); navy 30,000 minus ~8,000 marines and airborne counted as P = ~22,000 (MB 1981-82 navy 17,500); air force 44,000 (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru). 100,000 + 22,000 + 44,000 = 166,000 -> mid 160,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total National Defence: active 264,000 + 500,000 reserves = 764,000 (0.035 of 22.1M, low); + 1,000,000 Territorial Defence (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru) = 1.76M (0.08, mid); with the 1-3 million TDF of The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) up to ~3.3M (0.15, high).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Rifle strength of the army's 8 infantry divisions, 15-16 independent infantry brigades (incl. mechanised and 3 light) and 1 mountain brigade (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru; The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)); army 190,000 with 130,000 conscripts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5 relative to 1980 NATO/Warsaw Pact. Evidence: domestic small arms, Sagger and Snapper ATGW, 82-105 mm RCL, SA-7 (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); few IFVs (M-980 on order).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 15-month conscription, 130,000 of 190,000 conscripts.

count.note: Educated guess. Airborne brigade and the marine brigade (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru lists 15,000 marines in the navy, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) 2,500 marines in one brigade of 2 regiments); mid assumes ~3,000 airborne + ~5,000 marines.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: light weapons, RCL and ATGW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: selected volunteers and conscripts in elite brigades.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 1,500 T-34/-54/-55 and M-47 (mid) plus about 650 M-4 medium tanks (high 2,150). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1,240 T-34/-54/-55 and 60 M-47 (low 1,300), M-4 and T-34/85 in reserve storage. Some PT-76 light tanks not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: T-54/55 and many T-34 and M-47 against T-72 and M60A3 era best; domestic M-84 not yet in service.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 8 independent tank brigades of conscripts.

count.note: The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 200 BTR-50/-60/-152 (low), some M-980 MICV and some M-60 APC; The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: M-980 MICV, BTR-50/-60P/-152 and M-60 APC without counts, 700 M-980 on order. Mid and high add the uncounted M-980 and M-60.

count.note: The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1,800 guns (M-1955 and SU-100 100 mm, 122, 130 and 152 mm) (mid); howitzers (M-48 76 mm, 105, 122, 155 mm) and 128 mm MRL listed without counts (high 2,400 allows ~600). Low 1,500 for unserviceable older pieces. 12 field artillery regiments (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Soviet 130 mm M-46 and US 155 mm alongside Second World War types; domestic 128 mm MRL.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 9 interceptor squadrons with 126 MiG-21F/PF/M (low, mid; The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) the same); high adds the 18 MiG-21U of the conversion unit.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: MiG-21F/PF/M with AA-2 Atoll against F-15/F-16 and MiG-23 era best.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 44,000-strong air force with 7,000 conscripts (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 15 FGA squadrons with 12 Kraguj and 130 Galeb/Jastreb = 142 (low, mid); high adds the 40 Galeb/Jastreb of 3 reconnaissance squadrons. 346 combat aircraft in all.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Galeb/Jastreb light jet trainers-attack aircraft and Kraguj piston COIN; the Orao only on order (25, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 5 AB-205, 14 Mi-1, 18 Mi-4, 12 Mi-8, 10 Whirlwind, 20 Partizan (Gazelle) = 79 (low). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 5 AB-205, 18 Mi-4, 50 Mi-8, 5 Whirlwind, 5 Partizan, 1 A-109 = 84 (mid), plus 15 Partizan trainers (high 99).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: transport helicopters, mostly Mi-4/Mi-8; no attack helicopters (94 Partizan on order).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: Educated guess. FROG-7 SSM launchers (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru lists the type without a count); one battalion assumed. Coastal Samlet batteries are counted under the navy.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: unguided FROG-7 rockets.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: SAM battalions count as one battery each, AA regiments as 3-4 batteries. The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 8 SA-2 + 6 SA-3 battalions = 14 and 12 army AA artillery regiments (low 14 + 12 x 4 = 62). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 24 AA regiments under the Air Defence Force (mid 14 + 24 x 3 = 86, high 14 + 24 x 4 = 110). SA-6/-7/-9 and ZSU-23-4 with the army.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: SA-2/SA-3 static sites and SA-6/SA-9 mobile systems, many towed guns of 20-94 mm.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 1 Split-class destroyer, in reserve (low 0, mid 1). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1 Koni-class frigate with SA-N-4 (high 2 counts both).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1950s domestic destroyer; Koni a light Soviet export frigate.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 18-month naval service (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 3 corvettes, 16 FAC(M) with Styx (6 Rade Koncar, 10 Osa-I), 15 Shershen FAC(T), 19 large patrol craft and 27 minesweepers = 80 (mid); low 67 without the 13 river minesweepers. The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 3 + 16 + 15 + 20 + 30 = 84 (high). 25 coast artillery batteries with Samlet not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Osa-I and Rade Koncar missile boats with Styx, effective in the Adriatic islands.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 6 submarines (1 Sava, 3 Heroj, 2 Sutjeska) (low, mid); The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 7 (2 Sava) (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: domestic diesel-electric boats of the 1960s-70s.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced Partisan-generation command and a worked-out Total National Defence doctrine combining the army with 1M+ Territorial Defence (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); never tested against a major power.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: multi-national conscript army with republic-based Territorial Defence; Tito died in May 1980 and national tensions later broke the army apart in 1991.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: defensive motivation against a Warsaw Pact invasion after Czechoslovakia 1968; conscript force.

weapons.note: Anchor: 8 (1943) toward 9 (1985). Evidence: Sagger ATGW, SA-7, 128 mm MRL and domestic small arms (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

armor.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: T-54/55 the best tank, many T-34, M-47 and M-4.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Styx-armed Osa and Rade Koncar missile boats, Koni frigate with SA-N-4.

fortification.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: coastal artillery and Samlet batteries (25), hardened airbases and mountain shelters of Total National Defence.

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: motorised army with a domestic vehicle industry.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: radio-equipped formations of Soviet and domestic types.

isr.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: 3 reconnaissance squadrons of Galeb/Jastreb, SA-2/SA-3 radars.

air.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: MiG-21 interceptors and domestic Galeb/Jastreb attack jets; Orao on order.

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV) Yugoslavia: 1980 = 10,037 (mid), 1979 = 9,873 (low), 1981 = 10,106 (high), 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Yugoslavia 1980 = 3.23% (low, mid). High = The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): defence 1981 $3.47 bn / GNP 1979 $64.4 bn = 5.4%. CIA World Factbook 1990: 4.6% of national income (1989).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry incl. mining and construction share of output. Agriculture employed 32.3% of the labour force in 1980 (World Bank WDI archive, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/sources/57/country/YUG/series/SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS/time/YR1980;YR1975?format=json&per_page=100); industrialised federation with a domestic arms industry.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed: Yugoslavia was broadly self-sufficient in food). World Bank WDI Database Archives, version 1989 Apr, Yugoslavia SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS 1980 = 32.3% -> 0.68 (mid); 1975 = 41.0% -> 0.59; CIA World Factbook 1990: 22% in agriculture (1986) -> 0.78. Low and high narrowed to 1978-82.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age per year. CIA World Factbook 1990: 188,028 males reach military age (19) annually (1990); the 1961 birth cohort reaching 19 in 1980 is assumed to be of similar size.

ifv_apc.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 700 M-980 MICV on order (The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 500 on order) for delivery over several years: ~100 a year.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Galeb/Jastreb and later Orao (25 on order, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)) from the SOKO plant at Mostar.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Missile boats (8 FAC(M) on order, The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru), patrol craft and minesweepers from Adriatic yards.

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: 120,747 km of highways (1987; high), of which 71,315 km hard surface (low). Mid 110,000 allows for growth 1980-87.

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: 9,270 km of railways (1987; low, mid); high allows for lines closed 1980-87.

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: ports Rijeka, Split, Koper, Bar, Ploce (5), inland Belgrade (high 6). Naval bases Split (Lora), Pula, Sibenik, Ploce and Kotor (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Deadweight tonnage. CIA World Factbook 1990: 3,608,705 GRT / 5,809,219 DWT (1989; high); the 1980 fleet was smaller, no 1980 figure fetched.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Defensive war on interior lines with a motorised army; Territorial Defence depots in every commune.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses still used on private peasant farms; marginal for the army.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Yugoslav warheads.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: Total National Defence with 1M+ Territorial Defence and Dinaric mountains (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); low 1.2 for the open Pannonian plain where a Warsaw Pact attack would come.

yugoslavia-1980.notes: Snapshot date mid-1980 (Military Balance 1980-81, with 1981-82 as the cross-check), months after Tito's death. Non-aligned federation with Soviet and Western equipment and a Total National Defence doctrine; the doctrine archetype is the regional mixed-equipment one. Weakest values: the P-role split, FROG launchers, merchant tonnage, roads in 1980, cohort and animals (educated guesses or later-year figures). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: destroyer and frigate ships_major; corvettes, missile and torpedo boats, patrol craft and minesweepers ships_minor; coastal Samlet batteries not counted.

zimbabwe-2026.notes: AUTO-GENERATED BASE SNAPSHOT. Population, economy, personnel and infrastructure from the World Bank (grade A/B). Force mix, ratings and tech copied from researched regional analogues (Republic of Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, State of Eritrea, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Kenya, Federal Republic of Nigeria, Republic of South Africa, Republic of the Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Republic of Uganda) and graded D. Replace with a researched snapshot when one exists.

areaKm2.note: world_1878 polygon "Zululand" = 25,400 km2 on the sphere (Thukela to Phongolo); kingdom with its northern marches ~27,000-32,000 km2.

population.note: Page infobox: 250,000 in 1828. Estimates for Cetshwayo's kingdom in 1879 run ~250,000-400,000 (Laband, Kingdom in Crisis ch. 1); no census.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: no towns; royal amakhanda (military homesteads) of a few thousand people each.

activePersonnel.note: Page infobox: 35,000-60,000 Zulu (Colenso 1880 p. 318: army 35,000, 4,000 kept with Cetshwayo). The amabutho were assembled at oNdini in January 1879, so the army counts as under arms. About 20,000-25,000 at Isandlwana (battle page).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: older married amabutho and local levies not called to oNdini.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: izindibi carrier boys and royal attendants.

mobilizationRatio.note: Every man was enrolled in an age-set ibutho; 35,000-60,000 warriors (Anglo-Zulu War page) of 250,000-400,000 people = 14-20%. audit 2026-10-30: mid 0.15 -> 0.17, inside the cited 14-20% range, so that active (40,000) + trainedReserves (10,000) fit inside mobilizable.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high). audit 2026-10-30: mid recomputed for the new ratio (300,000 x 0.17).

count.note: Close-order amabutho fighting in the horns-of-the-buffalo formation with isijula/iklwa spears and cowhide shields; total army less skirmishers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25 or below. Evidence: stabbing spears and shields against Martini-Henry rifles and artillery, several generations behind

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: lifelong age-set regiments, fast cross-country movement

count.note: Educated guess: warriors with firearms (~20,000 old muskets and some rifles in the kingdom) used as skirmishers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: obsolete trade muskets, little ammunition

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: poor marksmanship

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Ntshingwayo kaMahole's envelopment at Isandlwana; Cetshwayo's defensive strategy

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: age-set regimental identity; charged into rifle and Gatling fire at Kambula and Ulundi

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: defence of the homeland against invasion

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (iron weapons). Evidence: iron stabbing spears and throwing spears, a few muskets

armor.note: Anchor: 1 (leather). Evidence: cowhide isihlangu shields, no armour

ships.note: Anchor: 0 (rafts, canoes). Evidence: no watercraft of military use

fortification.note: Anchor: 0 (palisade). Evidence: stockaded homesteads, caves and the Hlobane strongholds

logistics.note: Anchor: 0 (porters). Evidence: boy carriers and cattle driven with the impi, 3-4 days' food

communications.note: Anchor: 0 (runners). Evidence: runners

isr.note: Anchor: 0-1 (runners). Evidence: excellent scouts and spies, but foot messengers only

air.note: No aircraft before 1903.

cyber.note: No computer networks before ~1990.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess: cattle-keeping and hoe-agriculture society near subsistence; Maddison has no estimate (South Africa 1879 = 1,985 reflects the colonial economy and is not comparable).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: amabutho served the king as unpaid labour and soldiers; not a monetary budget.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: iron smelting and smithing only.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: cattle herds and royal grain stores fed the assembled army for days only.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. A new ibutho was formed every few years from youths of the same age.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: no engineered roads; wagon tracks made by traders and the British.

railKm.note: Educated guess: no railway in Zululand (Natal had ~110 km in 1879).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: no port; the coast was open beach.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: no merchant shipping.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: impis carried a few days' food and drove cattle.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: no wheeled transport; cattle were food, not draught animals.

nuclearWarheads.note: No nuclear weapons before 1945.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row plus full population support; no fortified cities, so below the full 1.2 row.

zulu-kingdom-1879.notes: Snapshot = Zulu Kingdom in January 1879 when the British invasion began. Territory and population = Cetshwayo's kingdom between the Thukela and the Phongolo; includes is empty. Personnel: the whole assembled amabutho = active (they were mustered at oNdini for the first-fruits ceremony and the war); older regiments not called = trainedReserves. Army size from the Anglo-Zulu War page (Colenso 1880; 35,000-60,000) and Isandlwana page (20,000-25,000 engaged). Economy and logistics values are educated guesses: no statistics exist for the kingdom. Tech levels sit far below the industrial anchors by design.
